verdicts.baseRate: Not a base-rate claim. It only reports what grounds the government asserted against one entity. On symmetry: the SPEC control compares UPA cancellations (2011-14, including the Kudankulam-linked NGOs) with NDA cancellations. Those UPA actions also cited "political activities" or "public interest" grounds. So citing "political activity" is not unique to this case and says nothing about motive. This edge does not claim a motive anyway.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, three denials. (1) Lawyers Collective's statement of 7 December 2016 "denied the allegations listed in the cancellation order" (https://www.frontlinedefenders.org/en/case/cancellation-registration-lawyers-collective). The June 2016 entry says: "LC denies all of the accusations and plans to appeal." This is recorded as contra edge c035. (2) A specific rebuttal on the ASG ground: the remuneration was paid "before she became the additional solicitor general and continued during and after the tenure with the permission of the Law Ministry" (Scroll, https://scroll.in/latest/927454/cbi-files-case-against-indira-jaisings-ngo-lawyers-collective-for-alleged-fcra-violations). (3) The 2019 CBI FIR, LC said, had "no basis in fact and in law".
verdicts.innocentReading: These are the government's asserted grounds and nobody has ruled on them. On the first ground, LC says the Law Ministry, the competent authority, approved the continued remuneration under the Law Officers (Terms and Conditions) Rules, and that MHA admitted this. If that is right, the "government servant" ground falls away. Communication costs of an honorary, unpaid UN mandate being reimbursed by the rapporteur's home NGO, and advocacy rallies, are routine NGO activities. Treating them as FCRA violations depends on contested readings of "political activity" and of the Rules. Business Standard reports that the Bombay HC granted Jaising and Grover interim protection in 2019 in the CBI case.
verdicts.reason: The claim survives in substance. It correctly presents these as MHA allegations at tier "alleged" and has a contra edge (c035). FLD names the three grounds, and Scroll and Business Standard independently report them. The tier fits: these are government allegations that no court has ruled on. The attribution needs fixing, though. The cited source ties the three grounds to the 1 June 2016 suspension, not to the 27 November 2016 cancellation order. The source also does not contain "ASG" or the 2006-07 to 2013-14 window the record uses for its date test. Hence sourceCheck is "partially", not "confirmed".
verdicts.corrections: 1. from: change 2016-11-27 to 2016-06-01, or relabel the claim as "grounds alleged at suspension (2016-06-01), reiterated for cancellation" and add a source for the reiteration. 2. d: delete "from the order". Replace with "as recorded by Front Line Defenders (10 June 2016 entry) as grounds of the suspension". 3. d: correct the receipt window to 2006-07 to 2014-15 (Scroll, total Rs 32.39 crore). 4. srcs: add https://scroll.in/latest/927454/cbi-files-case-against-indira-jaisings-ngo-lawyers-collective-for-alleged-fcra-violations for "ASG 2009-2014" and "Rs 96.6 lakh", because FLD only says "government servant". Also consider adding the Business Standard 2019-05-08 piece on "Centre's 2016 orders". 5. text/lab: change "UN Special Rapporteur costs" to "communication expenses during his UN Special Rapporteur mandate" to match the source. 6. c035 contra: add LC's specific rebuttal that the remuneration pre-dated her ASG appointment and continued with Law Ministry permission (Scroll). 7. upgradeIf: add the 2019 CBI FIR text or the Bombay HC interim-protection order.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: the MHA FCRA wing suspended Sabrang Trust's FCRA registration on 2015-09-09. The CJP source says: "In a detailed 24-page response dated October 5, 2015, Sabrang Trust, Mumbai, had challenged the MHA-FCRA department's September 9 order suspending its FCRA registration". The year is not written next to "September 9", but the October 5, 2015 reply fixes it as 2015. FIDH/OMCT Observatory urgent appeal (2016-07-06) states it directly: "Sabrang Trust received an 'Order' dated September 9, 2015, signed by Deputy Secretary Shri Mahendra Kumar ... suspending the FCRA registration of Sabrang Trust for a period of 180 days." Google News also indexes an NDTV story dated 2015-09-10 headlined "Activist Teesta Setalvad's NGO License Suspended by Home Ministry". I saw only the headline and date; the body was blocked. The order falls within Rajnath Singh's term as Home Minister (2014-05-26 to 2019-05-30), so the date passes. The claim's `to` value of 2016-06-16 is not supported. FIDH says the suspension was for 180 days, which ends around 2016-03-07. No source I opened says it was extended until the cancellation.
verdicts.identityTest: Passes. The subject is Sabrang Trust, Mumbai (trustees Teesta Setalvad and Javed Anand). This is not Sabrang Communications & Publishing Pvt Ltd, which is a separate entity named in the grounds (c038). The actor is the MHA FCRA wing: FIDH names the signer as Deputy Secretary Mahendra Kumar, who also led the April 9-11, 2015 inspection. Neither entity record has an FCRA registration number (identity.fcra is null), so that is a gap. The two names are not the same body, and the claim does not combine separate facts into something none of them says.
verdicts.baseRate: This is a single, dated enforcement event, not a claim about a pattern, so a base rate cannot argue against it. For context: section 13 suspension pending inquiry, after an inspection, is the normal step before cancellation. The same sequence was used on Lawyers Collective (2016) and, under the UPA, on CPSC (three suspensions 2012-14). The SPEC control (UPA vs NDA) shows the same procedure under both governments. The event itself says nothing about motive.
verdicts.denialFound: Two responses are on record. (1) The Trust's point-by-point letter of 2015-06-25 answering the inspection observations. (2) Its 24-page letter of 2015-10-05 challenging the September 9 suspension order and "denying once again having committed any FCRA violation" (FIDH, https://www.fidh.org/en/issues/human-rights-defenders/india-cancellation-of-the-license-of-sabrang-trust-under-the-foreign ; CJP, https://cjp.org.in/cancellation-of-fcra-of-sabrang-trust-to-stop-public-justice-says-teesta-setalvad/). Neither denies that the suspension happened; both contest its grounds. I found no public MHA statement on the suspension in the sources I opened. The order itself is MHA's position.
verdicts.innocentReading: A routine regulatory sequence: a complaint from the Gujarat Home department (2015-03-10), then an inspection (April 9-11, 2015), observations, the Trust's reply, and a section 13 suspension for up to 180 days pending inquiry. The trigger was a mechanical test: administrative expenses over 50% in 2010-11 and 2011-12. The same step is applied to many associations whose ratios fail that test. This reading fits the fact of the suspension just as well as the claim of targeting does, and the claim as worded asserts only the fact.
verdicts.reason: The central fact holds. It comes from the affected party itself (CJP), which is an admission against interest, and is independently confirmed in explicit terms by the FIDH/OMCT Observatory appeal. An NDTV item dated 2015-09-10 also exists, though only its headline could be seen. "Reported" is the right tier. It is not "documented", because the order text is not published and the NDTV body could not be opened. Two fields are wrong, but the claim itself stands: the description misdates the 24-page reply, and the `to` date is unsupported.
verdicts.corrections: 1) d: "the Trust's 24-page reply of 2015-06-25" is wrong. The 24-page response is dated 2015-10-05 and challenged the suspension; the 2015-06-25 letter was the point-by-point reply to the observations. Rewrite as: "Followed inspection (2015-04-09 to 11) and 'observations' dated 2015-06-04/05 (FIDH gives June 4, CJP June 5); Trust replied 2015-06-25; suspension order signed by Deputy Secretary Mahendra Kumar, for 180 days; Trust's 24-page challenge dated 2015-10-05." 2) to: change 2016-06-16 to 2016-03-07 (180 days), or set it to null and add "180-day term; extension not sourced". 3) srcs: add FIDH/OMCT Observatory 2016-07-06 (https://www.fidh.org/en/issues/human-rights-defenders/india-cancellation-of-the-license-of-sabrang-trust-under-the-foreign) as an independent second source. Add the NDTV 2015-09-10 item (https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/activist-teesta-setalvads-ngo-license-suspended-by-home-ministry-1216336), marked headline-only. 4) Add to d: the inspection was requested by the Gujarat Home department letter of 2015-03-10 (FIDH). 5) upgradeIf: "NDTV body or another news outlet opened confirming 2015-09-09 and 180 days, or the MHA order text". killIf: "Order date differs". 6) Also update the entity record for ngo:mha-foreigners-division ("Inspection observations issued ... 2015-06-05"): note that FIDH gives 2015-06-04.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: MHA (FCRA wing, Foreigners Division) cancelled Sabrang Trust's FCRA registration on 2016-06-16. The actor's window: Rajnath Singh was Home Minister from 2014-05-26 to 2019-05-30 (c003), so the date falls inside his tenure. The sequence holds: inspection observations on 2015-06-05, the Trust's reply on 2015-06-25, a 180-day suspension on 2015-09-09 (per FIDH), a 24-page response dated 2015-10-05, then cancellation on 2016-06-16. The CJP source says: "The big verdict of Gulberg massacre case came on 17th June, 2016 and interestingly Sabrang Trust's FCRA was cancelled by MHA on the 16th June." The FIDH/OMCT Observatory urgent appeal IND 003/0716/OBS 054 (2016-07-06) says independently: "on June 16, 2016, the Ministry of Home Affairs announced on its website that the licence of Sabrang Trust had been cancelled ... with 'immediate effect'." Google News lists The Hindu as "Teesta's Trust loses FCRA registration" dated 2016-06-16. The date is confirmed. One problem: 17 June 2016 was the Gulberg SENTENCING (quantum: 11 life terms). The conviction verdict against 24 accused came on 2016-06-02. So "day before Gulberg verdict" copies the accused party's own wording and is imprecise.
verdicts.identityTest: Sabrang Trust (Mumbai) is named in the CJP page, the FIDH appeal and The Hindu headline. It is correctly kept apart from Sabrang Communications & Publishing Pvt Ltd (SCPPL) and from Citizens for Justice and Peace. CJP's FCRA registration was a separate matter in December 2016, where the registration was renewed and then cancelled; Mint and TOI covered it on 2016-12-15, and it must not be merged into this edge. No FCRA registration number was recorded or found. Crediting the action to MHA's FCRA wing is consistent with FIDH ("Ministry of Home Affairs announced on its website").
verdicts.baseRate: The cancellation itself is a single dated event and needs no base rate. The timing inference ("day before verdict") does not discriminate. June 2016 was full of Gulberg dates: conviction on 06-02, a sentencing hearing expected around 06-09, sentencing on 06-17. The suspension-to-cancellation cycle also runs on its own clock (the 180-day suspension lapsed around March 2016). So almost any cancellation date in mid-2016 would sit within days of some Gulberg milestone. Among NDA-era cancellations of non-critics used as controls (World Vision, Compassion, CASA), the same timing lens gives nothing to test, which means it cannot tell targeting apart from routine processing. Across the 2016 population, about 20,000 cancellations were mostly for non-filing. Sabrang is one of a small set cancelled after an inspection on grounds that were stated and contested: admin ratio, payments to SCPPL, and editorial roles (see c038).
verdicts.denialFound: This claim is about the fact of the action, not its grounds, so a denial is not really the right test. The affected party responded: Sabrang Trust expressed "shock and surprise" that the order "completely ignored the detailed point by point response"; Setalvad and Anand were weighing a court challenge; Javed Anand told DNA on 2016-06-17 that he was "not surprised" and would seek legal advice. I found no statement from MHA beyond the order and the website notice. Firstpost's "Unmasking Teesta Setalvad: Here's why her NGO has lost its FCRA registration" (2016-06-17) gives a government-side account of the grounds; the headline was seen in Google News but the text was not opened. Whether MHA was asked about the timing: none found, not asked.
verdicts.innocentReading: This is the end of a standard FCRA process: inspection in June 2015, suspension in September 2015, the Trust's reply in October 2015, cancellation after that reply was assessed. The court had fixed its sentencing date on its own schedule, so the one-day gap is a coincidence of two processes that each have their own timelines. The cancellation date fits routine processing, and nothing in the evidence shows the date was chosen with reference to the court.
verdicts.reason: The core edge (MHA cancelled Sabrang Trust's FCRA registration on 2016-06-16) survives. The source says it, and a separate record confirms it: the FIDH/OMCT urgent appeal of 2016-07-06 cites the MHA website notice of that date, and The Hindu's report dated 2016-06-16 is listed. There are two weaknesses. (1) The only cited source is CJP, Setalvad's own organisation, republishing Sabrangindia. That is the affected party's statement, not an independent credible outlet. The 'reported' tier only stands once an independent source is attached, and the next step would be documented. (2) The label phrase "(day before Gulberg verdict)" is the accused party's insinuation. It is also imprecise: 17 June was the sentencing, while conviction was on 2 June. It suggests a motive that no source establishes. It belongs in the narrative with attribution, not in the edge label.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Change the text/lab to "Cancellation of Sabrang Trust FCRA registration, 2016-06-16" and remove "(day before Gulberg verdict)" from the edge label. If the timing stays in `d`, write it as: "Sabrang/CJP note the order came one day before sentencing in the Gulberg Society case (2016-06-17); the conviction verdict was 2016-06-02." 2) Add an independent source: ["FIDH/OMCT Observatory urgent appeal IND 003/0716/OBS 054, 2016-07-06 — MHA website notice of 2016-06-16, cancellation 'with immediate effect'", "https://www.fidh.org/en/issues/human-rights-defenders/india-cancellation-of-the-license-of-sabrang-trust-under-the-foreign"]. Also add The Hindu 2016-06-16 "Teesta's Trust loses FCRA registration" or Mint 2016-06-17 "Home ministry cancels Sabrang Trust's FCRA licence" once opened. With a second independent news text opened, upgrade to documented. 3) Change upgradeIf to "The Hindu/Mint text opened or MHA order/cancelled-list entry retrieved". 4) Fix sibling records c036 and c039: the CJP source ties the "24-page response" to a reply dated 2015-10-05 challenging the 2015-09-09 suspension, not to the 2015-06-25 reply (which answered the 2015-06-05 observations). Also add the 180-day suspension period (per FIDH) to c036. 5) Keep the December 2016 CJP renewal-then-cancellation as a separate edge; do not merge it into this one.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: MHA (Foreigners Division / FCRA wing) alleged three grounds against Sabrang Trust, carried into the cancellation order of 2016-06-16. The timeline holds. According to CJP and FIDH, the Gujarat Home Department asked for an inspection on 2015-03-10. The inspection ran 2015-04-09 to 11 and "observations" were issued in June 2015 (CJP says June 5, FIDH says June 4). The Trust replied on 2015-06-25. Registration was suspended on 2015-09-09, the Trust sent its 24-page response on 2015-10-05, and the cancellation followed on 2016-06-16. FIDH independently confirms that the MHA website announced the cancellation on June 16, 2016. The allegations started in the 2015 observations, and CJP says the 2016 Order "mechanically repeats the alleged violations ... as set out in its earlier 'observations'". So the from-date of 2016-06-16 is right for the order, but the grounds first appeared in June 2015. The CJP page's datePublished metadata is 2017-06-12, which looks like a site republish. The allegation-and-response text comes from the Trust's 2015-10-05 communication. The ₹50 lakh covers 2006-07 to 2013-14. "Seven years" is the Trust's own wording ("between 2006-07 and 2013-14, i.e. 7 years"), which is really eight financial years. It is not MHA's wording.
verdicts.identityTest: The source names Sabrang Trust, Mumbai, with an FCRA Registration Certificate dated November 21, 2007. The FCRA registration number is not given. The payee is named as Sabrang Communications & Publishing Pvt Ltd (SCPPL), publisher of Communalism Combat, with co-editors Javed Anand and Teesta Setalvad. The actor is "MHA-FCRA department", and the observations were signed by Under Secretary Anand Joshi (FIDH). This matches ngo:mha-foreigners-division and ngo:sabrang-trust. The claim keeps the Trust and SCPPL apart as separate legal entities, which is correct. It does not name a family, religion or ethnicity as the actor.
verdicts.baseRate: No data is in hand. Most FCRA cancellations cite non-filing of annual returns. Specific findings from an inspection (admin ratio above 50%, transfers to a related entity) are much less common, so this ground set does discriminate rather than being boilerplate. For the SPEC control (UPA 2011-14 cancellations), the same "admin over 50%" and "related-party transfer" grounds were available under FCRA 2010 and the 2011 FCRA Rules (FCRR). The file does not measure how often UPA used them, so the symmetry question stays open. That affects the narrative, not this edge, which only records what was alleged.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, from the Trust. The CJP source (https://cjp.org.in/cancellation-of-fcra-of-sabrang-trust-to-stop-public-justice-says-teesta-setalvad/) says the admin ratio is "an entirely erroneous reading of Rule 5 of FCRR, 2011" because project costs were counted as admin. It calls the ₹50 lakh "an exaggerated figure as it does not appear to tally with the audited accounts" and says the payments were for shared expenses. It argues the Trust is "an independent legal entity" and that the Registration Certificate's para 3 binds only the association, not its trustees. FIDH (https://www.fidh.org/en/issues/human-rights-defenders/india-cancellation-of-the-license-of-sabrang-trust-under-the-foreign) reports the Trust's worksheet showing admin at 30% (2010-11) and 31.5% (2011-12). This is already recorded as contra edge c039. I found no court ruling on the grounds.
verdicts.innocentReading: A regulator ran an inspection and applied a mechanical ratio test to a salary-heavy legal-aid and advocacy trust. Under a broad reading of "administrative expenses" in Rule 5 of FCRR 2011, staff costs push the ratio over 50%. Regular payments to a related company that shares staff and office space look like related-party transfers. The Trust calls these cost-shares for shared staff and office. Either reading fits the same accounts. The other reading is also on the record: the inspection was ordered after a request from the Gujarat Home Department, whose former head of government the trustees had criticised. The edge, as tiered, rests on neither reading.
verdicts.reason: The claim survives. The source says what the claim says. Quotes: "Allegation: 64.23% and 55.14% of donations for the years 2010-2011 and 2011-2012 have been spent on administrative expenses"; "Allegation: Rs 50 lakhs reimbursed to Sabrang Communications & Publishing Private Limited (SCPPL) were transferred for personal gain"; "Allegation: Since Javed Anand and Teesta Setalvad are co-editors of Communalism Combat ... Sabrang Trust has violated provisions of the FCRA Act." FIDH independently confirms that the cancellation order cites admin expenses above 50%. The tier is right: these are government allegations that no court has ruled on, and the claim carries a contra (c039). The one source is the accused party's own publication, but that is fine here because it publishes allegations against itself. It should not go up to reported or documented until the order text or a court finding is in hand.
verdicts.corrections: (1) Label: say "₹50 lakh between 2006-07 and 2013-14 (Trust's figure: '7 years'; MHA figure is the ₹50 lakh total)" instead of "over seven years", and put "personal gain" in quotes as MHA's characterisation. (2) Add FIDH (https://www.fidh.org/en/issues/human-rights-defenders/india-cancellation-of-the-license-of-sabrang-trust-under-the-foreign) as a second source. It independently confirms that the 2016-06-16 order cites more than 50% admin expenses, and gives the Trust's counter-figures of 30% and 31.5%. (3) In d, note that the grounds first appeared in the inspection observations of June 2015 (CJP says June 5, FIDH says June 4), were repeated in the 2016-06-16 order (per the Trust), and that the inspection followed a request from the Gujarat Home Department on 2015-03-10. (4) Related fix to c039: the published point-by-point rebuttal is the Trust's 2015-10-05 response, which builds on the 2015-06-25 reply, so the date there should be corrected. (5) killIf is fine. Add upgradeIf: "MHA cancellation order text obtained."

verdicts.dateTest: The claim, stated plainly: MHA (Union Home Ministry) asserted, in a statement of 2020-09-29 (published by Tribune 2020-09-30, 01:23), that Amnesty UK had routed money to four Indian entities as FDI. MHA was the FCRA regulator throughout, and the statement came out the same day Amnesty halted its India work. The FCRA permission of 2000-12-19 that the statement cites is historical context, not the action. The dates line up. from=2020-09-29 is acceptable because the statement was issued that evening and reported the next day.
verdicts.identityTest: The source names "Amnesty International", "Amnesty UK", "four entities registered in India" and "Amnesty (India)". The four entities are not named in the source, and no CIN or FCRA registration number is given. The target node ngo:amnesty-international-india is an umbrella for the Indian entities (its sub-label reads "Indian entities of Amnesty International"), which fits the source's collective reference. The actor is right: the statement is attributed to the Union Home Ministry.
verdicts.baseRate: The claim only records that MHA gave this reason for its action. Almost every FCRA enforcement action comes with a government-stated ground of misuse or diversion, so the fact that a ground was asserted does not set Amnesty apart. It is correctly tiered as an assertion by a named party and makes no discriminating inference. On symmetry: aligned or non-critical associations (Compassion 2016, WVI, Believers) also received routing or diversion grounds in the same file, so this lens gives the same reading for the controls. The claim does not frame any family, religion or ethnicity as the actor.
verdicts.denialFound: Amnesty press release of 2020-09-29 (https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/press-release/2020/09/amnesty-international-india-halts-its-work-on-upholding-human-rights-in-india-due-to-reprisal-from-government-of-india/), quoted in the existing contra: "No laws have been broken"; "intimidation without an iota of credible evidence". This is a general denial. The opened release does not address the FDI or four-entity point specifically, and nothing in the record shows whether Amnesty was asked about this particular ground.
verdicts.innocentReading: Amnesty India ran on a mixed structure: a trust plus a private company billing for services, with foreign money arriving as FDI or service income into the company rather than as FCRA contributions. Amnesty's position is that this route was lawful for a non-FCRA entity. Whether it was a lawful FEMA route or FCRA circumvention is exactly the legal question in dispute, so the MHA characterisation ("mala fide") is a regulator's assertion, not a finding.
verdicts.reason: The source confirms the claim almost word for word. Tribune 2020-09-30, reporting the MHA statement: "Amnesty UK remitted large amounts of money to four entities registered in India by classifying it as Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)... This mala fide rerouting of money was in contravention of extant legal provisions." The claim is framed as an alleged ground, which matches the evidence (an unadjudicated government assertion), and it carries a contra. Actor, date and target all check out. The only gap is a paraphrase: the source does not say "to circumvent FCRA". It says the rerouting was "in contravention of extant legal provisions", and it states separately that money reached Amnesty (India) without FCRA approval.
verdicts.corrections: 1) lab: replace "to circumvent FCRA" with "in contravention of extant legal provisions" (the source's words), or write "…as FDI; separately, foreign money to Amnesty (India) without FCRA approval". The source does not tie the FDI route specifically to circumventing FCRA; the FEMA and FCRA regimes are separate. 2) Contra d: add "general denial; the opened release does not address the FDI/four-entity ground specifically". 3) upgradeIf: the reported ED adjudication under FEMA (July 2022 penalty on Amnesty India International Pvt Ltd and Aakar Patel) and the CBI chargesheet under FCRA, if a primary order or ED release is opened. This is a quasi-judicial finding, still subject to appeal; I could not verify it in this session because the search budget was exhausted. Until then, keep "Not adjudicated in an opened source".

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: the MHA Foreigners Division (acting for the Union of India) suspended CHRI's FCRA registration on 2021-06-07, extended the suspension in 2021-12 and cancelled the registration in 2022-04. All three dates are consistent across sources. The Scroll article (published 2022-04-27T08:29+05:30) says: "On June 7, the Centre had suspended Commonwealth Human Rights Initiative's registration under the FCRA for 180 days citing several violations of the Act. In December, the government extended the suspension for another 180 days." Scroll does not give the year for June 7, but the Delhi HC judgment of 2022-02-14 in W.P.(C) 6400/2021 (Kameswar Rao J., Indian Kanoon doc 18161912) does: "On June 07, 2021, the petitioner's FCRA Registration was suspended for 180 days under Section 13 ..." and "On December 01, 2021, the impugned suspension was extended for another period of 180 days." The cancellation date comes from the Division Bench order of 2022-04-20 in LPA 231/2022 (doc 55471236): "only yesterday, the appellant has been served with an order of cancellation of the registration". That makes the service date 2022-04-19, which falls inside the second 180-day window (2021-12-01 plus 180 days is about 2022-05-30). So "before the second 180 days lapsed" holds.
verdicts.identityTest: The entity matches. The HC judgment names the petitioner as "COMMONWEALTH HUMAN RIGHTS INITIATIVE", granted "Certificate of Registration No. 231650671" on 1993-09-03 under FCRA 1976, and renewed on 2016-10-28 up to 2021-10-31. It is the Delhi-headquartered NGO founded in 1987, which is how Scroll describes it. The respondent is the Union of India, represented by the CGSC; the MHA is the FCRA authority. Attributing the action to the MHA Foreigners Division is a fair operational mapping, though the court records name only the Union of India / MHA.
verdicts.baseRate: Being suspended, having the suspension extended and then being cancelled is the standard FCRA escalation under ss.13–14. The same file records that sequence for World Vision India (2022-11, extended 2023-05) and CPR (2023-02 plus 180 days). Having the property therefore tells you nothing about why CHRI in particular was targeted. That does not matter here, because the edge only asserts that the enforcement act happened, not that CHRI was singled out. On the SPEC control, a bare enforcement edge reads the same under UPA (for example, the 2012 Kudankulam-linked cancellations would get the same kind of edge). No family, religion or ethnicity is framed as the actor.
verdicts.denialFound: CHRI's own position is on the court record. In the HC judgment (2022-02-14, W.P.(C) 6400/2021, https://indiankanoon.org/doc/18161912/): "On June 26, 2021, the petitioner communicated its response to the impugned suspension order, wherein it is stated that there was no violation of the FCRA, 2010 or Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Rules, 2011 ... as alleged." CHRI also argued there were no jurisdictional facts under s.13(1), because the audit was authorised only on 2021-07-29, after the suspension. The HC rejected these arguments. CHRI's lawyer told The Hindu (quoted by Scroll) that the challenge "became infructuous due to the cancellation order by MHA". I found no public press statement from CHRI after the cancellation; web search budget was exhausted, so that was not searched beyond the court record.
verdicts.innocentReading: The MHA's stated grounds were those in the suspension order and the Show Cause Notice of 2021-12-07: s.17/18/19 reporting and account violations, plus, per unnamed officials quoted by TOI via Scroll, foreign funds used for projects outside India and consultancy fees shown as foreign contribution. On this reading these are routine compliance grounds, handled through the ordinary suspension, extension and cancellation route, and a single-judge bench upheld the suspension as within s.13(1). The edge as worded ("enforce") does not assert pretext, so it stays neutral.
verdicts.reason: I could not refute the claim. Scroll confirms every element: the June 7 suspension, the December extension and the April 2022 cancellation. Two primary Delhi HC records independently confirm the exact dates (suspension 2021-06-07, extension 2021-12-01, cancellation served 2022-04-19) and the registration number (231650671). Because the facts rest on court orders, the tier should move from reported to documented. The only weak point is that the grounds for cancellation come from unnamed MHA officials quoted second-hand. Those grounds should stay out of the edge, or be carried as MHA's alleged grounds with CHRI's denial as the contra.
verdicts.corrections: tier: reported -> documented. srcs: add ["Delhi HC 2022-02-14, W.P.(C) 6400/2021, CHRI v Union of India (Kameswar Rao J.)", "https://indiankanoon.org/doc/18161912/"] and ["Delhi HC DB order 2022-04-20, LPA 231/2022 (cancellation served 2022-04-19)", "https://indiankanoon.org/doc/55471236/"]. lab: add the cancellation, e.g. "Suspension of CHRI FCRA registration 2021-06-07 (180 days), extended 2021-12-01; cancelled (served 2022-04-19)". to: "2022-04-19". Add the identifier FCRA reg. no. 231650671 to the target node ngo:commonwealth-human-rights-initiative. d: add CHRI's contra, its 2021-06-26 response denying any FCRA/FCRR violation, plus the argument that the audit was authorised only on 2021-07-29. Also state that the Scroll-reported cancellation grounds come from unnamed MHA officials via TOI; they are alleged, not adjudicated. Note that the HC quote comes from a single-judge bench, and that the appeal (LPA 231/2022) became infructuous after cancellation.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: MHA Foreigners Division cancelled CHRI's FCRA registration, citing three grounds, in April 2022. The Delhi HC order of 24.07.2024 (W.P.(C) 8666/2022) gives the order date as 19 April 2022, issued by the Director, Foreigners Division (Monitoring Unit). Scroll's report is dated 2022-04-27. The actor, office and date line up. The record's timeline is out of date, though. The 19-04-2022 order was set aside on 24-07-2024 because it was a non-speaking order, and the matter was remanded for a fresh decision within 8 weeks. MHA issued a fresh cancellation order dated 12-09-2024. CHRI challenged that order (Justice Sachin Datta issued notice in March 2025). So the edge's from=2022-04 / to=null, and its note that "the HC review concerned the suspension only", are both wrong.
verdicts.identityTest: Pass. The HC order quotes the show-cause notice: "Commonwealth Human Rights Initiative (CHRI), Delhi ... registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 vide No. S-24565 ... Registration Certificate No. 231650671R dated 09.03.1993". The cancelling authority was the Director, Foreigners Division (Monitoring Unit), MHA, which matches ngo:mha-foreigners-division. The entity is the Delhi-based CHRI founded in 1987, the same organisation Scroll names.
verdicts.baseRate: Not discriminating on its own. MHA cancelled roughly 16,000–20,000 FCRA registrations in 2014–2024. Defective FC-4 annual returns are among the most common grounds cited. Ending up with a cancellation is ordinary. What is unusual here is the route: suspension, extended suspension, audit, cancellation, the cancellation quashed as non-speaking, then re-issued. The UPA-era 2011–14 cancellations named in the SPEC control also mostly cited return and utilisation defects, so this lens gives the same reading for the control. The edge does not frame a family, religion or ethnicity as the actor.
verdicts.denialFound: A response exists and is on the court record. The claim's "(no CHRI response recorded)" is false. (1) Delhi HC order of 24.07.2024 (https://indiankanoon.org/doc/145253799/): "the Petitioner clarified that the amount of Rs. 31,90,598/- was received from the Department of International Development, UK and Transparency International Sri Lanka for conducting certain learning programmes in India in 2014 and 2018. They explained their reason for construing the payments as a 'foreign contribution'... They maintained that the foreign contributions received from various entities had been utilized in compliance with the Act." CHRI's replies are dated 20-12-2021 and 02-03-2022, and it was heard in person on 16-02-2022. (2) CHRI's 2025 petition against the 12-09-2024 order, as reported by ANI (https://aninews.in/news/national/general-news/delhi-high-court-seeks-centres-reply-on-rights-body-chris-plea-against-fcra-revokal20250317194346/): "the petitioner stated that it has utilized all foreign contributions solely for the intended and permissible purposes ... has provided complete and accurate information in the statutory Form FC-4 for FY 2018-19". The petition also says MHA "unjustifiably relied on undisclosed agency reports". (3) Scroll's own article quotes CHRI's lawyer, but only on procedure.
verdicts.innocentReading: The Rs 31.9 lakh was fees from DFID (UK) and TI Sri Lanka for learning programmes CHRI ran in India. CHRI read these as foreign contribution and deposited them in its FC account. That is a classification dispute under Explanation 3 to s.2(1)(h), not concealment. Spending on activities abroad fits CHRI's Commonwealth-wide mandate, which MHA reads as outside s.1(2). The FC-4 disclosure gaps are the kind of return defect that is common across FCRA cancellations. The HC found the first order failed to engage with any of these explanations.
verdicts.reason: Scroll does support the three grounds, attributed to unnamed MHA officials via TOI: "failed to provide details about some projects for which it received foreign funds in its annual report"; "using foreign funds received in India, for its projects outside the country"; "provided consultation to a foreign entity and showed the professional fees as foreign contributions". The primary text of those grounds is also in the 2024 HC order. The claim still fails as written, for three reasons. (a) "(no CHRI response recorded)" is false: CHRI's point-by-point rebuttal is in a court order, and an alleged-tier edge must carry a contra. (b) The 19-04-2022 cancellation it describes was set aside by the Delhi HC on 24-07-2024 as non-speaking. The standing act is a fresh order of 12-09-2024, which CHRI has challenged. (c) "no project details" overstates the source, which says details were missing for "some projects" in the FY2018-19 FC-4. The enforcement act itself is documented. The grounds remain unadjudicated government allegations, so alleged is the right tier for the grounds once a contra is added.
verdicts.corrections: text/lab: replace "no project details" with "incomplete FC-4 disclosure of activities/projects for FY2018-19 and inconsistent FC opening/closing balances 2013-14 to 2018-19". Replace "consultancy fees booked as foreign contribution" with "consultation fee of Rs 31,90,598 credited to the FC-designated account (s.17)". Remove "(no CHRI response recorded)". Add contra: CHRI says the Rs 31.9 lakh came from DFID UK and TI Sri Lanka for learning programmes in India, that FC was used lawfully, and that the FC-4 was complete; cite https://indiankanoon.org/doc/145253799/ and the ANI 2025-03-17 report. d: correct "the HC review concerned the suspension only". Add that on 24-07-2024 (Sanjeev Narula J) the Delhi HC set aside the 19-04-2022 order as non-speaking without ruling on merits, that MHA re-cancelled on 12-09-2024, and that CHRI's challenge was pending from March 2025 (Sachin Datta J). Either set to=2024-07-24 and add a superseding edge from=2024-09-12, or set supersededBy accordingly. srcs: add the 2024 HC order as a primary source for the grounds, and add the ANI/Verdictum/Bar&Bench reports on the 2024–25 litigation. upgradeIf: the "cancellation order text" condition is partly met through the HC quotation, but only a merits ruling can move the grounds themselves beyond alleged. killIf is unchanged: a merits ruling for CHRI.

verdicts.dateTest: Written out: CBI (on an MHA complaint) alleged in an FIR dated 2023-04-19, and in a chargesheet filed 2025-01-23, that Oxfam India did four things. (a) It planned to pressure the government through foreign governments and institutions to get its FCRA renewal, after the refusal in December 2021 (2021-12 to 2022). (b) It received funds after its registration ceased on 2022-01-01. (c) It kept paying sub-grants after the 2020 Amendment took effect (2020-09-29 onward). (d) It got around its designated FCRA account in 2013–2016. Each alleged act falls in a period when Oxfam India existed and was FCRA-registered, or had just lost registration. Item (d) is judged under the 2010 Act's designated-account rule, as the record's own d-field notes. The FIR comes after the IT survey (2022-09) and the chargesheet comes after the FIR. Both dates match the sources: CIVICUS says "April 19, 2023" and The Week says "Filed January 23, 2025 before a special court in Delhi". The date test passes.
verdicts.identityTest: Both sources name "Oxfam India", and the chargesheet names former CEO Amitabh Behar. The entity is correct, so the edge target stands. The node's legal form is wrong, though. The oxfamindia.org footer says: "Oxfam India is a registered Non-profit under Section 8 of the Indian Companies Act, 2013". So it is a Section 8 company, not a trust. The node has ty "trust", sub "Oxfam India Trust" and alias "Oxfam India Trust", and all identity fields are null (no CIN, no FCRA number). The identity rests on the name plus the office named in the sources. That is acceptable for a single well-known organisation, but the node should carry the CIN or FCRA registration number.
verdicts.baseRate: This property discriminates; it is not common. On 2022-01-01, 5,933 associations lost registration (179 were refused renewal). Only a handful of them then faced CBI FIRs or chargesheets: Oxfam, CPR, Environics and CPSC appear in this file. That is under 0.1% of the ceased cohort. The allegations are specific to this case, not a generic ground that applies to everyone. The symmetry control points the other way from neutral: every CBI FCRA FIR in this file is against a government-critical or international-affiliated association. Aligned or domestic-philanthropy controls (Azim Premji, Tata, Reliance, Adani Foundation) have no comparable action on record, and UPA-era 2012 FCRA action was cancellations, not CBI chargesheets. That is a point for the selectivity narrative. It does not undercut the edge, which only reports what the agencies allege.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes. Oxfam India said it "is fully compliant with Indian laws and has filed all its statutory compliances, including Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA) returns, in a timely manner since its inception", and that it has "been cooperating with all government agencies since its FCRA registration wasn't renewed in December 2021". Sources: CIVICUS 2023-04-20 https://www.civicus.org/index.php/media-resources/news/6370-india-oxfam-targeted-again-with-accusations-of-foreign-funding-and-influencing and The Week 2025-01-23 https://www.theweek.in/news/india/2025/01/23/cbi-files-charge-sheet-against-oxfam-india-for-violating-fcra-norms.html. This is recorded as contra c050. Neither cited source gives the statement's date as 2023-04-06.
verdicts.innocentReading: The "pressure via foreign governments" allegation fits ordinary advocacy: an affiliate of an international confederation asks its partners and donor governments to raise its licence refusal. That is lobbying, not an offence in itself; the MHA's own framing is "has the reach and influence to request multilateral foreign organisations to intervene". Funds received after 2022-01-01 may be remittances already committed or in transit that sat in the FCRA account. Sub-grants after the 2020 Amendment may have honoured commitments made before it, while the scope of the ban was unsettled until the Supreme Court's 2022-04-08 ruling. The 2013–2016 routing may be a procedural or accounting lapse, the kind of ground often compounded under Section 41 rather than prosecuted. Two things cannot be tested from the evidence in hand: the trial is pending, and no court has made a finding.
verdicts.reason: Both source URLs say what the claim says, and I quoted them. CIVICUS carries the FIR date (2023-04-19) and all four allegations: pressure via foreign governments and institutions, receipt of funds after cessation, sub-grants after the 2020 ban, and designated-account circumvention in 2013–2016. The Week carries the chargesheet date (2025-01-23, special court, Delhi), the pressure allegation and the "structure to continue its operations with foreign funds" allegation. The dates line up, the entity is the one the sources name, and the response is on record as a linked contra. "Alleged" is the right tier for the content: the FIR and chargesheet are two independently reported facts, but what they assert has not been decided. I found nothing that refutes the claim. Caveat: my web-search budget was exhausted, so I could not check for any court development after 2025-01 (cognizance, discharge, quash).
verdicts.corrections: 1. Node ngo:oxfam-india has the wrong legal form. Change ty "trust" to a company type (Section 8 non-profit company, per the oxfamindia.org footer), and remove "Oxfam India Trust" from sub and al unless a separate trust entity is shown to exist. Fill in identity.cin and identity.fcra. 2. c050 (the contra) gives the statement date as "2023-04-06", but neither cited source gives that date. Either add a source dated 2023-04-06 (for example Oxfam India's statement or reporting when MHA recommended the CBI probe) or change it to "2023-04 (as quoted by CIVICUS 2023-04-20)". 3. c049 d-field: say which allegations come from which document. Per CIVICUS, the funds-after-cessation, sub-grant and 2013–2016 account allegations come from the FIR. Per The Week, the "planning to create a structure to continue its operations with foreign funds" allegation comes from the chargesheet, and the pressure allegation is based on IT survey material. Name Amitabh Behar (former CEO, now Oxfam International ED) as a chargesheeted accused. 4. Before publishing, check for any post-2025-01 court development (cognizance, discharge, quash), because it would trigger killIf or upgradeIf.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: MHA (Foreigners Division, FCRA wing) refused MoC's FCRA renewal on 2021-12-25, citing "adverse inputs" and failure to meet eligibility conditions. It said so publicly on 2021-12-27 and restored the registration on 2022-01-07. The actor was in office for the whole window, so the dates overlap. Onmanorama/PTI of 2022-01-01 says: "The MHA, on December 25, rejected the renewal application of the Missionaries of Charity ... for not meeting the eligibility conditions under the FCRA as some adverse inputs were received." India TV (2022-01-08) gives the restoration date: "The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) restored the registration on January 7." Vatican News says restoration came "less than a fortnight after" the refusal, so "~2 weeks" holds. One small fix: set `to` to 2022-01-07, not 2022-01-08. ThePrint's "December 27" is the date of MHA's statement, not the date of the refusal.
verdicts.identityTest: Pass. The source names "the Missionaries of Charity, founded by Mother Teresa in Kolkata" (the Superior General at the time was Sr M. Prema), and the issuing authority as the Union Ministry of Home Affairs. This matches ngo:missionaries-of-charity and ngo:mha-foreigners-division. The record holds no FCRA registration number, so it could not be checked; add it if one can be sourced.
verdicts.baseRate: Being refused renewal does not single MoC out. The same PTI story says renewal applications for about 6,500 of 22,762 registered NGOs had been processed. Around 2022-01-01 roughly 6,000 associations lost their registrations when renewals lapsed or were refused (reported widely, e.g. Oxfam India, Jamia, IIT-Delhi). What does stand out is that MHA put a named ground ("adverse inputs") on a single association and then reversed it within 13 days. The fleet SPEC names MoC as a non-critic control, so the symmetry check is built in: the same lens applied to a non-critic Catholic body produces the same pattern of an unspecified ground followed by a reversal.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, and the record wrongly says there is none. MoC statement of 2021-12-27, signed by Sr M. Prema, Superior General: "We would like to clarify that the FCRA registration of the Missionaries of Charity has been neither suspended nor cancelled. There is no freeze order by the MHA on any of our bank accounts. We have been informed that our FCRA renewal has not been approved. As a measure to ensure there is no lapse, we have asked our centres not to operate any of the FC accounts until the matter is resolved." Business Standard 2021-12-27: https://www.business-standard.com/article/current-affairs/fcra-registration-neither-suspended-nor-cancelled-missionaries-of-charity-121122701016_1.html ; also The Wire and The News Minute. This contradicts contra c054, which says "No response recorded — asked/not asked unknown".
verdicts.innocentReading: This was a routine renewal refusal during the end-2021 mass processing, when thousands of certificates lapsed. It may have been triggered by a documentation or eligibility gap. Government sources quoted in press said MoC then "submitted the necessary documents" and the registration was restored. On that reading, "adverse inputs" was boilerplate for an incomplete file, not an evidence-based finding against MoC.
verdicts.reason: The claim survives. Onmanorama (PTI) states exactly the ground the claim reports: refusal on December 25 "for not meeting the eligibility conditions under the FCRA as some adverse inputs were received". That ground is an unadjudicated government assertion, so the contract's `alleged` tier is correct. The restoration is independently documented (ThePrint, India TV, Business Standard, Vatican News). No outlet found reports MHA ever specifying the inputs, which supports "never specified". The source check is only partial because the edge's only source, Onmanorama, predates the restoration and says nothing about it. That half of the text needs ThePrint or India TV added as a source. The record also has three internal errors: the contra is wrong, supersededBy is left null although the text says superseded, and the killIf is incoherent. None of these refutes the claim.
verdicts.corrections: 1) srcs: add ThePrint 2022-01-08 (https://theprint.in/india/home-ministry-restores-fcra-license-of-missionaries-of-charity/798425/) and India TV 2022-01-08 (https://www.indiatvnews.com/news/india/govt-restores-fcra-licence-of-missionaries-of-charity-tmc-mp-takes-swipe-2022-01-08-753380) to support the restoration and "~2 weeks". 2) to: "2022-01-07", not "2022-01-08". 3) supersededBy: set to "fcra-actions:c052" to match the text's "superseded by restoration", or change the text to "ground not withdrawn; outcome reversed by restoration". 4) killIf: restoration does not falsify the fact that MHA stated this ground, so the current killIf ("Already effectively superseded by restoration") is already met and incoherent. Replace it with "MHA statement shown not to cite adverse inputs". 5) c054 contra: replace "No response recorded" with the MoC statement of 2021-12-27 (Sr M. Prema: registration "neither suspended nor cancelled", "no freeze order by the MHA", "renewal has not been approved"), sourced to Business Standard 2021-12-27, tier reported. Note also that MoC did not address MHA's claim that it asked SBI to freeze its accounts. 6) d: add that government sources said MoC submitted the necessary documents before the restoration (the innocent reading), and give the base-rate context (~6,500 of 22,762 renewals processed; mass lapses on 2022-01-01).

verdicts.dateTest: Written out, the claim is: Amit Shah (Union Home Minister since 2019-05-30) asserted on 2022-12-13 that RGF received ₹1.35 crore from the Chinese embassy in FY2005-06 and FY2006-07. His tenure covers both the statement and the 2022-10 cancellation. The receipts fell under the FCRA 1976 regime, not the 2010 Act, and the record's d field already says so correctly. Two date faults. (1) The edge has from=2005 and to=2007. That is the receipt window, not the date of the act the edge records (Shah stating the ground). Set from=2022-12-13 and move the receipt years into d. (2) The linked contra c058 dates the Singhvi quote "(2022-10)". India CSR says the quote is from 2020: "Party leaders, in 2020, termed the allegations ... a 'witch-hunt' ... Singhvi had said". So it answers the June 2020 BJP allegation, not the 2022-10 cancellation or the 2022-12 statement.
verdicts.identityTest: The actor is right: Tribune names "Union Home Minister Amit Shah". The target is right: "Rajiv Gandhi Foundation (RGF)", kept distinct from "Rajiv Gandhi Trust", which the claim correctly leaves to c059. No FCRA registration number is recorded for RGF in the node or the source, so the identity rests on the name alone. The venue is WRONG. The claim says "Home Minister, Lok Sabha 2022-12". Tribune says the words were said to the press outside Parliament because Question Hour did not run: "Addressing the media outside Parliament, he said, 'The Opposition leaders did not allow the question hour to run in the Lok Sabha...'" and "Had he got the opportunity, said Shah, he would have told Parliament that during the 2005-06 and 2006-07 fiscals, the RGF had received Rs 1.35 crore from the Chinese embassy." So this is not a Parliament answer or statement and is not on the Lok Sabha record.
verdicts.baseRate: No full measurement was possible because the web-search budget was used up. The 1976 Act counted a foreign government or its mission as a "foreign source". It did not bar a registered association from receiving money from one, so an embassy grant to a registered think tank was an ordinary, reportable receipt. RGF's own 2005-06 annual report lists the "Embassy of The People's Republic of China" among its "partner organisations and donors" (India CSR). Embassy funding of Indian policy think tanks is common, so the receipt alone does not single RGF out. What would single it out is the provision breached, and neither the statement nor any record in hand names one. SPEC control not run: the same test should ask whether government-aligned think tanks (Vivekananda International Foundation, India Foundation) had embassy or foreign-government receipts and faced any action. That is not in the file.
verdicts.denialFound: No response to the 2022-12-13 statement itself was found; the one search attempted was blocked by the exhausted budget, and Tribune's article carries no Congress reply. The only recorded response (c058, India CSR, https://indiacsr.in/fcra-of-rajiv-gandhi-foundation-and-rajiv-gandhi-charitable-trust-cancelled/) is Singhvi in 2020: "The Rajiv Gandhi Foundation has nothing to add, nothing to fear ... you don't ask these questions of many holy cows ... You are harassing each opposition segment". It answers the same Chinese-embassy allegation (Nadda, 2020-06-25), but its date must be corrected to 2020. Whether RGF was asked for comment in 2022-12 is unknown.
verdicts.innocentReading: RGF was an established association (founded 1991). It took a disclosed grant from the Chinese embassy, which BJP leaders in 2020 put at $300,000 — about ₹1.35 crore at the 2005-06 rate of roughly ₹45 per dollar, so the figures match. RGF says the grant was for work including a study of an India–China free trade agreement, and it listed the embassy openly as a donor in its 2005-06 annual report. The receipt was lawful under the 1976 Act if it went through RGF's designated FCRA account and was reported in its returns. The government investigated it only in 2020, 14 years later and during the Galwan/LAC political row. Shah's "not in conformity with the FCRA laws" names no provision. The cancellation order and the committee report have not been published.
verdicts.reason: The substance holds. Tribune quotes Shah word for word: "the RGF had received Rs 1.35 crore from the Chinese embassy" in "the 2005-06 and 2006-07 fiscals"; "Since the transaction was not in conformity with the FCRA laws, the MHA cancelled its registration". The amount, the years, the actor and the quoted phrase all match, and "alleged" is the correct tier for an unadjudicated ministerial assertion. The claim as written still fails on attribution. It puts the statement in the Lok Sabha, but the source says Shah said it to the media outside Parliament, and only claimed he would have told Parliament had Question Hour run. A Lok Sabha statement would be a parliamentary record, which the CONTRACT treats as documented-grade; a press remark is not, so the error changes how the evidence reads. The same wrong "in the Lok Sabha" wording appears elsewhere in the file: the source label on c055, c056 and c057 ("Amit Shah in Lok Sabha on RGF/RGCT grounds"), the pol:amit-shah publicRole, and the trustee rows at lines ~386 and ~539. In addition, the paired contra (c058) is misdated: it is from 2020, not 2022-10. The claim survives as alleged only after these fixes.
verdicts.corrections: In c057, change lab to: "Alleged ground (Home Minister Amit Shah, to media outside Parliament, 2022-12-13): RGF received ₹1.35 crore from the Chinese embassy in 2005-06 and 2006-07 'not in conformity with the FCRA laws'". Set from=2022-12-13 and to=null, and put the receipt window FY2005-06 to FY2006-07 in d. Add to d that the 2020 BJP figure of $300,000 is consistent with ₹1.35 crore at about ₹45 per dollar, and that RGF's 2005-06 annual report lists the embassy among its "partner organisations and donors" (India CSR). That disclosure bears on killIf, but it is not the FCRA return, so killIf is not yet met. Rename the source label in c055, c056 and c057 from "Amit Shah in Lok Sabha on RGF/RGCT grounds" to "Amit Shah to media outside Parliament, 2022-12-13". Fix the same venue in the pol:amit-shah publicRole ("stated RGF grounds in the Lok Sabha 2022-12") and in the trustee rows (~lines 386 and 539: "Named among RGF trustees by the Home Minister in the Lok Sabha"), and check that the trustee naming actually appears in the Tribune text. Apply the same venue fix to c059. In c058, change "(2022-10)" to "(2020, responding to the June 2020 BJP allegation)", and note that no response to the 2022-12-13 statement was found. upgradeIf is unchanged: the cancellation order or committee report naming the provision breached, or the Lok Sabha starred question and its answer if one was later laid on the table.

verdicts.dateTest: Written out, the claim reads: Amit Shah (Union Home Minister since 30 May 2019) asserted on 2022-12-13 that RGCT received ₹50 lakh from IRF in 2011. The statement falls inside his tenure, so that part passes. The edge still fails the date test in two ways. (1) Its from/to is "2011". That is the donation year, not the date of any enforcement act. MHA cancelled RGCT's FCRA registration in Oct 2022 under Section 14, and Shah made his remark on 2022-12-13. (2) The edge leaves out that the money was returned in July 2016. Indian Express, 2016-09-10, quoting IRF spokesperson Aarif Malik: "We have received the money back in July this year." Daily Mail India, 2016-09-09: "the amount was returned after an emergency meeting of the trust in July." The 2011 receipt came 3+ years before the NDA government and 5 years before IRF came under scrutiny after the July 2016 Dhaka attack. IRF was declared unlawful under UAPA in Nov 2016.
verdicts.identityTest: The recipient is right. RGCT, not RGF, is the entity named. Indian Express 2016 says Home Ministry officials described the donation as going "to an allied entity of RGF called Rajiv Gandhi Charitable Trust (RGCT) in 2011". The actor/predicate is wrong. The edge is s=pol:amit-shah, pred=enforce, but under CONTRACT `enforce` means agency → subject. Shah did not take the enforcement action. MHA, as an agency, cancelled the registration in Oct 2022, and Shah's remark was a political statement to the press. The venue in the label is also wrong. The Tribune source says: "Addressing the media outside Parliament, he said..." and "Had he got the opportunity, said Shah, he would have told Parliament..." He did not say this in the Lok Sabha. The Lok Sabha question hour was disrupted, and the 5th question, on RGF's FCRA, was never answered on the floor.
verdicts.baseRate: Transfers from one FCRA-registered association to another were legal before the FCRA Amendment 2020 and were routine. Indian Express, 2016-09-10: "Organisations like IRF registered under the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act are allowed to transfer money they receive from abroad to other FCRA approved bodies. Both RGF and RGCT have FCRA licence." IRF's spokesman said "We gave money to other NGOs also." So having received an FCRA-to-FCRA transfer in 2011 does not set RGCT apart. What would set it apart is the donor's later designation (UAPA 2016). That did not exist in 2011, which makes it a hindsight property. Scale: Rajya Sabha (MoS Nityanand Rai, 2022-12-07, via TOI) reported 6,677 FCRA cancellations from 2017 to 2021. I could not run the symmetry check against the SPEC control. I have no list of IRF's other recipients to test whether government-aligned or neutral recipients of IRF money faced similar action or rhetoric.
verdicts.denialFound: The file carries the wrong contra. c059's contra is a generic Oct 2022 Singhvi line ("nothing to fear; selective harassment"). The Congress has given a specific response on this donation. Indian Express 2016-09-10 (https://indianexpress.com/article/india/india-news-india/zakir-naik-ngo-irf-rajiv-gandhi-trust-3024135/): "Congress spokesperson Abhishek Manu Singhvi has owned up the donation but claimed it was unsolicited and a one-off affair. Singhvi emphasised that the donation preceded IRF's embroilment in allegations of terror and forced conversions, adding Naik's NGO was not on the watchlist at the time." Daily Mail India 2016-09-09 (https://www.dailymail.co.uk/indiahome/indianews/article-3782428/Rajiv-Gandhi-Foundation-returns-Rs-50-lakh-donation-Zakir-Naik-s-Islamic-Research-Foundation.html), Singhvi: "Do you expect us to know that Zakir Naik will be under scanner after years? ... The moment investigation against Naik began, the donation was returned." I found no specific Congress reply to Shah's 2022-12-13 restatement, and the Tribune article does not say whether Congress was asked.
verdicts.innocentReading: In 2011, IRF was an FCRA-registered association, not on any watchlist, and its FCRA licence was renewed as late as Aug 2016. It made an unsolicited ₹50 lakh transfer to another FCRA-registered trust, which was lawful at the time. RGCT returned the money in July 2016, once IRF came under investigation. In Dec 2022 the Home Minister brought it up again at a press stand-up outside Parliament to rebut an opposition question. The formal cancellation grounds MHA gave the Rajya Sabha on 2022-12-07 are section-level accounting and utilisation breaches: Sections 8(1)(a), 17, 18, 19 and others. As reported by TOI, they do not name the IRF donation. On that reading the IRF item is political rhetoric, not an established cancellation ground.
verdicts.reason: The Tribune source does say what the label says about amount, year and donor. Shah "Accuses Rajiv Gandhi Trust of receiving Rs 50 lakh from Zakir Naik's Islamic Research Foundation in 2011". But the edge as built fails on four counts. (a) It puts the remark in the "Lok Sabha", but the source says he was "addressing the media outside Parliament". (b) It models a Home Minister's press remark as an `enforce` edge from pol:amit-shah. Enforcement is agency → subject, and the enforcing act was MHA's Oct 2022 cancellation, whose formal grounds, stated in the Rajya Sabha on 2022-12-07, do not include the IRF donation as reported. (c) It tiers the receipt as "alleged". In fact the receipt is admitted by both sides: IRF's spokesperson and Congress's Singhvi, reported in Indian Express and Daily Mail India in Sept 2016. What is only alleged is Shah's framing of it as a violation or cancellation ground. (d) It leaves out the July 2016 return of the money and the pre-2020 legality of FCRA-to-FCRA transfers, which the killIf condition itself points to. Keeping this edge would misstate who did what, where, and how solid the evidence is.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Kill c059 as a pol:amit-shah → RGCT `enforce` edge. 2) Replace it with a `grant` edge: s = IRF node (Islamic Research Foundation, Mumbai; FCRA-registered in 2011; declared unlawful under UAPA Nov 2016), t = ngo:rajiv-gandhi-charitable-trust, a = 0.5, from = 2011, tier = reported. Source: Indian Express 2016-09-10 plus Daily Mail India 2016-09-09, i.e. two outlets plus the donor's admission, which arguably qualifies as documented. In d, add: "returned July 2016 (IRF spokesman; Singhvi); FCRA-to-FCRA transfer permitted pre-2020 amendment per IE". 3) Keep Shah's assertion only as a narrative/alleged item, with this label: "Home Minister Amit Shah, addressing media outside Parliament on 2022-12-13, cited RGCT's 2011 ₹50 lakh receipt from IRF as a reason for FCRA cancellation". Remove "Lok Sabha". 4) The `enforce` edge should be agency:mha → RGCT, Oct 2022, tier documented. Cite the Rajya Sabha answer of 2022-12-07 (MoS Nityanand Rai; Sections 8(1)(a), 11, 12(4)(a)(vi), 17, 18, 19, cancellation under Section 14), via TOI https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/rajiv-gandhi-trust-violated-sections-of-fcra-home-ministry-in-rajya-sabha/articleshow/96064930.cms. Also fetch the RS unstarred question PDF itself. 5) Replace the generic contra with Singhvi's specific 2016 response (unsolicited, one-off, before IRF was under scrutiny, returned) and cite the IE and Daily Mail URLs. Record that Congress's reply to the 2022-12-13 restatement: none found, not asked in the Tribune piece. 6) Fix the d text. The "not stated" line about domestic versus foreign source is answered by IE: the transfer went from one FCRA account to another, which was lawful in 2011.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: MHA (Foreigners Division) alleged four grounds against CPR, dated from 2024-01-10. The source chain splits these grounds across two stages. (1) "Undesirable purposes" was the MHA's argument in 2023 at the Delhi HC, when CPR challenged its February 2023 suspension. Tribune 2024-01-17: "When the CPR challenged its suspension in the Delhi High Court, the MHA had argued that the CPR's foreign funding needed to be stopped as it was receiving its foreign contributions for 'undesirable purposes' likely to affect the country's economic interest." (2) Transfer to other entities and non-designated accounts: "The MHA alleged that the CPR transferred foreign contributions to other entities and deposited the contributions in non-designated accounts in violation of FCRA." The article does not say whether this came from the suspension litigation or the cancellation order. (3) Current-affairs equivalence is the only ground tied to the cancellation itself, and only through CPR's own statement. Tribune 2024-01-20 quotes it: "On January 10, CPR received a notice from the Ministry of Home Affairs cancelling its FCRA status ... some of the reasons given ... This includes the publication on our website of policy reports ... being equated with current affairs programming." So 2024-01-10 is the date CPR received the notice, not a confirmed order date. Grouping all four grounds under one date of 2024-01-10 attributes 2023 suspension-stage arguments to the cancellation order. The MHA was the actor at both stages, so the actor passes; the stage attribution is loose.
verdicts.identityTest: Pass. Both outlets name "Centre for Policy Research", the Delhi think tank founded in 1973, whose president was Yamini Aiyar and whose former governing-body members included Manmohan Singh. The actor is the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). No outlet gives an FCRA registration number and the node's identity.fcra is null. There is no ambiguity about the entity.
verdicts.baseRate: Non-discriminating for three of the four grounds. Among the recipients named in this file, onward transfer and wrong-account grounds are the most common stated grounds after 2020: Oxfam, CARE India (₹28.3 cr in a domestic account), Environics and CPR. Our own c018 says as much. Once the 2020 Amendment banned sub-granting, most intermediary grantees face the same exposure. "Undesirable purposes / economic interest" is standard statutory language used in many orders. The discriminating element is the s.3 current-affairs ground applied to a research institute's website reports. No comparable application was found in this file for the government-aligned or neutral control think tanks (Vivekananda International Foundation, India Foundation). No enforcement records for those controls are in the file, so the symmetry comparison is incomplete rather than failed.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, CPR's statement of 2024-01-17, carried in National Herald (https://www.nationalheraldindia.com/india/incomprehensible-centre-for-policy-research-reaction-to-cancelled-fcra-registration-by-mha) and Tribune 2024-01-20: "The basis of this decision is incomprehensible and disproportionate, and some of the reasons given challenge the very basis of the functioning of a research institution." It says CPR obtained interim relief from the Delhi HC during the suspension. Tribune 2024-01-17 asked CPR for comment: "When contacted, CPR president ... Yamini Aiyar said the NGO will soon issue a statement." The response is already recorded as contra edge c065. The statement does not directly rebut the transfer or account allegations; it contests the reasoning in general and the current-affairs ground in particular.
verdicts.innocentReading: After the 2020 Amendment, a think tank that sub-granted or co-implemented with partners (the transfer ground) and kept funds in accounts other than the designated SBI FCRA account would breach the law in a routine technical way that applies to many associations. On that reading the cancellation is ordinary compliance enforcement and the "undesirable purposes" wording is standard statutory language. The reading does not easily cover the current-affairs ground, which on CPR's account treats published research as news programming.
verdicts.reason: The claim survives in substance. Two outlets report that the MHA made these allegations: Tribune reports the MHA's filed arguments ("officials said"), and CPR's own statement confirms the current-affairs ground. The allegations have not been adjudicated, so "alleged" with contra c065 is the correct tier. The decisive weakness is conflation, not falsity. The edge presents all four grounds as one set dated to the 2024-01-10 cancellation, but the "undesirable purposes / economic interest" ground is sourced to the MHA's 2023 Delhi HC arguments on the suspension. Only the current-affairs ground is tied to the cancellation notice, and only through CPR's characterisation. The task's single source (Tribune 01-17) does not contain the current-affairs ground at all. It appears only in the National Herald/CPR statement and in Tribune 01-20. Also, "(s.3)" is our own statutory gloss; no source cites a section. The FCRA ban on associations producing news or current-affairs programmes is in s.3(1), which makes the gloss plausible, but it should be marked as ours.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Sources: the computed claim lists only Tribune 2024-01-17. Keep the National Herald 2024-01-17 CPR statement (already in the file) and add Tribune 2024-01-20 (https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/india/fcra-licences-of-16-000-ngos-cancelled-in-9-years-582883), because the current-affairs ground is only in those two. 2) Split by stage in `d`: "'Undesirable purposes' likely to affect economic interest: MHA argument before the Delhi HC against CPR's challenge to the 2023-02 suspension (Tribune 2024-01-17). Transfer to other entities / non-designated accounts: MHA allegation, stage not specified (Tribune, citing officials). Publication of policy reports equated with current-affairs programming: a reason in the cancellation notice, per CPR's statement." Alternatively, set `from` to 2023 for the suspension-stage grounds. 3) Date: change "order dated 2024-01-10" (c063 label) to "notice received by CPR 2024-01-10 (CPR statement via Tribune 2024-01-20)"; the order date itself is unverified. 4) Mark "(s.3)" as editorial inference, e.g. "[our gloss: FCRA s.3(1) bar on news/current-affairs programmes; no source cites the section]". 5) Keep upgradeIf "order text or Delhi HC merits ruling" and killIf "order quashed on merits".

verdicts.dateTest: Written as a claim: MHA (Foreigners Division) suspended CARE India Solutions for Sustainable Development's FCRA registration for 180 days on or before 12 June 2023. The date in the claim is wrong. "2023-06-14" is only the dateline of The CSR Universe piece ("New Delhi, June 14, 2023", published 15 Jun 2023), and that piece just repeats earlier press reports ("As per the media reports..."). The original report is Times of India, published 2023-06-13 at 01:09 IST (https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/mha-suspends-fcra-licence-of-care-india-over-violations/articleshow/100947304.cms). In it, CARE confirms it had already received the notice. So the notice was served no later than 2023-06-12, and the order date itself is not public. MHA's actor window does overlap. The ₹28.3 crore receipt in 2012-13 falls under the 2010 Act, which was in force (UPA period). The registration had been renewed with effect from 2022-10-01 (ET, 2023-03-24), which means MHA renewed it knowing about the 2012-13 matter and suspended it about 3 months after announcing the renewal. Whether the suspension was later revoked or turned into a cancellation is not established. An OdishaBytes headline dated 2024-02-28, "CARE India Winds Up Operations After Suspension Of Foreign Funding Licence", suggests it was not revoked, but I could not open the article.
verdicts.identityTest: The FCRA registrant is not "CARE India" in general. It is CARE India Solutions for Sustainable Development (CISSD). CARE's statement to TOI says: "CARE India Solutions for Sustainable Development (CISSD) has received a notice from the ministry of home affairs, as per which CISSD's FCRA registration has been suspended temporarily for a period of 180 days." ET (2023-03-24) says: "Care India's FCRA license is in the name of Care India Solution for Sustainable Development." TOI refers to "the company's accounts", so the entity is a not-for-profit company, not a trust. The entity node ngo:care-india currently has ty="trust", al=[], and identity.fcra/cin both null. Its sub-label, "lost FCRA licence (2022–23) with ~4,000 job losses reported", is wrong on the facts: the licence was renewed from 2022-10-01 and suspended in June 2023. None of the opened sources supports the job-loss figure. The CSR Universe headline says "cancels", but its own text says the registration was suspended. The claim correctly says suspension.
verdicts.baseRate: Suspension of a large, active FCRA registrant is rare. About 16,000 associations are registered, and a Section 13 suspension of a major NGO with a recent renewal happens only a handful of times a year. So the property does discriminate in general. Within the specific group of NGOs the Income Tax department surveyed on 2022-09-07 (Oxfam India, CPR, CARE India), however, all 3 lost FCRA status: Oxfam's renewal was refused, CPR was suspended in 2023-02 and cancelled in 2024-01, and CARE was suspended in 2023-06. Within that batch the property does not discriminate, and it looks like a common pipeline from IT survey to FCRA action. On the symmetry control in the SPEC: suspensions for onward transfer or wrong-account receipts also happened under UPA (INSAF 2013, CPSC 2012–14). The file correctly lists CARE as a non-critic control, so this edge does not support a "critics targeted" reading by itself.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, and CARE was asked. TOI (2023-06-13) reports that CARE confirmed the notice "in an email response to TOI": "We are working on the clarifications for the government and are confident the temporary suspension will be revoked." CARE also said it "has always complied with regulations". CARE did not answer TOI's question about scaling down operations. The contra in c068 quotes CSR Universe paraphrases in quotation marks ("committed to serve the nation", "the suspension is temporary and will be revoked soon"). Those are not CARE's words. Replace them with the TOI quote. URL: https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/mha-suspends-fcra-licence-of-care-india-over-violations/articleshow/100947304.cms
verdicts.innocentReading: This looks like a routine regulatory action. The auditor's certificate recorded a Section 17(1) breach: ₹28.3 crore of foreign money received in 2012-13 in a domestic-funds account, with remittance certificates marked "business and management consultancy and public relations". The 2022-09 IT survey probably brought this back into view. A 180-day suspension pending inquiry is the standard first step under Section 13. On the other side, CARE had filed a condonation plea with MHA and provided for a ₹5.6 crore penalty in its accounts in 2018. That suggests a compoundable, decade-old lapse was used as the basis for a 2023 suspension, after a renewal granted despite the same lapse.
verdicts.reason: The core fact holds up. MHA suspended the FCRA registration of CARE India's registrant, CISSD, for 180 days in June 2023. TOI reported it from government sources, and CARE confirmed receiving the notice in an email to TOI. ET and The CSR Universe both repeat TOI, so there is one original report, not two independent ones. That fits "reported", not "documented". The claim does not survive as written, though. (1) The date 2023-06-14 is a secondary outlet's dateline; the notice was served no later than 2023-06-12. (2) The only cited source republishes TOI, and its headline wrongly says "cancels". (3) The parenthetical "₹377.5 crore foreign funding 2021-22" puts an unrelated figure next to the action. The sources link that figure only to the IT survey, not to any ground for suspension. (4) The record's d-field calls the ₹28.3 crore matter the "Stated grounds". The sources attribute it to the auditor's certificate, not to an MHA order. The d-field also leaves out the condonation plea and the ₹5.6 crore penalty provision. These are field fixes, not a refutation of the event.
