verdicts.dateTest: Written out, the claim is: MHA Foreigners Division took enforcement action against CARE India, on the ground of ₹28.3 cr received in a non-FCRA account, with the edge dated 2012 to 2013. MHA's action, a 180-day suspension of CARE India Solutions for Sustainable Development (CISSD), was served around 2023-06-13/14. Nothing MHA did happened in 2012 or 2013. The 2012-13 dates belong to CARE India's own receipt, not to MHA's action. So an `enforce` edge from MHA dated from=2012 to=2013 has the wrong chronology. The receipt happened under UPA and the 2010 Act. By 2018 it had been self-reported, a condonation plea had been filed with MHA, and a ₹5.6 cr penalty had been provided for in CARE India's accounts. The action came in 2023, 10 years after the receipt and 5 years after the condonation plea. The claim leaves out that sequence.
verdicts.identityTest: Pass on the entity. The CSR Universe names "CARE India Solutions for Sustainable Development (CISSD)" as the entity that received the MHA notice, and names CARE India as part of the CARE International Confederation. The FCRA registration number is not given in any source. The headline says "MHA cancels", but the article body describes a 180-day suspension, so the headline is wrong.
verdicts.baseRate: Not discriminating. The CSR Universe cites MHA data showing about 20,664 FCRA cancellations from 2011 to 2022 for diversion, misuse or non-filing, and about 6,677 suspensions from 2017 to 2021. Designated-account breaches under s.17 are among the most common FCRA findings. A self-disclosed breach from 10 years earlier that already had a pending condonation plea does not set CARE India apart. On the SPEC control: the breach happened under UPA and was not acted on then. Under NDA, action came only in 2023, after the 2022-09 IT survey that also covered Oxfam and CPR. Applying the same lens to UPA-era cases would count such a breach as a condonable, penalty-level matter, not a ground for suspension.
verdicts.denialFound: Partial response on record. CARE India (TOI, carried by indiacsr.in and myind.net): "We are working on the clarifications for the government and are confident the temporary suspension will be revoked." The CSR Universe says the NGO "believes that the suspension is temporary and will be revoked soon." This is already recorded as contra fcra-actions:c068. CARE India did not deny the 2012-13 receipt. It disclosed that receipt itself, through its auditor's certificate, and filed for condonation. No MHA statement of grounds was found. Final status (revoked or cancelled) is not verified.
verdicts.innocentReading: The ₹28.3 cr in 2012-13 is a disclosure in CARE India's own auditor's certificate, not a government allegation. The auditor flagged it as a s.17(1) breach, CARE India filed a condonation plea, and it provided a ₹5.6 cr penalty in its 2018 accounts. The news outlets reprinted the auditor's certificate next to the 2023 suspension story, and that placement is the only link between the two. MHA's notice may rest on something else entirely (for example, material from the 2022 IT survey, or FY2021-22 transfers). No source says what the notice's stated grounds were.
verdicts.reason: The source does not call this the ground for the suspension. The exact sentence in The CSR Universe (2023-06-15) is: "Earlier, in 2012-13, CARE India had received a foreign contribution to the tune of Rs 28.3 crore (without a permission from MHA) in a bank account that was meant for local funds. Furthermore, the foreign inward remittance certificate reflects that the NGO received these funds for business, management consultancy and public relations." The fuller TOI-derived text (indiacsr.in, myind.net) attributes this to "the auditor", not MHA, and adds that "a condonation plea was later filed with MHA and Rs 5.6 crore penalty provided for in the company's accounts in 2018." The claim is therefore a conjunction: a true self-disclosed 2012-13 breach plus a true 2023 suspension, joined into "MHA's ground", which no source states. The `alleged` tier is also wrong. No named party is making an allegation here; the fact comes from the subject's own auditor. The edge dates (2012 to 2013) attach MHA enforcement to a period when MHA took no action. As an MHA-to-CARE `enforce` edge, it duplicates c066 and adds an unsupported causal link. Kill the edge, and move the fact, with the condonation plea and the penalty, into c066 as disclosed background.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Kill fcra-actions:c067 as an `enforce` edge. It duplicates c066 (same s, t and a) with a causal link no source supports. 2) If the fact is kept, restate it as disclosed background inside c066.d. Suggested wording: "CARE India's auditor's certificate discloses ₹28.3 cr foreign contribution received in FY2012-13 into a local-funds account without MHA permission (FIRCs coded business/management consultancy/PR), a s.17(1) breach; condonation plea filed with MHA; ₹5.6 cr penalty provided in 2018 accounts. Sources do not state that the 2023 suspension notice cites this." 3) Fix c066.d, which currently says "Stated grounds (The CSR Universe)". Change it to "Background reported alongside the suspension; stated grounds of the MHA notice not published." 4) Add sources: indiacsr.in (https://indiacsr.in/care-india-india-govt-suspends-foreign-funding-licence-for-180-days/) and myind.net (https://myind.net/Home/viewArticle/suspension-of-care-indias-fcra-license-by-mha-for-violations). Both derive from TOI, so they are not independent of each other or of The CSR Universe, and c066 stays `reported`, not `documented`. 5) Note in c066 that the CSR Universe headline says "cancels" but its body describes a 180-day suspension. 6) If any residual claim keeps from/to, it must not use 2012 to 2013 on an MHA-sourced edge. 7) Remove c067's `upgradeIf` "Order text". The real upgrade test is MHA's suspension order or a Parliament answer that states the grounds.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: MHA (Foreigners Division, the FCRA regulator throughout) alleged that World Vision India did not comply with FCRA provisions, covering FY2012-13 to FY2020-21. The allegation was the stated basis of the November 2022 suspension (180 days, extended May 2023) and the January 2024 cancellation. MHA's role as regulator covers the whole period, so the dates overlap. The Hindu says suspension came "in November 2022, a year after it applied for the renewal", so from=2022-11 matches. One point to note: the 2012-13 to 2020-21 span comes from WVI's own financial statement, submitted to MHA on 2023-10-14. It is not taken from an MHA document. WVI registered under FCRA in 1986, so the whole span falls inside its registration. No date conflict.
verdicts.identityTest: The Hindu (Vijaita Singh, 2024-01-21) names "World Vision India (WVI)", registered under FCRA since 1986 and the Indian affiliate of US-based World Vision. The actor is "The Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)". The entity ngo:world-vision-india matches. The FCRA registration number is not given in the source; adding it from the FCRA portal would tighten identity. There is no conjunction problem: the claim states only the allegation and its period, and draws no inference from them.
verdicts.baseRate: Generic "violation / non-compliance with FCRA provisions" wording, with specifics not published, is the norm for MHA suspension and cancellation orders under both UPA and NDA. Probably ≥80% of reported cancellations carry it, so it does not discriminate. That is fine here because the claim records the stated ground and makes no targeting inference. The symmetry control (UPA 2011-14 cancellations) reads the same way: opaque, generic grounds.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes. The Hindu quotes WVI's financial statement: "the Society (WVI) has submitted its detailed responses to the MHA for all matters raised by them alleging non compliance by the Society with the provisions of FCRA relating to the periods from 2012-13 to 2020-21. The Society has also provided the required supporting documents for all the matters raised in the letters from the MHA." Christianity Today (2024-04-02) quotes WVI as "profoundly disappointed". https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/mha-cancels-fcra-registration-of-world-vision-india/article67760041.ece ; https://www.christianitytoday.com/2024/04/india-fcra-ngo-world-vision-foreign-funding-close/ . This is already recorded as contra c072. A search found no reported court challenge or quashing, so the killIf condition has not been met.
verdicts.innocentReading: This was a routine compliance review triggered by WVI's 2021 renewal application. MHA looks back over nine years of annual returns and queries accounting or utilisation irregularities, which is normal for a large recipient (₹170 crore in 2022). Recording the allegation says nothing about whether it is true. The orders were never published and never adjudicated, and WVI says it answered every query with documents.
verdicts.reason: The source supports the claim exactly. The Hindu, reachable at the original URL and at the mirror, says: "The Ministry initially suspended the registration for 180 days for alleged non-compliance with the FCRA's provisions". WVI's own statement fixes the period as "2012-13 to 2020-21". "Specifics not published" is accurate: no opened source gives the provisions. "Alleged" is the correct tier for an unadjudicated government notice, and the claim already has its required contra (c072). The actor is a ministry, not a family, religion or ethnicity. Nothing refutes it.
verdicts.corrections: 1. srcs: make the original The Hindu URL the primary source. It is reachable (HTTP 200): https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/mha-cancels-fcra-registration-of-world-vision-india/article67760041.ece (Vijaita Singh, 2024-01-21). Keep the hindutvawatch.org mirror only as a fallback, because the mirror is an advocacy site. 2. d: attribute the period, e.g. "period 2012-13 to 2020-21 per WVI's FY2022-23 financial statement (filed with MHA 2023-10-14) describing MHA's letters; MHA orders not published". The Hindu's "2022-33" is a typo for 2022-23; do not copy it. 3. Related fix, not this claim: fcra-actions:c018 lists "World Vision's 2012-13→2020-21 compliance queries" as an onward-transfer / non-designated-account ground. No opened source says what WVI's non-compliance was. Either remove World Vision from c018's list of onward-transfer grounds or mark its ground as unspecified.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: MHA (Foreigners Division) cancelled CASA's FCRA registration on a generic ground in 2024-04. The month holds. Business Standard, citing ET, says the ministry cancelled the five "on Tuesday", which is 2024-04-02. The Hindu (via the hindutvawatch mirror) has "sources said on April 3". The Wire (2024-04-04) says April 3. The actor was in office for the whole window, so there is no tenure problem. The cited CSR Universe piece is dated 2024-05-01 and places the five "close to a month back", which is consistent. `from` should be 2024-04-02, citing BS/ET and The Hindu.
verdicts.identityTest: The target is right: CSR Universe, The Hindu, The Wire, Business Standard and Swarajya all name "Church's Auxiliary for Social Action". None gives an FCRA registration number, and the entity's `identity.fcra` field is null. The failure is in which batch the ground belongs to, not in who CASA is. CSR Universe attaches the conversion ground to a DIFFERENT set of six NGOs cancelled in 2024-04/05. Those are Diocesan Society Church of North, Jesus and Mary Delhi Educational Society, Delhi Diocese Overseas Grant Fund, IEG, Sansam Foundation and Hemophilia Federation. Quote: "The Union Home Ministry has revoked the ... licenses of six prominent ... NGOs, citing alleged violations of FCRA regulations, misuse of foreign funds, and unauthorized activities related to religious conversions." For the five that include CASA, the same page says only: "cancelled the foreign funding licence of at least five NGOs over alleged violation of provisions of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010, and Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Rules, 2011 ... for allegedly utilising the foreign contributions for purposes other than their declared objectives." The claim therefore moves the six-NGO ground onto the five-NGO batch. It is a conjunction of two separate paragraphs.
verdicts.baseRate: The ground is not specific to CASA. Every one of the five cancelled together (CNI-SBSS, VHAI, IGSSS, CASA, EFI) shares it, which is 100% of the batch. That batch includes VHAI, a secular health body that works with WHO and ICMR, so a collective "religious conversion" line tells you nothing about CASA in particular. The CSR Universe control batch of six, which includes IEG, an academic institute, carries the same generic wording. Under the SPEC's UPA-vs-NDA control, the UPA also cited generic "FCRA provisions" formulae (2012-13 cancellations, INSAF), so the lens gives the same reading on both sides. What is known about CASA specifically comes to zero stated grounds.
verdicts.denialFound: This is wrong in the file. The claim text says "no CASA response recorded", and contra c075 says "No response recorded — asked/not asked unknown". Christianity Today (2024-04-02) does record a CASA response. Bishop Subodh C. Mondal, CASA's vice chairperson: "CASA's entire work is jeopardized. They had to terminate close to 350 staff in India ... Ninety percent of their work is affected by this. We will apply afresh for FCRA." (https://www.christianitytoday.com/2024/04/india-fcra-ngo-world-vision-foreign-funding-close/). It does not rebut any specific ground, and no specific ground was published to rebut. CT also quotes an unnamed Christian NGO leader: reasons for cancellation are "often unclear and sometimes even illegitimate". There is also a third-party op-ed rebuttal in Morung Express (2024-04-14), by Rev Rümatho Nyusou. The Wire (2024-04-04) does not say whether CASA was contacted.
verdicts.innocentReading: The ministry cancelled five registrations in one order sweep on compliance grounds: use of foreign contributions outside declared objectives, which the FCRA 2020 amendment tightened. The press, working from anonymous "sources" (ET, PTI/The Hindu), attached a composite list of grounds to the whole batch. The conversion element may apply to some members, or to none, but not necessarily to CASA. CASA's own reaction was to reapply, which fits a registration or compliance dispute as well as it fits targeting.
verdicts.reason: The only cited source (The CSR Universe, 2024-05-01) does not say what the claim says. It attaches "misuse of foreign funds, and unauthorized activities related to religious conversions" to a later batch of six NGOs that does not include CASA. For the April five that include CASA, it gives only FCRA/FCRR violations and use of funds "for purposes other than their declared objectives". The substance can be rescued from other outlets. Business Standard (2024-04-03) and Swarajya both cite an Economic Times report that the five were revoked over "alleged involvement in religious conversion, violations of foreign grants". But that ground is anonymously sourced, applies to the whole batch (including the secular VHAI), and is not specific to CASA. Separately, "no CASA response recorded" is false: CT quotes CASA's vice chairperson. The claim fails as written. It can survive only as `alleged`, re-sourced to ET/BS/The Hindu, reworded as a collective ground, and paired with a contra that records the Mondal statement.
verdicts.corrections: (1) c074 `srcs`: replace or augment the CSR Universe link with Business Standard 2024-04-03 (https://www.business-standard.com/india-news/here-is-why-modi-govt-cancelled-the-fcra-licences-of-five-prominent-ngos-124040300154_1.html, citing ET) and The Hindu 2024-04-03 via mirror (https://www.hindutvawatch.org/fcra-registration-of-five-ngos-cancelled-by-mha-for-violation-of-laws-the-hindu/). Keep CSR Universe only for the "purposes other than their declared objectives" wording. (2) c074 `lab`: "Alleged ground, attributed by unnamed MHA sources to all five NGOs cancelled 2024-04-02 (CNI-SBSS, VHAI, IGSSS, CASA, EFI): violation of FCRA 2010/FCRR 2011; use of foreign contributions outside declared objectives (The Hindu/PTI); 'religious conversion' (ET via Business Standard). No CASA-specific ground published." (3) c074 `from`: "2024-04-02". (4) c075 `d`: replace the no-response wording with the CT quote from Bishop Subodh C. Mondal, CASA vice chairperson ("CASA's entire work is jeopardized ... terminate close to 350 staff ... We will apply afresh for FCRA"), noting that it does not address any specific ground. Tier: reported. Src: the CT URL. (5) c073 `d`: the quoted ground "alleged violations of FCRA regulations, misuse of foreign funds, and unauthorized activities related to religious conversions" is CSR Universe's wording for the six-NGO batch, not the five. Re-attribute it or fix it the same way. (6) The narrative "Christian associations are the real target" says "the generic 2024 ground cites 'religious conversions'". Specify which batch, and cite ET/BS for the April five. (7) Remove "(no CASA response recorded)" from the claim text.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: MHA Foreigners Division refused or ended EFI's FCRA registration on the stated ground of prejudice to "public interest" and "harmony between religious... groups", dated "2023". Christianity Today (2024-04-02) says: "Last year, the Evangelical Fellowship of India (EFI) and the Church of North India lost their licenses." That supports 2023. The CSR Universe (2024-05-01), The Wire, and the Economic Times (via The Wire and Business Standard, 2024-04-03) all report EFI among five NGOs whose licences were cancelled or not renewed in the news cycle around 3 April 2024. The date is unresolved. "from":"2023" rests on one outlet's "last year" and conflicts with three reports placing it in 2024-04. The actor is MHA in either year, so there is no tenure problem.
verdicts.identityTest: The organisation is the Evangelical Fellowship of India. CT calls it "the umbrella body for evangelicals in India", and Business Standard abbreviates it "EFOI". General secretary Vijayesh Lal is named in both CT and ET/The Wire. No FCRA registration number appears in any source, so the match rests on the name plus a named office-bearer, which is adequate. One problem: the claim's `d` calls this a "Cancellation", but CT says "was refused renewal", and ET/The Wire says "their renewal application of FCRA licence was denied." A renewal refusal under s.16 (applying the s.12(4) conditions) is legally different from a cancellation under s.14. The CSR Universe calls it cancelled "as per the sources", which is looser.
verdicts.baseRate: The quoted wording is the statutory text of FCRA s.12(4)(f) ("not likely to affect prejudicially... public interest... harmony between religious, racial, social, linguistic, regional groups, castes or communities"). It appears routinely in refusal orders as a template ground, so the phrase alone does not show targeting. The symmetry control holds: the UPA-era 2012 Kudankulam-linked actions also used "public interest" grounds against NGOs. The claim records only what ground was stated and asserts no pattern, so the base rate does not refute it. It does limit any inference drawn from the wording.
verdicts.denialFound: EFI responded. CT quotes Vijayesh Lal: "it came as a surprise that the government would categorize us in this way... perhaps we were punished for speaking about religious freedom for Christians... but I hope that is not the case." ET/The Wire quotes Lal: "It is very surprising that the umbrella and representative body of Evangelical Christians in India... is identified as a body that can 'prejudicially' affect inter-religious, or social harmony." This is already recorded as contra c077. The government side, per ET citing officials in Business Standard, says EFI's licence was revoked "for violating FCRA rules". MHA said the actions followed "due process of law". Sources: https://m.thewire.in/article/government/mha-cancels-fcra-licence-of-3-major-church-related-charity-organisations-2-others and https://www.business-standard.com/india-news/here-is-why-modi-govt-cancelled-the-fcra-licences-of-five-prominent-ngos-124040300154_1.html
verdicts.innocentReading: The refusal order used the standard s.12(4)(f) template grounds that MHA applies to many renewal refusals. The substantive reason may have been compliance or rule violations, as ET's officials said, rather than a specific finding about EFI's interfaith work.
verdicts.reason: The sources support what the claim asserts, which is only that this was the government's stated ground. CT quotes it verbatim: "was refused renewal for the stated reason that it would affect 'prejudicially' the 'public interest' and 'harmony between religious, racial, social, linguistic, regional groups, castes or communities.'" ET/The Wire independently confirm it through EFI's own general secretary, who quotes the "'prejudicially' affect inter-religious, or social harmony" wording. The ground is an unadjudicated government assertion and the claim carries a contra (c077), so the alleged tier is correct. The fact that this ground was stated could be tiered reported, since two outlets carry it. The claim survives, but three field errors need fixing: the action type (renewal refused, not cancellation), the 2023 date resting on a single "last year", and the missing ET/Wire corroboration.
verdicts.corrections: 1. `d`: replace "Cancellation dated 2023 by CT" with "Renewal refused (CT: 'refused renewal'; ET/Wire: 'renewal application... was denied'); CT dates it 'last year' (2023); CSR Universe, ET and The Wire report it in the 2024-04-03 batch of five. Date unresolved." 2. `from`: set to null, or "2023/2024-04" flagged as unresolved; do not assert 2023. 3. `srcs`: add The Wire / Economic Times 2024-04 (https://m.thewire.in/article/government/mha-cancels-fcra-licence-of-3-major-church-related-charity-organisations-2-others), which carries Lal's confirmation of the ground wording. 4. `d`: note that the wording is the statutory s.12(4)(f) text, and add the officials' parallel ground "violating FCRA rules" (ET via Business Standard 2024-04-03). 5. The CSR Universe source does not state this ground, only "utilising the foreign contributions for purposes other than their declared objectives" for the batch. Label it as supporting the event only, not the ground. 6. `upgradeIf`: keep "Order text with date (s.16 refusal order)".

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: MHA Foreigners Division (FCRA Wing) suspended INSAF's FCRA registration on 2013-04-30 and later alleged onward transfer of funds for protests. That falls within the UPA government, under Home Minister Shinde (2012-07-31 to 2014-05-26), so the "UPA, 2013" label holds. One caveat: the ground was not in the 30.04.2013 order. The court recorded it from the government's counter-affidavit in W.P.(C) 4982/2013, filed around Aug 2013 and decided 19.09.2013, and held that the order recorded no reasons. So the allegation dates to the counter-affidavit (Aug–Sep 2013), not to 2013-04-30. The field from=2013-04-30 is the suspension date, not the date of the allegation.
verdicts.identityTest: Pass. The judgment names the petitioner as "INDIAN SOCIAL ACTION FORUM (INSAF)", a society registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860. The order was "issued by the Director to the Government of India, Ministry of Home Affairs, Foreigners Division (FCRA Wing)", which matches s=ngo:mha-foreigners-division. The FCRA registration number is not in the judgment; the entity's identity.fcra is null and should be filled if found. The entity type is "trust" but the court says society; this is a minor correction.
verdicts.baseRate: Onward transfer of funds and protest or "public interest" grounds are common across MHA FCRA actions in this file under both UPA and NDA (CPR, Environics, Oxfam, Lawyers Collective). Having this ground is not distinctive in itself. The claim does not assert discrimination, though. It records one government allegation, and it is itself the UPA-side symmetry control required by the SPEC. Across the 6 decided court challenges in the file, 4 went for the association, and this is one of them.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, and it is in the same source. Delhi HC judgment, para 2: "In its rejoinder, the petitioner has denied having transferred funds to any non-FCRA registered NGOs." (https://indiankanoon.org/doc/112525478/). The denial is partial: it covers only non-FCRA recipients and does not address transfers to FCRA-registered NGOs or the protest use. The court made no finding on the truth of either side. In later rounds, INSAF's 2016–21 renewal was refused by a one-line email, which the Delhi HC reviewed, and in INSAF v UoI (SC, 2020) the Supreme Court read down the "political nature" provisions. Neither ruling adjudicated this 2013 ground.
verdicts.innocentReading: INSAF is a network forum. Passing grants to member groups is how a network works, and before the 2020 amendment, transfers to FCRA-registered partners were lawful. The government put forward the "protests against welfare policies" description only after the fact, in a counter-affidavit, to justify an order that recorded no reasons. The court said such reasons "cannot be given, by way of extraneous evidence at a later stage", which fits a post-hoc rationale rather than a documented finding.
verdicts.reason: The source says what the claim says. Para 2 reads: "reports were received by the Government which revealed that foreign funds received by the petitioner were being transferred to other FCRA registered as well as non-FCRA registered NGOs, which were utilizing the said fund for organizing the protest, etc. against the welfare policies of the Government". The court quashed the suspension on procedural grounds: it was premature and unreasoned, and fresh action was not barred. The court did not rule on the allegation. A government assertion that has not been adjudicated is exactly the "alleged" tier, and the claim carries a contra (c081). No family, religion or ethnicity is framed as the actor. The claim survives with wording and field corrections.
verdicts.corrections: 1) c080 text/lab: replace "Alleged ground" with "Ground asserted in MHA's counter-affidavit (Delhi HC W.P.(C) 4982/2013), not stated in the 30.04.2013 order". Add to d: "The court held the order recorded no reasons and that reasons 'cannot be given, by way of extraneous evidence at a later stage'." 2) c080 from: the allegation dates to the 2013 counter-affidavit (Aug–Sep 2013), not 2013-04-30. Either note this in d or set from to 2013-09-19 as the date it was recorded. 3) c081 is factually wrong where it says "no substantive denial text is quoted". Replace with the quoted rejoinder: "the petitioner has denied having transferred funds to any non-FCRA registered NGOs", and note that the denial is partial and does not address FCRA-registered transfers or protest use. Tier for c081 can be documented, since the source is a court record. 4) ngo:insaf entity: ty "trust" should be society (registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 per the judgment), and identity.fcra should be filled if findable. 5) Add later history to the entity or narratives: renewal refused for 2016–21, reviewed by the Delhi HC; INSAF v UoI, SC 2020, read down the s.5 "political nature" provisions. killIf "None recorded" is acceptable, since no later finding on this ground was found.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: MHA (Foreigners Division) suspended CPSC's FCRA registration three times, 2012 to 2014, for about 18 months in total, and the Delhi HC ruled for CPSC in March 2014. The UPA government held office until 26 May 2014, so the window falls inside it: roughly 18 months from mid-2012 ends around early 2014, and the HC ruling in March 2014 also came before the change of government. The source does not give the exact start date. FIDH says only "between 2012 and 2014", and it mentions July 2012 only for the alleged cash withdrawal "after the suspension of its FCRA registration in 2012 ... in July 2012". The '2012-07-16' in `from` and in the text is not in the cited source, and no other source was found for it. The "Chidambaram → Shinde" attribution in `d` comes from that unsourced date (Shinde became Home Minister on 31 Jul 2012). It is our inference and the source does not say it. FIDH is also sloppy with dates in this same piece: "next hearing ... January 24, 2002", and it gives the renewal refusal as "January 29, 2016", while the Delhi HC order of 28.11.2025 in W.P.(C) 10527/2016 gives the order date as 29.10.2016.
verdicts.identityTest: Pass. FIDH names "Centre for Promotion of Social Concerns (CPSC) and its program unit, People's Watch", based in Madurai. The Delhi HC order in W.P.(C) 10527/2016 (indiankanoon.org/doc/150583269/) confirms CPSC is a charitable trust registered on 17.11.1981 and under FCRA 1976 on 29.08.1985, which fits the node. The FCRA registration number is still null in the entity record. The subject node is ngo:peoples-watch, but the registrant is CPSC; the alias covers this. The actor ngo:mha-foreigners-division is right for FCRA suspensions under s.13, though FIDH does not name the division.
verdicts.baseRate: Not discriminating on its own. In 2012–13 a suspension under s.13 FCRA (180 days, pending inquiry) was a common step under UPA: the Kudankulam-linked actions in 2012 and INSAF's suspension, which the Delhi HC quashed on 2013-09-19 (c080/c081). Being suspended and then winning in the HC was a pattern shared by several rights groups in that period. The edge matters as the cross-era control named in SPEC (UPA action against a government-critical association). It carries no signal about targeting by one party. Symmetry holds: the same lens applied to NDA actions after 2016 (non-renewal, CBI FIR) reads the same way, and the record already treats People's Watch as the both-governments control.
verdicts.denialFound: MHA: none found, and it is not known whether MHA was asked. The only statement of MHA's grounds is secondhand in FIDH, describing its 2014 complaint: unaccounted withdrawals of Rs 2.8 million in July 2012 and Rs 16.9 million over 2008–12, and Rs 4.5 million withdrawn on 240 occasions in 2011–13. CPSC: contested the suspensions in the Delhi HC and, per FIDH, won in March 2014. The 2014 judgment was not found on Indian Kanoon, which lists only CPSC orders from 2024–25.
verdicts.innocentReading: MHA inspected CPSC's accounts in 2012, found what it treated as cash withdrawals and fund transfers it could not account for, and suspended the registration under s.13 pending inquiry. It re-suspended when the inquiry ran past 180 days, and the court then ended the practice. That is routine regulatory process, not retaliation. The claim as worded implies no motive, so this reading fits it.
verdicts.reason: The substance is confirmed word for word by the only cited source. FIDH 2022-01-14: "between 2012 and 2014, CPSC had its FCRA registration suspended on three occasions, for a total period of 18 months, until the Delhi High Court ruled in CPSC's favor in March 2014 following a writ petition by CPSC, which had challenged the suspension of its FCRA registration." The date test passes because everything falls within UPA's term. The claim is not refuted, but it adds a precise start date (2012-07-16) and a minister handover (Chidambaram → Shinde) that the source does not contain. Tier stays 'reported', not 'documented': FIDH is an advocacy body aligned with CPSC, the sentence is unsourced ("The Observatory recalls"), the source has date errors elsewhere, and the 2014 HC judgment has not been retrieved. A structural problem: c082 is marked supersededBy c083, but c083 is a different edge (Delhi HC → MHA, covering the ruling only). If the supersession stands, the graph loses the MHA → CPSC suspension edge, which is the UPA-era side of the control SPEC requires.
verdicts.corrections: 1) `from`: change '2012-07-16' to '2012'. If month precision is wanted, cite a source other than FIDH that gives the date. Also remove the '2012-07-16 first CPSC suspension' wording from the minister entity's `d` (fcra-actions.json line ~1539). 2) `d`: delete 'UPA era (Chidambaram → Shinde)' or relabel it as our inference; keep 'UPA era'. 3) Text/lab: 'Three suspensions of CPSC FCRA registration between 2012 and 2014 (UPA), totalling 18 months (FIDH); Delhi HC ruled for CPSC 2014-03'. 4) Set `to` to '2014-03' as the end of the suspension series, and note that FIDH does not give the date the last suspension ended. 5) Set `supersededBy` to null. c083 (HC → MHA) is a separate edge and cannot replace the MHA → CPSC enforcement edge. Keep both and link them. 6) Add a contra per the wording rule: CPSC's HC challenge that succeeded in 2014-03 (FIDH), plus 'MHA grounds: 2014 complaint alleging unaccounted withdrawals (as described by FIDH); no MHA statement recorded, asked/not asked unknown'. 7) upgradeIf: the Delhi HC judgment of 2014-03 on CPSC's writ against the suspension. 8) Sibling fixes found along the way: in c084, the HC order of 28.11.2025 gives the refusal date as 29.10.2016 (FIDH says 29 Jan 2016). The same order (Amit Sharma J., W.P.(C) 10527/2016, https://indiankanoon.org/doc/150583269/) set aside the 2016 refusal and allowed CPSC to apply afresh, with a decision due within 90 days. That meets c085's killIf ('HC directs renewal'), and c084's 'case pending' is out of date.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: MHA (FCRA wing, then under the Foreigners Division) refused CPSC/People's Watch's FCRA renewal in 2016. Rajnath Singh was Home Minister from 2014-05-26 to 2019-05-30, so the year falls in his tenure. The cited source, FIDH's 2022 appeal, says "rejected by the Ministry of Home Affairs on January 29, 2016". Two contemporaneous accounts give a different date. FIDH's own appeal of 2016-11-11 (https://www.fidh.org/en/issues/human-rights-defenders/india-refusal-to-renew-the-licence-of-the-centre-for-promotion-of) says "on October 29, 2016, the Ministry of Home Affairs announced on its website its refusal to renew the registration", with the licence expiring on October 31. HRW's release of 2016-11-08 and Front Line Defenders also say 29 October 2016. The 2022 FIDH text has other date typos too ("January 24, 2002" and "Geneva-Paris, January 14, 2021"). So the right date is 2016-10-29, not January. The claim only says "2016", so it survives, but the date field needs fixing.
verdicts.identityTest: The target is right. The Centre for Promotion of Social Concerns (a Madurai charitable trust) is the FCRA registrant, and People's Watch is its programme unit, as FIDH, FLD and HRW all say. The node ngo:peoples-watch carries CPSC as an alias, which is acceptable, but the registrant is CPSC. No FCRA registration number is recorded; it should be added if found. On the actor: every source names the "Ministry of Home Affairs". Assigning the act to the Foreigners Division is our own inference (the FCRA wing sat in that division in 2016). It is defensible but no source states it.
verdicts.baseRate: The property is discriminating. In the same period (announced 2016-11-03), MHA cancelled 11,319 licences for not applying to renew. Refusals "on the basis of field agency report" were a small cluster: about 25 NGOs, reported as refused for "anti-national" activities (Tribune; HRW 2016-11-08). Hazards Centre got the identical one-line refusal on 2016-10-28 and INSAF got a no-reason refusal on 2016-10-21. That is well under 1% of 2016 FCRA actions, far below the 80% non-discrimination line. Symmetry control (UPA vs NDA): the same organisation was suspended three times under the UPA in 2012–14 (c082), so the lens gives the same reading across governments. The file already presents CPSC as the cross-era control.
verdicts.denialFound: The government's position is on record, and it was asked, in court. At the Delhi HC hearing on 2016-11-07, Central Government Standing Counsel Anil Soni "told the court that the Government was exempted from providing reasons for refusing to renew FCRA registrations, adding that the decision was based on 'inputs of intelligence agencies'" (FIDH 2016-11-11; Front Line Defenders https://www.frontlinedefenders.org/en/case/refusal-renew-registration-centre-promotion-social-concerns). The later written reply cited Tiphagne's engagement with embassies and UN Special Rapporteurs (FIDH 2022). We have no denial of the refusal itself; the government confirms it and gives intelligence inputs as the basis. CPSC's side is its Delhi HC petition of 2016-11-03 and its NHRC petition of 2016-11-01.
verdicts.innocentReading: This was a routine five-year renewal decision, taken on a field-agency (IB/police) verification report, of the kind MHA made for dozens of applicants in October 2016 under s.12/16 FCRA 2010. It also came against an organisation that already had an open 2014 MHA complaint about how it used funds in 2008–14 (the basis of the later CBI FIR). A refusal on an adverse verification report is lawful in form. The edge records only that the action happened, which is undisputed. Whether the grounds were legitimate belongs in c085 (alleged), not here.
verdicts.reason: Not refuted, because the core fact is confirmed by the government's own statements in court and by several sources. MHA refused to renew CPSC's FCRA registration in 2016, citing field reports, and the government confirmed the refusal in the Delhi HC. The cited FIDH 2022 page says it: "CPSC's application for FCRA renewal was however rejected by the Ministry of Home Affairs on January 29, 2016 'on the basis of field reports'". FIDH 2016, HRW 2016 and Front Line Defenders all confirm a 2016 refusal on a field-agency report. The source check is only partial for two reasons. First, the cited source's day and month (January 29) are wrong; contemporaneous records give October 29, 2016. Second, the quoted words in the claim paraphrase FIDH 2022 rather than the MHA wording, which was "On the basis of field agency report, the competent authority has decided to refuse your application for renewal". Reported is the right tier. The primary record (the MHA FCRA portal notice and the Delhi HC filings) has not been opened. FIDH, HRW and FLD are advocacy bodies that co-sign joint statements, so they are not clearly independent of each other, and an upgrade to documented is not justified.

2. lab: replace the paraphrase 'on the basis of field reports' with the MHA wording as quoted: "On the basis of field agency report, the competent authority has decided to refuse your application for renewal".
3. d: the CPSC challenge was filed in the Delhi HC on 2016-11-03 (FLD), not in "October 2016". At the 2016-11-07 hearing, CGSC Anil Soni said the decision rested on "inputs of intelligence agencies" and that the government need not give reasons. Record this as the government's stated position.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim bundles two MHA allegations that fall in different time windows. (1) Ground A: MHA's written reply in the Delhi HC challenge to the 2016 non-renewal. The challenge was filed around Oct/Nov 2016, so the reply is late 2016 or after, during the NDA government (Rajnath Singh was Home Minister from 2014-05-26). The dates of the refusal itself conflict between sources. FIDH says "rejected by the Ministry of Home Affairs on January 29, 2016". Front Line Defenders says "On 29 October 2016, the Ministry of Home Affairs denied the renewal ... which was due to expire on 31 October 2016". FIDH also has an obvious typo ("next hearing ... January 24, 2002"), which lowers confidence in its January date. (2) Ground B: FCRA violations in 2008–2014. This rests on an MHA complaint dated 2014-07-22 from A.K. Sinha, then MHA Director (Leaflet/NewsClick). That complaint drew on inspections in May 2012 (UPA) and 2014. CBI registered the FIR on 2022-01-06 and searched on 2022-01-08. The claim's `from: 2016` is therefore wrong for Ground B. MHA made that allegation in July 2014 (NDA, about two months into the Rajnath Singh tenure), based on a May 2012 UPA-era inspection. The actor (MHA) does overlap each date, so the claim is not refuted on dates, only mis-dated.
verdicts.identityTest: This passes. The registration holder is the Centre for Promotion of Social Concerns (CPSC), a Madurai charitable trust. People's Watch is its programme unit, and its Executive Director is Henri Tiphagne. The node `ngo:peoples-watch` carries the CPSC alias, and FIDH names "CPSC and its program unit, People's Watch" in both the complaint and the refusal. The accusing party for Ground B is correctly MHA: the complaint was by A.K. Sinha, Director (MU&I), MHA, per Deccan Herald 2022-01-09. However, the FIR itself is a CBI act (EOB Chennai), not an MHA Foreigners Division act. Ground A concerns Tiphagne personally, not the trust's accounts. No FCRA registration number appears in any source opened.
verdicts.baseRate: The 2016 non-renewal wave was not discriminating: over 11,000 registrations lapsed in 2016, mostly because no application was filed (FLD). Refusing an organisation that did apply, with a stated ground that reaches engagement with UN Special Rapporteurs and embassies, is rare. In this file only CPSC has that ground, and Oxfam 2022, with its lobbying-foreign-governments FIR, is the nearest analogue. A CBI FIR following an MHA FCRA complaint is also rare: in this file only Oxfam, Environics and CPSC have one. The property is therefore discriminating, well under 80%. Symmetry control from the SPEC (UPA vs NDA): the same organisation was suspended three times under the UPA (2012–14, from the May 2012 inspection), so the accounting track began under the UPA. The embassies/UN ground is NDA-era only. The file already records both (c082, c084).
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, and the linked contra c086 wrongly says "No response recorded — asked/not asked unknown". (1) Henri Tiphagne, via Twitter, reported by Deccan Herald 2022-01-09 (https://www.deccanherald.com/india/cbi-registers-case-against-cpsc-ngo-alleges-witch-hunt-1069542.html): he termed the FIR a "witch-hunt" and wrote, "CPSC received funds in 2015 & 2016 till October. FCRA suspension orders issued by the MHA in 2017 (was) withdrawn. FCRA Account frozen now for more than 2,500 days. If this is not vindictiveness, what is it? We are willing to still cooperate because of our trust in the rule of law. But can anyone explain why an FIR u/s 120B & 420 IPC? What is the conspiracy? Cheating?" (2) Tiphagne's statement on the FIR, dated 2022-01-09, is on peopleswatch.org (http://www.peopleswatch.org/media/peoples-watch-media/executive-director-henri-tiphagnes-statement-cbis-fir-against-peoples; the page holds only a video). (3) CPSC formally contested the refusal by filing a Delhi HC writ in Nov 2016 (FLD: https://www.frontlinedefenders.org/en/case/refusal-renew-registration-centre-promotion-social-concerns; FIDH). (4) Tiphagne's first-person account appeared in The Leaflet on 2026-04-24 (https://theleaflet.in/due-process/i-did-not-know-that-this-visit-would-inaugurate-the-longest-battle-of-my-life-henri-tiphagne-on-14-years-of-fighting-the-fcra-regime): "Perhaps our advocacy at the United Nations was what unsettled the Union government." He was not asked by us; he responded publicly.
verdicts.innocentReading: MHA inspected CPSC in May 2012 and again in 2014. It reported cash withdrawals that did not match vouchers: Rs 28 lakh in July 2012 after the suspension, and Rs 1.69 crore over 2008–12. It also reported People's Watch acting as a separate entity from the registered trust, onward transfers that were under-declared, and use of funds for other purposes. On this reading, the non-renewal rests on these accounting findings and on intelligence inputs. In court, government counsel said the refusal was "based on inputs from intelligence agencies" and that the government was "exempted from giving reasons" (FLD). On that view, the embassies/UN-engagement line is FIDH's paraphrase of one passage of a pleading that has not been opened, not the operative ground. The formal order said only "on the basis of field reports". None of this is adjudicated. The FIR is at the pre-chargesheet stage, and the HC case was pending as of 2022-01.
verdicts.reason: The one cited source (FIDH Observatory urgent appeal, 2022-01-14) says what the claim says. Quote 1: "in its written response, the Ministry of Home Affairs mentioned People's Watch Executive Director Henri Tiphagne's engagement with embassies and United Nations Special Rapporteurs as the reason for denying the renewal of CPSC's registration under the FCRA". Quote 2: the FIR "is based on a complaint filed in 2014 by the Ministry of Home Affairs, alleging violations of foreign contribution regulations by CPSC and its program unit, People's Watch, by receiving and utilising foreign funding between 2008 and 2014." Both are unadjudicated assertions by a named state party, so `alleged` is the right tier and the claim survives. The defects are fixable, not fatal. (a) The conjunction runs two different actions together under `from: 2016`: a 2016 refusal ground and a 2014 complaint that led to a 2022 CBI FIR. Read together, they suggest the refusal rested on the 2008–14 violations, which no source says. (b) Ground A reaches us only through FIDH, which advocates for CPSC, paraphrasing an MHA pleading that nobody has opened. The formal order and government counsel gave "field reports" and "intelligence inputs" instead. (c) The contra c086 is wrong: a public denial exists.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: Union Home Ministry cancelled Navsarjan Trust's FCRA registration on 2016-12-15. Scroll (Aarefa Johari, 2017-01-12) says: "its license to receive foreign funding was renewed as recently as August 3, 2016. But on December 15 last year, the Union Home Ministry issued an order in 'public interest', cancelling Navsarjan's registration under the Act". 2016-08-03 to 2016-12-15 is 4 months 12 days, so "four months after renewal" holds. The actor's window is the MHA under Home Minister Rajnath Singh (2014-05-26 to 2019-05-30, c003), which covers the date. The article was published 28 days after the order, so it is contemporaneous.
verdicts.identityTest: The target is right. Scroll names "Navsarjan Trust", founded 1989, "Gujarat's oldest Dalit rights trust", founder and managing trustee Martin Macwan. That matches entity ngo:navsarjan-trust. The record has no FCRA registration number (identity.fcra is null), so the match rests on name, state and founder, which is adequate here because no other trust shares the name. On the actor, Scroll says "the Union Home Ministry", not the Foreigners Division. In 2016 FCRA sat in the MHA's Foreigners Division (FCRA wing), so the attribution is reasonable, but the source never names the division.
verdicts.baseRate: This does not discriminate as a bare fact. Tens of thousands of FCRA registrations were cancelled in 2015–17, mostly for not filing returns, so being cancelled is common among registered associations. The discriminating features are the content-based ground (s.14 "harmony" / public interest, quoted in c088) and the fact that it came 4 months after a renewal. Scroll places it in a December 2016 batch cancelled on "undesirable" grounds: Anhad, Marwar Muslim Education and Welfare Society, Rural Development Research Centre, and Institute of Public Health. A cancellation shortly after renewal is also not unique. The edge only states the enforcement fact and implies no motive, so the base rate does not refute it. Motive belongs in c088/c099 and the narrative, which already carry the UPA control (INSAF 2013, CPSC 2012–14, Kudankulam 2012).
verdicts.denialFound: The MHA's stated position is the order itself. Scroll quotes its ground: "undesirable activities aimed to affect prejudicially harmony between religious, racial, social, linguistic, regional groups, castes or communities", and notes the order "did not offer any further explanation or cite examples". The affected party's response is on the record (c089). Macwan says "the government's accusation that we are disrupting harmony between castes is baseless" and planned a Gujarat High Court challenge. I found no further MHA statement. Scroll does not say it asked the MHA for comment. I could not check the outcome of any Gujarat HC petition (killIf: order quashed) because the web search budget was exhausted and fallback searches returned nothing I could parse.
verdicts.innocentReading: A regulator used its statutory s.14 power on a public-interest ground against one of several December 2016 targets. A renewal in August does not stop later cancellation if intelligence or inspection inputs arrive afterwards. This reading fits the edge equally well, because the edge asserts only that the cancellation happened and when, not why. The Una-protest timing link is Macwan's belief, reported as such, and it is correctly confined to c088/c089.
verdicts.reason: The single cited source, opened and quoted, states the actor (Union Home Ministry), the act (cancellation of FCRA registration), the date (15 December 2016) and the prior renewal (3 August 2016). The claim's arithmetic ("four months") is correct, and the claim does not combine separate facts to imply a motive. It is one named-byline outlet quoting the order, which meets the "reported" bar exactly. HRW (2022-01-18) independently lists "Navsarjan Trust" among groups whose FCRA licence was revoked, suspended or not renewed since 2016. That corroborates the fact of the cancellation but not the date, so it does not lift the claim to documented. The family/religion/ethnicity-as-actor test does not apply: the actor is a ministry.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Add to d or lab that the source names the actor as "Union Home Ministry". Keep s = ngo:mha-foreigners-division only with a note that the FCRA wing sat in that division in 2016, or retarget s to min:ministry-of-home-affairs. 2) Add the order's framing: issued "in public interest" under the Act, one of a December 2016 batch (Anhad, Marwar Muslim Education and Welfare Society, Rural Development Research Centre, Institute of Public Health). 3) Sharpen d: Scroll says "almost all of Navsarjan's 92 employees" lost jobs and "80 of Navsarjan's staff members" were laid off a week after the order, with salaries paid to 31 March. 4) Add HRW 2022-01-18 (https://www.hrw.org/news/2022/01/18/india-should-stop-using-abusive-foreign-funding-law) as a secondary source for the fact of the cancellation only. 5) Keep upgradeIf as "MHA FCRA portal cancelled-list entry with registration number, or Gujarat HC record". Fill identity.fcra once the registration number is found.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: MHA (FCRA wing, Foreigners Division) cancelled Navsarjan Trust's FCRA registration by an order dated 2016-12-15, stating the "harmony" ground. The actor is the office, not a person, so the tenure question is simply whether the ministry held the power at that date, and it did. Rajnath Singh was Home Minister from 2014-05-26 to 2019-05-30, which covers the date, although the edge rightly does not name him. Scroll (Aarefa Johari, 2017-01-12) says: "on December 15 last year, the Union Home Ministry issued an order in 'public interest', cancelling Navsarjan's registration under the Act on the grounds that the trust was involved in 'undesirable activities aimed to affect prejudicially harmony between religious, racial, social, linguistic, regional groups, castes or communities'". The renewal date of 2016-08-03 is also confirmed. The note in `d` that this came "five months after Una" is arithmetically right: the Una assault was 2016-07-11, a little over five months before 2016-12-15. But that link is Macwan's causal inference, which the article attributes to him ("Macwan believes that the crackdown is connected..."). It is not the record's own date test and should be attributed to him.
verdicts.identityTest: Passes. The entity is Navsarjan Trust, Ahmedabad: founded 1989, managing trustee Martin Macwan, and the same trust the source names. There is no FCRA registration number in the record (identity.fcra is null), so the match rests on name, founder and place. That is unambiguous here, but the FCRA number would make it stronger. One caution: Indian Kanoon's "Navsarjan Trust vs State of Gujarat" (Gujarat HC WP(PIL) 97/2016, order of 2019-10-22) is an unrelated PIL, not an FCRA challenge, and must not be attached to this claim. The source says "Union Home Ministry", and mapping that to ngo:mha-foreigners-division (which administers FCRA) is acceptable.
verdicts.baseRate: The ground does not single out Navsarjan. The "prejudicially affect harmony between religious, racial, social, linguistic, regional groups, castes or communities" wording is the statute's own clause (FCRA 2010 s.12(4), applied through s.14 cancellation). MHA used it as standard wording across the same December 2016 batch of about seven NGOs "following alleged adverse intelligence reports" (DeshGujarat 2016-12-24; Scroll lists Anhad, the Marwar Muslim Education and Welfare Society, the Rural Development Research Centre and the Institute of Public Health). The fleet SPEC control (UPA, 2011–14) used grounds of the same form, e.g. the 2012 Kudankulam-linked cancellations. So the wording tells us nothing about motive. What makes the case notable is the four months between renewal and cancellation, and the timing after Una, not the ground itself.
verdicts.denialFound: Navsarjan's side: Scroll 2017-01-12 reports that Macwan ties the action to the post-Una Dalit mobilisation and planned a High Court challenge. Natubhai Parmar asks "How can the government consider this anti-national or even undesirable?" (https://scroll.in/article/826311/...). Counterview 2016-12 carries Macwan attributing it to the BJP's loss of Dalit votes after Una (https://www.counterview.net/2016/12/bjp-dalit-electoral-erosion-following.html). The government's side is missing from the record: DeshGujarat 2016-12-24 reports "According to the MHA officials quoted in a report, Navsarjan Trust was under the scanner following adverse field reports from the intelligence agencies. The FCRA licence, however, was 'inadvertently' renewed in August this year, before it was cancelled on December 15 when the error was discovered during a scrutiny." (https://deshgujarat.com/2016/12/24/fcra-cancellation-forces-navsarjan-ngo-to-lay-off-its-80-odd-staff/). I found no court outcome. One 2017 secondary mention says the writ was filed in the Delhi HC, not the Gujarat HC; this is unverified.
verdicts.innocentReading: MHA cancelled on the strength of adverse IB field reports that were already on file. By MHA's account, the August 2016 renewal was an administrative error that a later scrutiny caught. The "harmony" wording is the statute's standard clause, used for the whole December batch, not a finding written for this trust. On that reading, how close the cancellation fell to Una reflects when the scrutiny happened, not retaliation. Neither reading is proven. No field reports have been disclosed and I found no court ruling.
verdicts.reason: The source says exactly what the claim says: a verbatim quote of the stated ground, the date 2016-12-15 and the actor (Union Home Ministry). A second outlet (DeshGujarat 2016-12-24) independently quotes the order ("has come to adverse notice for its undesirable activities aimed to affect prejudicially harmony..."). That MHA stated this ground is therefore documented. Whether the ground is true is a government assertion that no court has ruled on, so it is correctly `alleged`, and it carries a contra (c089). I could not refute it. The weaknesses are in the annotation, not the edge. The `d` field presents Macwan's Una link as a neutral date test, and the record leaves out MHA's own stated account (IB reports, "inadvertent" renewal). The claim does not frame a family, religion or ethnicity as the actor.
verdicts.corrections: 1. srcs: add ["DeshGujarat 2016-12-24 — MHA order text; MHA officials: IB adverse reports, renewal 'inadvertent'", "https://deshgujarat.com/2016/12/24/fcra-cancellation-forces-navsarjan-ngo-to-lay-off-its-80-odd-staff/"]. 2. d: replace "Date test: cancellation came five months after the 2016-07 Una assault protests in which Navsarjan was active" with "Una link (2016-07-11, about 5 months earlier) is Macwan's attribution per Scroll; MHA officials (per DeshGujarat) said the trust was under scrutiny on adverse IB field reports and that the 2016-08-03 renewal was 'inadvertent'. The ground is the standard s.12(4) harmony clause, used across the December 2016 batch of about 7 NGOs." 3. Add a contra or government-account note carrying the MHA explanation, so the record states the government's reason as well as the trust's. 4. upgradeIf: change "Gujarat HC finding" to "Any High Court ruling on the cancellation (forum unconfirmed; one 2017 report says Delhi HC), or the order itself on fcraonline.nic.in". Do not link Gujarat HC WP(PIL) 97/2016, which is unrelated. 5. killIf: keep "Order quashed", and add "MHA order text shows a different ground". 6. Entity ngo:navsarjan-trust: fill in identity.fcra with the FCRA registration number when it is found.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: the MHA (FCRA wing, Foreigners Division) cancelled Environics Trust's FCRA registration by an order dated 2024-03-04. The source (Devdiscourse carrying PTI, New Delhi, 2024-04-05 14:18 IST) quotes the court: "The petitioner has approached this court challenging an order dated March 4, 2024 cancelling the registration under FCRA." MHA administers FCRA without interruption, so there is no tenure-window problem. The date sequence is consistent: CBI FIR in January 2024, cancellation 2024-03-04, High Court notice 2024-04-05, listing 2024-05-10. A later primary record exists: Delhi HC order of 2026-05-15 (Kaurav J) in W.P.(C) 9059/2023 and W.P.(C) 5004/2024 (Environics Trust v Union of India, https://indiankanoon.org/doc/196640405/). It shows the challenge still pending, listed for 2026-08-04, with no quashing. So `to: null` is correct as of 2026-05.
verdicts.identityTest: The target matches: the source names "NGO Environics Trust", and the 2026 High Court order names the petitioner "ENVIRONICS TRUST" (Sr. Adv. Rakesh Khanna). The FCRA registration number is not in the source. The actor is inferred. The source says "the Centre" and the 2024 petition's respondent is "Union of India The Secretary". Attributing it to MHA's FCRA wing (Foreigners Division) is the standard reading, but the source does not name that unit. There is also a discrepancy about what kind of action this was. The 2026-05-15 High Court order describes the subject of both petitions as "The rejection of the petitioner's FCRA renewal application", not a s.14 cancellation. PTI (2024) calls it cancellation. The 2026 wording may simply cover both petitions together (the 2023 and 2024 actions), but whether the March 2024 order was a cancellation or a refusal to renew is not fully settled.
verdicts.baseRate: Loss of FCRA registration is common: over 20,000 cancellations since 2011, and 5,933 associations ceased registration on 2022-01-01 alone. So the event itself does not discriminate between critics and non-critics. That does not weaken this edge, which only records that one enforcement event happened. It supports no inference about targeting. The SPEC controls (VIF, India Foundation, Azim Premji, Tata, Reliance, Adani Foundation) have no comparable action in the file. Any selectivity reading belongs in analytic claims (c099, c018), not here.
verdicts.denialFound: The Trust's response is in the source. Its senior counsel told the Delhi HC on 2024-04-05: "They have to give us a personal hearing before they pass the order of cancellation. There was no hearing given to us." (https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/law-order/2878882-hc-seeks-centres-stand-on-plea-by-environics-trust-against-fcra-cancellation). The Trust is challenging the order, not denying it exists. MHA/Centre: the court asked for a reply within four weeks, but no public MHA statement was found. Asked (by the court); no reply on the public record.
verdicts.innocentReading: The boring explanation: a routine FCRA regulatory action following a CBI FIR over 2018 transfers and alleged use of funds for purposes other than those declared. It sits in the same post-2020 wave of cancellations and non-renewals that hit thousands of associations. The edge claims nothing beyond the cancellation and the Trust's procedural objection, so this reading does not conflict with it.
verdicts.reason: The one source, a PTI wire carried by Devdiscourse, states the exact fact, date and target, and records the Trust's response. A 2026 Delhi HC order confirms the litigation over Environics Trust's FCRA status is real and still pending, which rules out quashing so far. The claim is not refuted. It stays at reported rather than documented: syndicated copies of PTI are not independent outlets, the order text itself was not opened, and the 2026 order calls the action a renewal rejection, which leaves its legal type slightly unsettled. The search budget ran out, and the direct site searches that followed (LiveLaw, The Wire, Bar & Bench) found no second independent outlet.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Add to `d`: "Delhi HC W.P.(C) 5004/2024 (with W.P.(C) 9059/2023) still pending. Order of 2026-04-15 directed MHA, without prejudice, to consider an application for fresh registration. Order of 2026-05-15 (Kaurav J) describes the subject as 'rejection of the petitioner's FCRA renewal application', asks MHA for a sealed-cover report, and lists the case for 2026-08-04." Add the source ["Indian Kanoon — Environics Trust v Union of India, Delhi HC, 2026-05-15", "https://indiankanoon.org/doc/196640405/"]. 2) Note in `d` that the source names the actor as "the Centre" and that the Foreigners Division attribution is inferred. 3) Flag the ambiguity between cancellation (s.14) and refusal to renew (s.16), and word the `lab` as "cancellation (per PTI) of FCRA registration". 4) Change `upgradeIf` to "Text of the 2024-03-04 MHA order, or a Delhi HC order in W.P.(C) 5004/2024 reciting it, or a second independent outlet". Keep `killIf` as "Order quashed/set aside". 5) Replace the stale "hearing 2024-05-10 on interim relief" with the 2026 status.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim as a sentence: CBI (named agency) alleged in an FIR registered January 2024 (ThePrint: registered Tue 2024-01-16, reported 2024-01-19) that Environics Trust transferred Rs 1,250 each to 711 people on 2020-11-15. The Trust held FCRA registration in 2020. It was suspended in 2023 and cancelled on 2024-03-04, so the alleged act falls inside the registration window, and the FIR comes before the cancellation. The Devdiscourse/PTI copy is internally inconsistent: it says the FIR covers "several bank transfers carried out in 2018" and then gives the 15 November 2020 transfer. The claim correctly uses 2020-11-15, and ThePrint confirms "on 15 November, 2020". The record is stale: CBI filed a chargesheet on 2025-01-24 before a special court in New Delhi (ThePrint/PTI, Business Standard), and the claim does not mention it. That meets the claim's own upgradeIf ("Chargesheet"), although a chargesheet is still unadjudicated.
verdicts.identityTest: Entity matches. Every source names "Environics Trust" (New Delhi NGO; FIR accused managing director Ramamurthi Sreedhar, who died 2023-12-29, and finance director Vanitha Sreedhar). The chargesheet names Environics Trust, Vanitha Sreedhar, Nishant Kumar Alag and Prasanta Kumar Paikray under IPC 120-B, 417, 468 and 471 plus FCRA. No FCRA registration number was cited or checked (fcraonline is blocked). Subject problem: the edge's s is "agencies", but the source names the actor specifically as CBI. The cancellation (c090) is MHA's; the FIR allegation is CBI's.
verdicts.baseRate: This does not turn on a base rate. The claim is one specific, quantified allegation (711 x Rs 1,250 = Rs 8,88,750, so a = 0.0889 crore is arithmetically correct), not a shared property. Symmetry: the "diversion to protests" ground is not unique to this government or to critics. Under the UPA, the 2012 Kudankulam cluster and INSAF were actioned on the same kind of ground, and CPSC got a CBI FCRA FIR in 2022. The SPEC control (critical versus aligned associations) would record an identical CBI allegation against a neutral body the same way. The claim carries no framing by family, religion or ethnicity.
verdicts.denialFound: None found, and the Trust was asked. PTI emailed Environics Trust about both the FIR (2024-01) and the chargesheet (2025-01): "An email sent to ET by PTI seeking a response on the development remained unanswered by the time of filing this story." ThePrint (2024-01-19) also wrote: "ThePrint has reached Environics Trust on email for comment. This report will be updated if and when a response is received." The only recorded position is a procedural one from counsel in the Delhi HC on 2024-04-05: "They have to give us a personal hearing before they pass the order of cancellation. There was no hearing given to us" (Devdiscourse/PTI). That is not a denial of the payments.
verdicts.innocentReading: Dhinkia is in Jagatsinghpur district, which was reportedly among the Odisha coastal districts hit by Cyclone Amphan (May 2020). The same 711 villagers could have been genuinely cyclone-affected relief recipients and also participants in the long-running anti-JSW (formerly POSCO) agitation. A relief disbursement six months after the cyclone, made to residents of a protest village, fits both readings. CBI's case that the money was "actually paid to the protesters for JSW agitation" has not been tested in court.
verdicts.reason: The one cited source (Devdiscourse, syndicated PTI copy, 2024-04-05) states the claim almost verbatim: "According to the CBI, Environics Trust had allegedly transferred Rs 1,250 each in the bank accounts of 711 people on November 15, 2020, for distribution among Amphan cyclone-affected people in Odisha but actually the payments were made to protestors for JSW agitation at Dhinkia, Odisha." ThePrint (2024-01-19) confirms it independently. The claim is worded as an allegation, attributed to the CBI FIR and marked not adjudicated, so "alleged" is the correct tier. Nothing refutes it. The fixes needed are the actor field, a stale status (a chargesheet was filed 2025-01-24) and the contra, which should record that the Trust was asked and did not answer.
verdicts.corrections: 1) s: change "agencies" to the CBI entity (e.g., "ngo:cbi" / "agency:cbi"). 2) lab/text: say "Amphan cyclone relief" rather than generic "Odisha cyclone relief", to match the source. 3) d: add "CBI chargesheet filed 2025-01-24 before special court, New Delhi, against Environics Trust, Vanitha Sreedhar, Nishant Kumar Alag, Prasanta Kumar Paikray (IPC 120-B/417/468/471 + FCRA); also alleges forged MAA Plasto invoices of Rs 6.50 lakh + Rs 4 lakh; Rs 30,000 to Deme Oram. Not adjudicated." Also note the PTI copy's inconsistent "2018 transfers" line. Tier stays alleged. Keep killIf as "Closure report / discharge / acquittal" and change upgradeIf to "Conviction or court framing of charges". 4) srcs: add ThePrint 2024-01-19 FIR report (https://theprint.in/india/cbi-registers-fir-against-ngo-environics-trust-its-directors-for-funding-agitations-in-odisha/1930188/) and ThePrint/PTI 2025-01-24 chargesheet (https://theprint.in/india/cbi-files-chargesheet-against-ngo-environics-trust-for-fcra-violations/2461234/). 5) contra c092 d: add "Asked: PTI emailed ET (2024-01 and 2025-01) and ThePrint emailed ET (2024-01-19); no response recorded. Counsel's only recorded position is procedural (no personal hearing), not a denial of the payments." 6) Add innocentReading: Jagatsinghpur was an Amphan-affected district, so the recipients may have been both cyclone-affected and protesters.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: MHA (Home Ministry FCRA wing) cancelled Bal Raksha Bharat's FCRA registration in 2023-09. Outlook's article is datePublished 2023-09-15T09:20 IST and names the date only as 'ahead of the September 30 deadline'. The ET original it relays is datePublished 2023-09-14T00:11 IST, so the cancellation happened on or before 13-14 Sept 2023. Unless it happened in late August, 2023-09 fits. The ₹163.18 crore figure is for FY2021-22 and was disclosed in an audited report filed in March 2023, so it comes before the action. The cancellation falls within the NDA government's term. Test passes.
verdicts.identityTest: Both sources name the same NGO. Outlook: "UK-based NGO Save The Children's India unit Bal Raksha Bharat's licence has been revoked." ET: "the government has cancelled the licence of Bal Raksha Bharat, also known as Save The Children". No FCRA registration number is given in either source, so the entity is matched by name only. That match is backed by the organisation's own confirmation (see denialFound). The actor is 'the government' / 'home ministry' per 'officials'. Mapping this to ngo:mha-foreigners-division, the division that houses the FCRA wing, is a reasonable institutional mapping, but no named officer is given. Caution: the co-cancelled 'SEWA' is a North East Delhi animal-husbandry NGO, not the Ahmedabad SEWA. This does not affect c093 but should be checked wherever SEWA appears.
verdicts.baseRate: An FCRA cancellation is not unusual in itself. Parliament was told that 6,677 registrations were cancelled in 2017-21 (quoted in Outlook). ET notes 16,497 active licences in Sept 2023, and a wave of non-renewals and cancellations came around the 30 Sept 2023 deadline. The claim does not assert targeting, only the event and its scale. Scale does discriminate: ₹163 crore a year puts Bal Raksha Bharat among the largest FCRA recipients. Symmetry control from the SPEC: UPA also cancelled or blocked registrations on a large scale (about 4,000+ in 2012 for non-filing, plus the Kudankulam-linked cases). So the fact of a cancellation alone says nothing about which government is doing it. The claim does not frame a family, religion or ethnicity as the actor.
verdicts.denialFound: No denial. The party was asked and confirmed the cancellation. ET, 2023-09-14, Rahul Tripathi (https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/india/home-ministry-cancels-fcra-licence-of-bal-trust/articleshow/103643895.cms): "A senior functionary of the trust confirmed that its FCRA licence has been cancelled but did not elaborate further." No public statement from Bal Raksha Bharat or Save the Children disputing the grounds was found. Further web search was blocked by the search budget.
verdicts.innocentReading: This may be a routine refusal or cancellation in the 30 Sept 2023 re-registration round after the 2020 FCRA amendments, for a technical or compliance reason (for example, the post-2020 SBI New Delhi FCRA account or utilisation-for-administration limits). It need not be a finding of misuse. The source's 'misuse or diversion' sentence is generic background on the law ("Any misuse or diversion of foreign funds by NGOs is considered a violation"). It is not a ground attributed to this NGO. The ₹163.18 crore figure is total bank receipts from an audited report. It shows size, not wrongdoing, and the source does not explicitly call it foreign contribution.
verdicts.reason: The source holds up. Outlook states the cancellation and the amount: "Bal Raksha Bharat's licence has been revoked... it had received Rs 163.18 crore in its bank accounts and Rs 66.66 lakh worth of in-kind contributions for the year 2021-22, ET reported". Outlook says 'reportedly' and relays ET's story rather than reporting independently. The ET original (Rahul Tripathi, ET Bureau, 2023-09-14) has 'officials said' sourcing and the exact figure '₹163,18,59,530'. It also has the NGO's own confirmation ("A senior functionary of the trust confirmed that its FCRA licence has been cancelled"). That is one credible outlet with named sourcing plus a party confirmation, which fits 'reported'. It is not 'documented': there are no two independent outlets (Outlook is derivative), and no MHA order or FCRA portal entry was opened. Nothing found shows the order was quashed.
verdicts.corrections:
1. srcs: add the ET original as the primary source, before Outlook: ["ET 2023-09-14 (Rahul Tripathi) — Home ministry cancels FCRA licence of Bal Raksha Bharat; trust functionary confirms", "https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/india/home-ministry-cancels-fcra-licence-of-bal-trust/articleshow/103643895.cms"]. Mark Outlook as derivative (it says 'reportedly' / 'ET reported'), not a second independent outlet.
2. d: change 'received in 2021-22' to 'total receipts in bank accounts per audited report filed March 2023 (₹163,18,59,530) plus ₹66,66,444 in kind, FY2021-22; source does not label it foreign contribution'. Replace 'grounds not specified beyond "misuse or diversion of foreign funds"' with 'no ground stated; the misuse/diversion sentence in both sources is generic background, not attributed to this NGO'.
3. from: keep 2023-09, but note 'on or before 2023-09-14 (ET publication)'.
4. c095 (contra): replace 'No response recorded — asked/not asked unknown' with 'Asked; a senior functionary confirmed the cancellation and did not elaborate (ET 2023-09-14)', and add the ET URL.
5. c094: no opened source attributes the misuse/diversion ground to Bal Raksha Bharat. Downgrade to a void/gap or kill it as an edge; do not keep it as an 'alleged ground'.
6. upgradeIf: 'MHA order, FCRA portal cancelled-list entry, or an independent second outlet'.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: MHA Foreigners Division cited misuse or diversion of foreign funds as its ground for cancelling Bal Raksha Bharat's FCRA registration in 2023-09. The actor fits: MHA administers FCRA. The date is wrong. The Outlook piece (published 2023-09-15) rewrites an Economic Times report. The action was reported in early August 2023: Insights 2023-08-04, India CSR 2023-08-05 and LiCAS 2023-08-08, all describing the renewal as rejected and the order posted on MHA's website. So `from` should be 2023-08, not 2023-09. This affects c093 as well.
verdicts.identityTest: The entity is right. Outlook: "UK-based NGO Save The Children's India unit Bal Raksha Bharat's licence has been revoked." The FCRA registration number is not recorded (identity.fcra is null), and it should be added from the MHA order if one can be found.
verdicts.baseRate: Not discriminating, and the claim depends on that. The "misuse or diversion" sentence is the general FCRA test that applies to every registrant. Outlook: "If any misuse or diversion of foreign funds is reported within the NGO, it is considered a violation of the FCRA Act." The Wire has the same boilerplate: "Any misuse or diversion of foreign funds by NGOs is considered a violation of the FCRA Act." A sentence that is true of 100% of FCRA registrants cannot serve as a stated ground against one of them. For the control, the same Wire article names YWCA Delhi as a case where MHA actually cited fund diversion. That is the kind of case-specific attribution this claim lacks.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, there is a response, so "no response recorded" is wrong. Bal Raksha Bharat's spokesperson "expressed surprise but assured that they would work closely with the government to resolve the matter" and committed to "continuing critical services to the community and children" (India CSR, 2023-08-05, https://indiacsr.in/bal-raksha-bharat-loses-fcra-permit/). The Wire also reports that a senior representative "confirmed the cancellation of its FCRA licence to the business daily, but did not provide further details" (https://m.thewire.in/article/rights/home-ministry-cancels-fcra-licence-of-bal-raksha-bharat-two-other-ngos).
verdicts.innocentReading: The Outlook sentence is explanatory background on how FCRA works, not an MHA ground for this organisation. No opened source states MHA's reason. Where press coverage links the action to anything, it is the November 2022 Ministry of Women and Child Development complaint calling Save the Children's malnutrition fundraising campaign "misleading", plus NCPCR's objection to how children were portrayed. That is a different allegation from fund diversion, and it is press context, not a stated ground in the order. It could also be an ordinary renewal refusal during the 2020–2023 re-registration window, when many renewals were refused.
verdicts.reason: The claim takes a generic sentence from the Outlook article ("If any misuse or diversion of foreign funds is reported within the NGO, it is considered a violation of the FCRA Act") and presents it as MHA's alleged ground against Bal Raksha Bharat. Neither Outlook nor The Wire (which carries the same boilerplate) says MHA cited diversion for this organisation. Under CONTRACT, `alleged` needs a named party making the assertion, and here nobody makes it. The record's own `d` field admits "No specific ground in an opened source." An edge that attributes an unsourced diversion allegation to a named NGO should be killed. The linked contra c095 is also wrong: a spokesperson response exists. The date 2023-09 is wrong too; the action was reported in 2023-08.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Kill c094 and its contra c095. 2) In c093, remove "grounds not specified beyond 'misuse or diversion of foreign funds'" and replace it with "grounds not stated in any opened source; press links it to MWCD's Nov 2022 'misleading' complaint about the malnutrition campaign (context, not a stated ground)". Change `from` from 2023-09 to 2023-08. Add sources: The Wire (https://m.thewire.in/article/rights/home-ministry-cancels-fcra-licence-of-bal-raksha-bharat-two-other-ngos) and India CSR 2023-08-05 (https://indiacsr.in/bal-raksha-bharat-loses-fcra-permit/). Both still trace back to ET, so a genuinely independent second outlet or the MHA order is needed before any upgrade to documented. 3) If a ground-type claim is wanted, create a new `alleged` claim with MWCD, not MHA, as the actor ("MWCD called the Save the Children malnutrition campaign 'misleading', 2022-11-02"). Its contra should quote the Bal Raksha Bharat spokesperson's response. 4) In the entity `sub` field, change "FCRA cancelled 2023-09" to "FCRA renewal rejected / registration cancelled, reported 2023-08-03/04". Add the FCRA registration number if the MHA order can be found.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: MHA (Foreigners Division, FCRA wing) cancelled the FCRA registrations of three of twelve Kudankulam-area associations in 2012-02. MHA administered FCRA in 2012 and P. Chidambaram was Home Minister (2008-11 to 2012-07), so the actor and window overlap and the date passes. The Tribune print edition is dated 2012-02-25 with a 24 February dateline, and it reports the cancellation in the past tense, so it happened on or before 2012-02-24. The record's "Tribune 2012-02-24" label matches the dateline. The URL date (20120225) is the print date, which is fine.
verdicts.identityTest: This partly fails. The source never names the three associations. The "12 NGOs" are unnamed, so ngo:kudankulam-linked-associations is an aggregate node with no FCRA registration numbers. The statement also does not come from MHA. It comes from V. Narayanasamy, Minister of State in the PMO and for Personnel, a different ministry, who is relaying what MHA had supposedly done. Tribune's words are: "The Minister of State for Personnel said the home ministry had cancelled licences of three of the 12 NGOs whose fund utilisation was under scrutiny." The source says "operating licences", not "FCRA registrations". Reading it as FCRA is plausible but is our inference; it could also mean prior-permission or suspension.
