Home Minister Chidambaram, who was actually responsible, spoke on 2012-02-29 (Deccan Herald, published 2012-03-01). He described bank accounts of FOUR NGOs being frozen and CBI/TN police cases, and did not mention any cancellations. Deccan Herald on 2012-02-28 likewise reports four NGOs "booked" with accounts frozen, following MHA checks of "audited accounts of 12 NGOs", and again mentions no cancellations. Deccan Herald on 2012-02-24 reports Narayanasamy "blamed three NGOs for diverting foreign funds" and says "the government took action", but it does not say their licences were cancelled.
verdicts.baseRate: Cancellation itself does not single anyone out. The News Bharati figures (a weak source), reproduced by Hinduism Today, put MHA's cancellations at 4,141 of 39,236 registered associations in 2012-13, and 794 of those were in Tamil Nadu. Three cancellations in a year with thousands is routine volume. What would make this notable is the stated link to the Kudankulam protests, and that link rests only on ministers' statements. Chidambaram "refused to confirm that there was any link between inspection of accounts and activities of the NGOs and their support to the anti-KNPP movement" (DH 2012-03-01). On symmetry, this claim is itself the UPA-era control named in SPEC. The same lens applied to NDA cancellations (Greenpeace, Tuticorin Diocesan Association 2015) reads the same way: a government statement of grounds without a published order is at most alleged or reported, not documented. The claim does not name a religion as the actor, although DH calls them "Christian NGOs". Keep it that way.
verdicts.denialFound: Only the movement's general denial is on record. Tribune 2012-02-25 quotes S.P. Udayakumar of PMANE: "It is unfortunate that the Prime Minister has made the allegations without any documentary proof. We strongly deny his observation that the agitation is being funded by other countries." DH 2012-02-28 reports that Udayakumar sent a legal notice to the PM calling the imputation "totally false" (https://www.deccanherald.com/content/230728/4-ngos-booked-funding-protests.html). No response from the three unnamed associations exists, because they were never named; whether they were asked is unknown. The contrary official account is Chidambaram's (freezes and cases, no cancellations): https://www.deccanherald.com/india/pc-says-more-ngos-scanner-2317244
verdicts.innocentReading: Narayanasamy was not the minister responsible for FCRA. He may have conflated account freezes or suspensions of prior permission with "cancelled licences", or counted routine 2011-12 cancellations for non-filing of FC returns among Tamil Nadu associations that happened to be under the same scrutiny. The official version that followed (four accounts frozen, criminal cases, no cancellations mentioned) fits a picture in which no Kudankulam-specific FCRA cancellation had been completed by 24 February 2012.
verdicts.reason: The Tribune URL loads, and it does carry the sentence "the home ministry had cancelled licences of three of the 12 NGOs". But the claim turns a second-hand statement by a minister from another ministry (MoS PMO/Personnel Narayanasamy) into an MHA enforcement act. It also turns "operating licences" into "FCRA registrations". The Home Minister's own account five days later describes four NGOs with frozen accounts and criminal cases and mentions no cancellations. Contemporaneous DH reporting on 24 and 28 February does not corroborate any cancellation. As worded, the edge states as fact something that only one relayed ministerial assertion supports, and the responsible ministry's account does not match it. As an MHA enforce edge it should be alleged, carrying a contra. Keep it at reported only if it is recast as Narayanasamy's statement.
verdicts.corrections: 1. lab: "MoS (PMO/Personnel) V. Narayanasamy said MHA had cancelled 'operating licences' of three of 12 unnamed Kudankulam-area NGOs under scrutiny, 2012-02-24 (UPA)". Drop "FCRA registrations" unless an MHA record says so. 2. tier: reported -> alleged for the s=ngo:mha-foreigners-division enforce edge. Alternatively, set s=wel:v-narayanasamy (or a statement node) and keep reported. 3. Add a contra: Chidambaram 2012-02-29, bank accounts of four NGOs frozen and cases filed by CBI/TN police, no cancellations mentioned (DH https://www.deccanherald.com/india/pc-says-more-ngos-scanner-2317244). Add DH 2012-02-28 (https://www.deccanherald.com/content/230728/4-ngos-booked-funding-protests.html) as a second source for the "12 NGOs" scrutiny and the four cases. 4. d: note that the associations are unnamed and there are no FCRA registration numbers, so identity is unresolved. 5. upgradeIf: keep the requirement for a Parliament answer or MHA Annual Report 2011-12 naming the associations and the cancellation orders. killIf: add "MHA or Parliament record shows only freezes or prior-permission for the Kudankulam cluster in 2012-02, and no cancellations".

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: PM Manmohan Singh (in office 2004-05-22 to 2014-05-26) said in a Science interview in Feb 2012 that US/Scandinavian-funded NGOs were behind the Kudankulam agitation. Tribune (dateline New Delhi, Feb 24, 2012; edition dated 2012-02-25) says: "The Prime Minister had yesterday in an interview with a Science journal pointedly accused US-based NGOs". So he said it on about 2012-02-23, within his tenure. from=2012-02 is correct. The source label "Tribune 2012-02-24" matches the dateline, but the URL is the 25 Feb edition. Minor.
verdicts.identityTest: The speaker is right: the PM, in the Science (AAAS) interview. The target is off. The PM's words were aimed at foreign NGOs: "these NGOs, mostly I think based in the United States". The India-based recipients ("to some of the India-based NGOs ... close to the Kudankulam area, to Tuticorin, Tirunelveli") were named by MoS PMO V. Narayanasamy on 2012-02-24, not by the PM. The Tribune does not support the "Scandinavian" part for the PM. It says Narayanasamy "also added Scandinavian countries". The Science interview itself does (per ANS Nuclear Newswire): "There are NGOs, often funded by the U.S. and the Scandinavian countries...". So the quote holds against the primary interview, which is not in srcs. No FCRA registration numbers or names for the 12 associations appear in the opened source. The contra (c098) comes from PMANE/S.P. Udayakumar, a movement, not from the unnamed associations.
verdicts.baseRate: Non-discriminating as evidence of foreign funding. Governments of both blocs have said "foreign-funded NGOs are behind protests against a project": UPA on Kudankulam (2012), NDA in the 2014 IB report on Greenpeace and anti-development NGOs, and Sterlite/Thoothukudi (2018). This is the usual government response to a stalled project, so the statement shows a political stance, not a funding finding. Symmetry: the SPEC names the 2012 Kudankulam cancellations as the UPA control. Tiering this UPA claim as alleged is consistent with how NDA-era foreign-hand claims should be tiered. The same lens gives the same reading.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, in the same source. PMANE's S.P. Udayakumar (Chennai, 2012-02-24): "It is unfortunate that the Prime Minister has made the allegations without any documentary proof. We strongly deny his observation that the agitation is being funded by other countries." (https://www.tribuneindia.com/2012/20120225/main2.htm). This is already recorded as contra fcra-actions:c098. Arun Jaitley (BJP) and D. Raja (CPI; the Tribune prints "A. Raja") asked the government to make the evidence public. The Tribune reports only that the NGOs "took a strong exception". The individual associations were not named, so whether they were asked is unknown.
verdicts.innocentReading: Several Tuticorin/Tirunelveli church and social-service associations were long-standing FCRA-registered recipients of Western church and development funding for relief, fishing-community and post-tsunami work. Local anti-nuclear mobilisation drew on the same parish networks. The overlap in geography and personnel is enough to fit the PM's remark without any foreign funds being diverted to the agitation. The statement is also consistent with political pressure to commission a stalled Indo-Russian project.
verdicts.reason: The substance survives as an allegation. The quoted sentence appears in the Tribune: "these NGOs, mostly I think based in the United States, dont appreciate the need for our country to increase the energy supply". The "US and Scandinavian" funding wording is in the PM's primary Science interview. The claim is dated inside his tenure, and a denial is recorded (c098). No adjudicated finding of diversion appears in any opened source, so alleged is the correct tier. The edge is mis-encoded, though. pred=enforce with s=wel:manmohan-singh says the PM took an enforcement action against the Kudankulam-linked associations. He did not: he gave a magazine interview aimed at foreign NGOs. The enforcement (3 of 12 licences cancelled, an MHA probe) is MHA's and is already edge c096. The "Scandinavian" attribution in the Tribune belongs to Narayanasamy.
verdicts.corrections: 1) pred: the PM's interview is a statement, not an enforcement action. Either re-encode s as MHA (ngo:mha-foreigners-division, "investigation") with the PM/PMO statement cited as the basis, or move the PM remark into the narratives array and keep c096 as the enforcement edge. 2) text/lab: quote the PM exactly: "these NGOs, mostly I think based in the United States, don't appreciate the need for our country to increase the energy supply". Attribute "often funded by the U.S. and the Scandinavian countries" to the Science interview, and "sent money close to the Kudankulam area ... to some of the India-based NGOs" plus the Tribune's "Scandinavian" addition to MoS PMO V. Narayanasamy (2012-02-24, ANI). 3) srcs: add the primary Science (AAAS) interview, Feb 2012, and a secondary such as https://www.ans.org/news/article-952/indian-pm-singh-alleges-anti-nuclear-protests-funded-by-u-s-ngos/. Relabel the Tribune as edition 2012-02-25, dateline 2012-02-24. 4) Target: the PM's remark targets foreign (US-based) NGOs. The India-based associations are Narayanasamy's target, so split or retarget. 5) contra c098: set s to a PMANE / S.P. Udayakumar node rather than ngo:kudankulam-linked-associations, since PMANE is not shown to be one of the 12 associations. 6) upgradeIf: add an MHA Parliament answer or MHA Annual Report 2011-12/2012-13 that names the associations whose accounts were frozen or cancelled.

verdicts.dateTest: Written as a claim: MHA Foreigners Division (UPA, Home Ministers Chidambaram and then Shinde, 2011 to 2014-05-26; NDA from 2014-05-26) applied FCRA grounds to registered associations, 2011 to 2026. The dated UPA acts fall inside UPA tenure: the Kudankulam cancellations were announced 2012-02-24 (Chidambaram), and the INSAF suspension order is dated 2013-04-30 (Shinde). The Delhi HC quashed that suspension on 2013-09-19. The NDA cases (Greenpeace 2015, CHRI 2022, Noel Harper 2022-04-08) fall inside NDA tenure. Date test passes. One nuance: the whole UPA comparison window, 2011-14, ran under the FCRA 2010, which was itself a new UPA statute in force from 2011-05-01. So "after 2020 the statute" leaves out that the statute also changed at the start of the comparison window.
verdicts.identityTest: The actor, MHA Foreigners Division (FCRA Wing), matches the INSAF judgment: "order dated 30.4.2013 issued by the Director to the Government of India, Ministry of Home Affairs, Foreigners Division (FCRA Wing)". The edge target does not match. The task payload gives t = "ngo:fcra-registered-associations", but the record in fcra-actions.json has t = "ngo:fcra-associations-aggregate". One of them is wrong. The srcs list also differs: the payload has 3 URLs, the file has 8 (FIDH, Mongabay, Scroll, hindutvawatch mirror, CSR Universe). The Kudankulam associations are not named in the Tribune piece, so their identities, and the grounds they were cancelled on, cannot be checked.
verdicts.baseRate: This fails as a comparison. It sets about 3 UPA cases against about 20 NDA cases, and only one UPA case has a stated ground on record (INSAF). The Tribune gives no statutory ground for the three Kudankulam cancellations, only "fund utilisation under scrutiny" and "did not follow the guidelines". No reachable source gives a ground for the three CPSC suspensions under the UPA. With n=1 stated UPA ground, "identical grounds" cannot be measured. Aggregate data (Factly, from MHA data) shows 3,922 cancellations in 2012 and 10,003 in 2015. More than 99.5% of 2011-2019 cancellations fell in 2012, 2015, 2017 and 2019, and most were for non-filing (s.18). Noel Harper records "more than 19,000" cancellations for 2011-2019, for statutory non-compliance. So the scale change is real, roughly 2-3x per year. However, the 2015 wave cleared non-filers of FY2009-12 returns (10,343 notices issued in Dec 2014), and the 2016 and 2022 cessations came from the five-year renewal introduced by the UPA's 2010 Act. The file says government-aligned associations (VIF, India Foundation, Ekal) were not examined, so the SPEC's critic/aligned control has only been run on one side.
verdicts.denialFound: None found; not asked. This analytic claim covers two governments and no party was asked. The closest statement from the government is the Union's position recorded in Noel Harper (SC, 2022-04-08): 20,600 "non-compliant" registrations cancelled and "no absolute right inheres in any one ... to receive foreign contribution". That supports the compliance/scale reading. On the UPA side, S.P. Udayakumar called the Kudankulam allegations "baseless" (Tribune 2012-02-25), but that answers c097, not this claim.
verdicts.innocentReading: A single statute (the 2010 Act, with its five-year renewal, s.14 "public interest" ground and the 2011 Rule 3 "political nature" test covering bandh/hartal) was enforced by one bureaucracy under both governments. Its public-interest ground was invoked against protest-funding intermediaries under the UPA (INSAF, Kudankulam) and under the NDA. The volume jump after 2014 reflects a backlog of non-filers from FY2009-12 and the first renewal cycle due in 2016, and the 2020 Amendment then outlawed sub-granting. That reading fits the evidence and does not need "identical" or "only scale changed".
verdicts.reason: The sources confirm the parts of the claim. They do not support the headline as worded. The INSAF judgment records the UPA ground: "foreign funds ... transferred to other FCRA registered as well as non-FCRA registered NGOs, which were utilizing the said fund for organizing the protest, etc. against the welfare policies of the Government and such utilization ... may prejudicially affect the public interest". The Tribune confirms "the home ministry had cancelled licences of three of the 12 NGOs", with the PM blaming US and Scandinavian funders. Noel Harper confirms the 2020 statute was upheld. But "identical grounds" is a conjunction inference drawn from one UPA case with a stated ground. Several NDA grounds have no UPA counterpart on record: "engagement with embassies and UN Special Rapporteurs" (CPSC 2016), economic-interest / IB-report grounds (Greenpeace), "harmony", and donor-side watch-list and prior-reference controls (Ford, Compassion). "What changed after 2014 is scale, and after 2020 the statute" presents one of several changes as the only one. It leaves out the 2010 UPA statute that drove the renewal-cycle cessations, the donor-side controls, and the 2016/2018 retrospective Finance Act amendments. It also cites a weak 4,141 figure while a better-sourced 3,922 (calendar 2012) exists. The analytic tier fits once the wording is narrowed; as worded, the claim overstates.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Change lab to: "Grounds on record overlap: onward transfer to fund protests / public interest was invoked under the UPA (INSAF 2013; Kudankulam 2012) and the NDA. After 2014 the volume rose (3,922 cancellations in 2012 vs 10,003 in 2015, mostly non-filing), the first renewal cycle under the 2010 UPA Act fell due in 2016, and in 2020 the statute was tightened." 2) In d, replace "4,141 cancellations in 2012-13 (weak source)" with "3,922 cancellations in calendar 2012 (Factly, from MHA data; 4,138 per Newslaundry/Factly 2015-04)" and add the source https://factly.in/the-history-of-fcra-and-the-trends-in-fcra-registration-cancellations/. 3) In d, state that the stated grounds for the Kudankulam cancellations and the UPA-era CPSC suspensions are not on record in the sources opened, so the UPA ground sample is n=1 (INSAF). 4) In d, list the NDA-only grounds and instruments: embassies/UN Special Rapporteurs (CPSC 2016), economic interest (Greenpeace), and the donor watch-list / prior-reference category (Ford, Compassion). 5) Settle the target id: ngo:fcra-associations-aggregate (file) vs ngo:fcra-registered-associations (payload). 6) Add the Noel Harper figure "more than 19,000 ... between 2011 and 2019" as a scale source. 7) Keep upgradeIf/killIf, and make upgradeIf also require running the government-aligned control (VIF, India Foundation, Ekal).

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: Ayana Charitable Trust declared about ₹826 cr of foreign contribution for FY2015-16 (1 Apr 2015 to 31 Mar 2016), with Gospel for Asia, Hong Kong named in its return as the source of most of it. It was reported on 20 Mar 2017, after the FY closed and after the returns were uploaded, so the timing is consistent. The record's from/to dates are correct. One error: the Asianet Newsable citation is dated "31 Mar 2018" in srcs[2], but the page's datePublished is 2017-03-20T12:32:00+05:30, the same day as TOI, TNM and Matters India. It is a same-day rewrite of TOI, not a follow-up a year later.
verdicts.identityTest: Recipient: the sources name Ayana Charitable Trust, Thiruvalla, Pathanamthitta. TOI calls it "the new name under which US charity Gospel for Asia is reportedly funding projects in India." No FCRA registration number appears in any source, so identity rests on name and place only. Donor: TOI names "Gospel for Asia, Hong Kong". That is a different legal entity from Gospel for Asia Inc (Wills Point, Texas) and from GFA Canada. The node ngo:gospel-for-asia is labelled "Gospel for Asia (Hong Kong / US)", which merges the two. The claim text then hangs the US lawsuits and the Canadian ~$94m fraud allegation on the donor edge. Those allegations concern GFA US and GFA Canada, not the HK entity the return lists. That is a conjunction problem: the edge implies the allegations attach to this money flow, and no source says they do.
verdicts.baseRate: "Largest FCRA recipient in FY2015-16" describes one entity by definition, so it is not a base-rate property. What matters here is scale and a single foreign donor. The same TOI article gives the symmetry controls with identical fields: Param Shakthi Peeth (Sadhvi Rithambara, "associated in the past with RSS and VHP") was #2 at about ₹417 cr, Believers Church #3 at ₹342.63 cr, World Vision India #4 at ₹319.26 cr, followed by CARE India, RDT, Kiran Nadar Museum of Art, PHFI (Gates a top donor) and The Hans Foundation. Mostly-one-donor funding is common across the top 10 (Compassion to CEI, Gates to PHFI, WVI's parent to WVI), so a dominant foreign parent donor does not discriminate. The edge has to be judged on amount and identity alone, and Param Shakthi Peeth should get a parallel edge with the same fields.
verdicts.denialFound: None found, and they were not asked. TOI, TNM, Matters India and Asianet carry no comment from Ayana, GFA or K.P. Yohannan, and none says they were approached. On the US and Canadian allegations, GFA's own public position (for example, that the 2019 US class-action settlement admitted no wrongdoing) was not opened in this pass because the web-search budget was used up. That position must be sourced before any allegation text stays attached to this record.
verdicts.innocentReading: Ayana is the Indian field arm of the Gospel for Asia network, renamed from GFA India. Mission agencies routinely route donor money through a regional hub (here Hong Kong) to their national partner, and declaring it in FC-4 is exactly what FCRA requires. A large, legally declared, single-parent transfer to an affiliate is how international NGO networks are funded. WVI, Compassion partners and CARE India are funded the same way. The size of the receipt alone shows no wrongdoing.
verdicts.reason: The core edge survives. The TOI original (timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/christian-ngos-top-in-foreign-funding/articleshow/57723766.cms), opened, says: "A look at Ayana's FCRA returns, which declare its total foreign funding in 2015-16 at a whopping Rs 826 crore, lists Gospel for Asia, Hong Kong, as the source of most of its foreign funds." Matters India reprints this verbatim ("Rs 8.26 billion … source: Times of India"). TNM confirms "With Rs 826 crore … Ayana Charitable Trust … topped the list." All three outlets derive from one TOI report, so there is one outlet with named documentary sourcing (the FCRA returns). That is reported, not documented. Several fields are wrong: (1) ₹826.27 cr appears in no source, only "Rs 826 crore"/"Rs 8.26 billion". (2) The edge amount a=826.27 treats Ayana's total receipts as the GFA-HK grant, but the source says only "most". (3) The claim's srcs omit TOI and Matters India, and TNM and Asianet never name Gospel for Asia Hong Kong as donor. Only TOI and Matters India do. (4) Asianet is misdated. (5) The US and Canadian allegations belong to different GFA entities and are appended with no contra.
verdicts.corrections: 1. a: change 826.27 to null (GFA-HK share not quantified). Put "Ayana total FC ₹826 cr FY2015-16; GFA Hong Kong listed as source of 'most' (TOI)" in d. If an amount must be kept, use 826 with d stating it is Ayana's total receipts from all donors, not the GFA-HK amount. Remove ".27" from lab, d, the entity notes at lines 882 and 1051, and the claim text. 2. srcs: add TOI original, 20 Mar 2017, https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/christian-ngos-top-in-foreign-funding/articleshow/57723766.cms, as the primary cite. Keep Matters India (verbatim TOI reprint, reachable with a browser UA). Mark TNM and Asianet as derivative; neither names GFA Hong Kong. 3. Asianet date: change "31 Mar 2018" to "20 Mar 2017" wherever it appears. 4. Node: split ngo:gospel-for-asia into "Gospel for Asia Hong Kong" (the donor named in the return) and "Gospel for Asia Inc (Texas)"/GFA Canada (the subjects of the lawsuits). Edge s should be the HK entity. 5. Remove "GFA faced US class action and Canadian fraud allegations" from this grant edge. The cited sources say only "several lawsuits … in USA, Canada and Europe" (Asianet) and "allegations of fraud totalling nearly $94 million" against "the Canadian arm" (TNM, via The Star). Move this to a separate alleged-tier claim on the US/Canada entities, with a contra from GFA's public response. 6. upgradeIf: the TOI original has now been opened, and that does not make it documented, because TOI is one secondary outlet. Change the trigger to "Ayana FC-4 FY2015-16 opened, or an independent second outlet with its own reading of the return". 7. Symmetry: add a parallel grant/receipt claim for Param Shakthi Peeth (~₹417 cr FY2015-16, same TOI source) with identical fields.

verdicts.dateTest: Actor: MHA, NDA government (2014 onward). Act: placed Compassion International, as a foreign donor, in the prior-permission category, so Indian associations needed MHA clearance before taking its money. When: 2016. The date falls inside the government's tenure, so it passes at year level. The month is disputed. Oakley's testimony (6 Dec 2016, p.3): "In May of 2016, MHA placed Compassion on a list of international NGOs that had to seek prior clearance". India Today (9 Dec 2016) also says "May last". Mellado's piece in The Hill, quoted by CT, says "a secret order issued in February", and CT says transfers were blocked "since April". The record's from:"2016-02" rests only on Mellado. The two sworn or reported sources say May. The ground in the claim, 'not conducive to national interest', belongs to a different act on a different date. It comes from the Times of India of 5 Nov 2016, about MHA refusing to renew the FCRA registrations of 25 associations. It is not about the prior-permission listing.
verdicts.identityTest: The entity is correct. Compassion International Inc. (Colorado Springs) is the foreign donor that was listed. Its Indian partners are Compassion East India and Caruna Bal Vikas, and India Today names both. The attribution is wrong. The claim says the ground is "known only through Compassion's own testimony". The testimony does not contain the phrase 'not conducive to national interest'. It says the reverse: "MHA has never provided Compassion or its partners with any explanation for the prior clearance order" (p.3). Its only national-interest wording is Compassion's own guess: "MHA evidently views Christian values as a threat to the national interest". CT takes the 'not conducive' phrase from the Times of India, not from Compassion: "The official explanation is that Compassion's activities are 'not conducive to national interest,' reported the Times of India". The TOI article (articleshow/55254613, 5 Nov 2016) says MHA "refused to renew the registration of 25 NGOs ... for their alleged indulgence in 'activities not conducive to national interest'". It is about renewal refusals. It does not name Compassion, and it says nothing about the donor listing. The record's d also says "listed May 2016 under s.11(3)(iv)". The testimony says the opposite. Compassion argues that s.11(3)(iv) requires a Gazette notification, that no such notice was given, and that the actual notice was an RBI prior-clearance notice issued on MHA direction under s.46. The claim joins facts that are each true: the donor was listed (May), and MHA gave a generic ground for the renewal refusals (Nov). Put together, they produce a ground for the listing that no source states.
verdicts.baseRate: Being placed in the prior-permission category is rare and targeted. Only a handful of foreign donors were listed in 2015–16: Ford Foundation in April 2015, Greenpeace International, and Compassion. It is far below the 80% non-discriminating threshold. The 'not conducive to national interest' formula is different. It was the standard wording MHA used for a whole batch of 25 renewal refusals in Nov 2016, so it does not tell us why Compassion in particular was listed. On symmetry, the same prior-permission tool was used against the secular Ford Foundation, which funded government critics. The pattern therefore does not show action against Christian donors alone. The claim does not name a religion as the actor, so no kill is needed on that rule.
verdicts.denialFound: A government-side ground is on record, and the claim leaves it out. A senior MHA official told India Today (9 Dec 2016): "We are ready to reconsider the case of Compassion International, the US donor, which was put under 'prior permission category' for alleged violation of Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA)". The article adds that Compassion "is accused of funding non-Foreign Contribution Regulation Act registered NGOs" (https://www.indiatoday.in/india/delhi/story/us-ngo-compassion-international-foreign-contribution-regulation-act-356547-2016-12-09). The MEA spokesperson, also to India Today and quoted in CT, said "India welcomes lawful operation of foreign NGOs in India" and called the hearing "based on limited understanding of India". Compassion's position is in the testimony: no explanation was ever given, and the renewal refusals cited only "On the basis of Field Agency Report".
verdicts.innocentReading: The government's own account is a compliance problem, not an ideological one. MHA says Compassion was listed because it allegedly sent money to Indian associations that were not registered under FCRA, which the Act restricts. There is some support for this in Compassion's own history. It worked through thousands of partner churches, and its partner CBV had a long-running income-tax dispute (from 2011–13) over transfers to religious-registered charities. The 'national interest' wording belongs to the batch of 25 renewal refusals, not to this listing. Neither the compliance account nor Compassion's discrimination account has been tested in a published order or a court ruling.
verdicts.reason: The central part of the claim is wrong on both points. (1) The ground 'not conducive to national interest' does not come from Compassion's testimony. The testimony says no explanation was ever given. CT gets the phrase from a Times of India story on 25 FCRA renewal refusals, which does not name Compassion or deal with the donor listing. (2) The ground is not 'known only through' Compassion. A senior MHA official is on record in India Today saying the listing was "for alleged violation of FCRA", meaning funding associations not registered under FCRA. The underlying event, MHA putting Compassion in the prior-permission category in 2016, is solid. The testimony, India Today with MHA confirmation, and CT all agree on it, so it holds at 'reported'. Treat it as a single outlet with named sourcing: CT relies on India Today and Compassion rather than doing its own reporting. The ground and the attribution must be rewritten.
verdicts.corrections: text: replace it with "MHA placed Compassion International (US donor) in the FCRA prior-permission category in May 2016 (Oakley testimony; India Today). A senior MHA official gave the ground as 'alleged violation of FCRA' (funding non-FCRA-registered associations). Compassion says no explanation was ever given and alleges religious targeting. MEA: India 'welcomes lawful operation of foreign NGOs'." Drop 'not conducive to national interest' from this edge. That phrase belongs to the Nov 2016 renewal refusals (TOI, 5 Nov 2016) and at most goes on c038 as the batch-level ground, with a note that TOI does not name Compassion's partners. lab: remove "ground 'not conducive to national interest' (per Compassion)". d: remove "listed May 2016 under s.11(3)(iv)". Replace it with "listed May 2016 by an RBI prior-clearance notice issued on MHA direction under s.46. Compassion argues no s.11(3)(iv) Gazette notification was issued." Keep the Mellado/CT claim of a February order as a disputed alternative. from: change "2016-02" to "2016-05", and note the February claim. tier: raise from alleged to reported for the listing event. srcs: add India Today, 9 Dec 2016 (https://www.indiatoday.in/india/delhi/story/us-ngo-compassion-international-foreign-contribution-regulation-act-356547-2016-12-09), the source of the MHA official's statement. c037: add the MHA official's ground and his offer to reconsider next to the MEA quote. Its d currently implies there was no government-side ground. killIf/upgradeIf: keep upgradeIf (an MHA order or a Parliament answer). Change killIf to "order or Parliament answer shows a ground other than FCRA violation / non-registered recipients".

verdicts.dateTest: Claim as written: "MHA refused FCRA renewal of CEI and CBV, Nov 2016". Actor window: MHA under the NDA government (Rajnath Singh was Home Minister May 2014 to May 2019), so the dates overlap and this core passes. The bundled facts do not. (a) The CBV income-tax audit was notified in 2011, the >US$18m assessment came in May 2013 and the bank account was seized in May 2014. The source says: "In 2011, [Compassion's] field-partner in South India, Caruna Bal Vikas (CBV), was notified that it was selected for an audit by the Commissioner of Income Tax (CIT). In May of 2013 ... the CIT assessed CBV more than $18 million". That action was taken by the Income Tax Department under the UPA government, before NDA took office. It is not an MHA act and it falls outside the NDA window. (b) The ED probe of CEI (Aug 2016) is an Enforcement Directorate action. ED sits under the Finance Ministry's Department of Revenue, not MHA. The 'from: 2016-11' date is correct for the refusal only. Note that the source says Compassion "learned" of the refusal in November 2016. The actual order date is not given.
verdicts.identityTest: Weak. The source names "Compassion East India (CEI)" and "Caruna Bal Vikas (CBV)" with no FCRA registration number, city or registered address. Both nodes have identity.fcra = null but are marked resolved:true. The node subtitles "Kolkata-based" (CEI) and "Chennai-based" (CBV) are not in the source, which says only "field-partner in South India" for CBV and gives no location for CEI. The edge target is CEI only, but the text also asserts a refusal and a tax demand against CBV (ngo:caruna-bal-vikas), so the edge covers two entities.
verdicts.baseRate: Compassion's own account, relayed by Christianity Today on 9 Dec 2016, says renewals were refused for "Compassion and at least 24 other NGOs" in the 2016 renewal cycle. That is about 25 refusals against a renewal pool of thousands. Separately, thousands of registrations lapsed for non-application. So a refusal is rare (well under 80%) and discriminating in itself. A refusal preceded by a donor prior-permission listing (Compassion was one of a handful of donors so listed in 2016, alongside Ford Foundation in 2015) is rarer still. Symmetry: the CBV tax action this claim bundles in began under UPA (2011–13), and sibling records (fcra-actions.json symmetryCheck) show UPA using the same unreasoned suspension and cancellation instrument on INSAF, CPSC and the Kudankulam associations. The anti-Compassion reading is therefore not NDA-specific for the tax component.
verdicts.denialFound: An MHA-side response exists, so c039's "no response recorded" is wrong. Times of India (Bharti Jain), 13 Dec 2016: "'We have no immediate plans to reconsider the case of Compassion International ... which was put under prior permission category for alleged violation of Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA),' a senior home ministry official said"; "put under prior permission category in March this year after intelligence agencies flagged its alleged role in encouraging religious conversions and proselytisation through Indian NGOs funded by it." https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/No-prior-permission-relief-for-US-NGO-Compassion-International/articleshow/55966483.cms . The Hindu, 13 Dec 2016: "accused of promoting religious conversion and funding of non-FCRA registered NGOs." https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/Home-Ministry-firm-on-Compassion/article16801760.ece . MEA via CT: "There is a well-established legal framework for NGOs to conduct their operations in India." These responses address the prior-permission listing, not specifically the CEI/CBV non-renewals. On the CEI/CBV refusals themselves, the source quotes the refusal letter's ground: "On the basis of Field Agency Report, the competent authority has decided to refuse your application". Whether the partners were asked for comment by any outlet: not found.
verdicts.innocentReading: MHA refused renewal on an adverse field-agency (IB) report. That is the ground quoted in the letter the source cites, and it matches MHA's public position that Compassion's partners passed foreign money to churches and NGOs not registered under FCRA, which is an FCRA s.7 onward-transfer problem. The CIT 2013 assessment concerned a charitable-vs-religious trust classification under income-tax law, a routine revenue dispute, and it began under the previous government. On this reading the refusals follow from a funding-structure compliance issue (Compassion's church-partner intermediary model), not from religious animus. The later 2020 FCRA amendment banning sub-granting to anyone points the same way.
verdicts.reason: The source (Oakley's written testimony, opened and read in full) does support the core fact as Compassion's account: "in November of 2016, Compassion learned that both its partners, CBV and CEI, had been denied FCRA renewal without explanation", the ED probe of CEI for "anti-national activity" in Aug 2016, and the CIT assessment of more than $18 million. The claim fails as written for four reasons. (1) The same document contradicts "without explanation" by quoting the refusal letter's stated ground: "On the basis of Field Agency Report ...". The record's own killIf is "Orders show a stated ground". The ground shown is formulaic and was not shared, so this is a correction rather than a kill. (2) It is a conjunction edge that credits MHA with an ED action (Finance Ministry) and a CIT assessment from 2011–13 (Income Tax Department, under UPA). (3) The "MHA side: no response recorded" is false: senior MHA officials on record in TOI and The Hindu (13 Dec 2016) cite an alleged FCRA violation, intelligence flags on conversion, and funding of non-FCRA-registered NGOs. (4) The only source is the affected party's own advocacy testimony. Under the CONTRACT a named party asserting something is 'alleged', not 'reported'. No independent outlet or MHA order corroborating the CEI/CBV refusals was opened; CT only relays Compassion's statement.
verdicts.corrections: 1. tier: reported -> alleged (sole source is Compassion's own congressional testimony), and keep the contra. 2. Text/d: replace "denied ... 'without explanation'" with "refused, per Compassion, on the stated ground 'On the basis of Field Agency Report' (report not shared with the partners); Compassion calls this 'without explanation'". 3. Remove the ED probe and the CBV CIT demand from this MHA 'enforce' edge. Record them as separate edges: ED (Finance Ministry / Dept of Revenue) -> CEI, Aug 2016, alleged; and Income Tax Dept (CIT) -> CBV, audit 2011, assessment May 2013 (UPA period), bank account seized May 2014, alleged. 4. Split the target: add a separate MHA -> ngo:caruna-bal-vikas enforce edge for CBV's non-renewal, so this edge covers CEI only. 5. c039: change from "No response recorded" to a contra quoting the senior MHA official (TOI and The Hindu, 13 Dec 2016): alleged FCRA violation, intelligence flags on conversion, funding of non-FCRA-registered NGOs. Note that this addresses the prior-permission listing and that no MHA statement specific to the CEI/CBV refusals was found. Add the MEA line from CT. 6. Nodes: drop "Kolkata-based" and "Chennai-based" (not in source), or add a source for them. Set resolved:false until FCRA registration numbers are found. 7. Add base-rate context: about 25 renewal refusals in the Nov 2016 cycle (per Compassion via CT). 8. upgradeIf: add "FCRA portal status or refusal orders for CEI/CBV with registration numbers; any Delhi HC appeal record".

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: MHA cancelled the FCRA registrations of Believers Church, Ayana Charitable Trust, Love India Ministries and Last Hour Ministry "in Oct 2017". The Christian Post piece is dated 7 Oct 2017 and says only that MHA "has cancelled the registrations". It gives no date for the cancellation itself. The spokesperson says the registrations had been "under revision for the last one year" under a "standing revision order". So the action, or the process leading to it, may be earlier than Oct 2017. MHA is a standing ministry, so there is no tenure-overlap problem. The date problem is precision: "Oct 2017" is when it was reported, not a proven date of the order.
verdicts.identityTest: The source names "the southern India-based Believers Church and three of its affiliates — Ayana Charitable Trust (formerly Gospel for Asia India), Love India Ministries and Last Hour Ministry". The node ngo:believers-eastern-church uses the church's later name (Believers Eastern Church). That is the same body, but the edge covers four associations, each with its own FCRA registration number. The only target node is the church, and no registration numbers were recorded, so the other three are carried in text only. No DIN or CIN applies.
verdicts.baseRate: Cancellation is not a discriminating property. The article itself says MHA cancelled 10,011 licences in 2015 and six in 2016. Tens of thousands of registrations were cancelled or lapsed under the NDA government, and more than 4,000 were cancelled under the UPA government in 2011–14, including the 2012 Kudankulam-linked ones. The groups hit include Christian ones (Compassion partners 2016) and secular and critical ones (Greenpeace, Amnesty, Lawyers Collective). One cancellation shows nothing about targeting. The edge does not claim targeting, so it passes, provided no narrative stacks it into a "crackdown on Christians" pattern without the SPEC controls.
verdicts.denialFound: A response exists, in the same source. Believers Church spokesperson Fr Sijo Panthapallil: "Our FCRA registrations are under revision for the last one year. They had sent us a letter asking for documents and we have submitted the required documents" and "We are sure that we will get the registrations back next week." This is recorded as c041. It describes the process and expects restoration; it does not deny that the registrations were cancelled or suspended. MHA gave no stated ground in the piece, and whether MHA was asked for comment is unknown.
verdicts.innocentReading: This is an ordinary regulatory action. The affiliated Gospel for Asia network faced US allegations of misusing donations, including a US class action settled in 2019, and the registrations were under a year-long document "revision". A cancellation or non-renewal for compliance or accounting reasons fits the facts. So does the church's own account that this was a pending review it expected to be reversed. Nothing in the source ties the action to religion, apart from the outlet's editorial lede about a "Hindu nationalist party".
verdicts.reason: The opened source supports the core claim, attributed: MHA cancelled the FCRA registrations of these four named associations, the ground is not stated, and the church spokesperson expected restoration. The claim uses a neutral agency→association framing with no religion as actor, and a response is recorded as c041. That supports "reported". It is not "documented": Christian Post is itself relaying one outlet (The Times of India, not opened, and the fetch failed), and no MHA order or Parliament answer was opened. The two defects are precision, not substance: the date is the report date, and the scope may be a revision or suspension rather than a final cancellation.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Date: change "from":"2017-10" to show it is a reported-by date. Either set d to "cancellation reported 7 Oct 2017 (Christian Post citing Times of India); order date not stated", or put "by 2017-10-07" in the text. The claim text "in Oct 2017" should read "reported Oct 2017". 2) Source chain: note in d or srcs that Christian Post is relaying The Times of India ("according to The Times of India"), so this is one outlet, second-hand. Add the TOI original as the primary report if it can be retrieved. 3) Scope: add to d that the spokesperson called it a "standing revision order" with registrations "under revision for the last one year", so the status may be cancellation pending revision; killIf already covers this. 4) Identity: record the FCRA registration numbers for all four associations. Either add nodes/edges for Ayana Charitable Trust, Love India Ministries and Last Hour Ministry, or state in d that the edge target stands for the group. 5) Amount: if the Ayana figure (~US$206m, "last financial year", per TOI) is used anywhere, mark it as TOI-sourced, give its FY, and convert it to ₹ crore with the rate cited. 6) c041: relabel it as a response rather than a denial. It does not dispute the cancellation; it expects restoration. 7) Follow-up: check whether the registrations were in fact restored (later reporting on Believers Eastern Church FCRA status, e.g. the 2020 IT searches) and add a supersede edge if they were not.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: MHA withheld RDT's FCRA renewal (2024) and cleared it (March 2026). Deccan Chronicle (Nagabhushanam Hoskote, published 2024-03-23T13:19+05:30) says the renewal "is still pending" and "This has led to denial of renewal", so a 2024 start holds. The South First (Raj Rayasam, 25 Mar 2026) says Ferrer met Naidu on "Tuesday, 24 March" to thank him for the "restoration of foreign funding", and TOI, Indian Express, NIE and The Hindu all ran renewal reports on 24–25 Mar 2026. So March 2026 holds. The record leaves out the middle of the timeline. NIE (30 Apr 2025, fetched) reports "non-renewal of its FCRA licence" as a crisis, which suggests the formal refusal came around April 2025 and the 2024 status was 'pending'. A Hans India headline dated 9 Oct 2025 ("Central govt renews FCRA approval for RDT") conflicts with the March 2026 clearance date. It returned 404 and I could not check it; it may have been an interim or prior-permission step. The date window from 2024 to 2026-03 has no overlap problem: Shah has been Home Minister throughout and Naidu has been CM since June 2024.
verdicts.identityTest: It is the right entity. Both sources name the Rural Development Trust, Anantapur, founded in 1969 by Vicente Ferrer, with programme director Moncho (DC spells it 'Manchu') Ferrer. Neither source gives an FCRA registration number, so the node is identified by name and place only. On the actor: the ground comes from an IB report, but MHA is the FCRA authority, so s=min:ministry-of-home-affairs is the right node for the non-renewal. It should not be read as MHA stating the conversion ground.
verdicts.baseRate: Weak discrimination. Many NGOs with Christian roots or foreign founders lost or failed to renew FCRA registration between 2021 and 2025, and several were restored after lobbying (Missionaries of Charity: renewal refused Dec 2021, restored Jan 2022). Non-renewal after a conversion complaint is common in this class and says nothing specific about RDT. Politicians intervening for large regional service NGOs is also common. On symmetry, the lobbying came from all sides. TDP MPs/MLAs met Shah (Aug 2025, The Hindu/DC/NIE). Opposition YSRCP chief Jagan also thanked the Centre for the renewal (The Hindu, 24 Mar 2026). Credit also went to BC minister S. Savitha/Yadav (Hans India, 2 Apr 2026). The 'beneficiary-by-intervention' reading therefore applies to the whole AP political spectrum, not just the NDA ally.
verdicts.denialFound: RDT denial, Deccan Chronicle 23 Mar 2024 (https://www.deccanchronicle.com/news/non-renewal-of-rdts-fcra-threatens-3k-jobs-medical-aid-886199): "the Rural Development Trust has maintained that it has never encouraged any religious conversions in the past 55 years of its existence. The organisation said it has even dismissed persons from its employment in case they have a tendency of converting people." This is already recorded as c047. No MHA or IB statement of the ground was found, and MHA was not asked in either source.
verdicts.innocentReading: The renewal may have been held up by routine MHA verification after complaints, and by the April 2025 refusal. It was later granted once the file was reviewed, and cross-party representations from both TDP and YSRCP may only have sped it up. Clearing a large secular hospital and development trust that serves 8.5 lakh patients a year is consistent with the merits, and a clearance 'after' lobbying does not show it happened 'because of' lobbying.
verdicts.reason: Both sources say what the claim says. DC: "Intelligence Bureau (IB) has reportedly filed a report that RDT is involved in religious conversions in Pathikonda area of Kurnool district, based on inquiries made after anonymous persons had complained. This has led to denial of renewal." South First: "Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu is learnt to have personally raised the matter with Union Home Minister Amit Shah... the Centre has now granted the necessary clearances." The ground comes from a 'reportedly' IB report and not from an MHA order, so the tier stays alleged. It has a named denial (c047), and the clearance is correctly split out as reported (c048). The claim is not refuted, but it has timeline and framing gaps that need correcting.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Timeline: say "renewal pending/not granted from early 2024 (DC 23 Mar 2024); formal non-renewal reported Apr 2025 (NIE 30 Apr 2025); renewed Mar 2026". Add the NIE Apr 2025 source. Check and reconcile the Hans India 9 Oct 2025 "Central govt renews FCRA approval" headline against the Mar 2026 date. 2) Complainants: 'anonymous complaints' is DC's wording. A named complainant, Legal Rights Protection Forum (LRPF), publicly sought cancellation in March 2024 (Organiser 28 Mar 2024; Commune 24 Mar 2024; Indian Express 28 Mar 2024, 'NGO accuses 2 organisations of religious conversions'). Add LRPF to the record, and add Commune's Apr 2025 reporting of 'fund misuse' allegations as a possible second ground. 3) The c046 record's srcs array lists only DC, while the narrative text also cites South First. Either add the SF URL or move the clearance sentence to c048 only. 4) Framing: 'beneficiary-by-intervention' should record that the intervention was cross-party (TDP MPs/MLAs Aug 2025; YSRCP's Jagan thanked the Centre, The Hindu 24 Mar 2026) and that SF says Naidu "is learnt to have" raised it, which is hedged, not confirmed. 5) Spelling: programme director is 'Moncho Ferrer' (DC writes 'Manchu'). 6) killIf/upgradeIf are fine. Keep tier alleged; do not upgrade until an MHA order or Parliament answer states the ground.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: Embassy of the PRC (New Delhi) is listed as a partner/donor of the Rajiv Gandhi Foundation in RGF's FY2005-06 annual report (FY runs 1 Apr 2005 to 31 Mar 2006). The listing falls inside the UPA-I period and the RGF board of the time. It comes under FCRA 1976, because the 2010 Act commenced on 1 May 2011, so from=2005 and to=2006 is consistent. Note that the Home Minister's ₹1.35 crore figure (Tribune, 2022-12-13) covers FY2005-06 AND FY2006-07. That is a different, wider window and should stay in fcra-actions:c057 rather than be merged here. The BJP's use of the listing came 14 years later, on 2020-06-25, during the Galwan/LAC row. The date test passes.
verdicts.identityTest: The source names "the Embassy of The People's Republic of China" and "the RGF", meaning the Rajiv Gandhi Foundation, which the article distinguishes from the Rajiv Gandhi Charitable Trust and from RGICS. The claim's nodes ngo:china-embassy-prc and ngo:rajiv-gandhi-foundation match. The claim gives no FCRA registration number for RGF, so the identifier is null and should be recorded as a gap. A foreign-government mission is a foreign source under both the 1976 and 2010 Acts, so the identity test passes. One caveat: the listed category is "partner organisations and donors", which mixes the two. The listing alone does not show that money moved rather than a programme partnership, even though the Home Minister's separate statement says ₹1.35 crore was received.
verdicts.baseRate: Not quantified, because the search budget was exhausted and comparable think-tank donor lists from 2005-06 were not retrieved. A base rate is a comparison: what share of similar organisations have the same property. Qualitatively, Indian foreign-policy think tanks and foundations accepting foreign-embassy partnerships or grants for India-China dialogue work in the mid-2000s, during the India-China Friendship Year in 2006, was not unusual. By itself a foreign mission appearing in a published donor list does not tell this organisation apart from its peers. Symmetry: HT (2020-07-08) records Congress pointing to BJP-CPC delegation exchanges over the previous decade. India Foundation (the SPEC's aligned control) took foreign corporate conference sponsorship while saying it received no foreign contribution. Both points show that the same lens applied to the aligned side produces comparable "foreign-link" readings. The discriminating fact is the later MHA cancellation ground, not the listing.
verdicts.denialFound: No denial of the listing itself was found. Congress's response to the June 2020 allegation (Hindustan Times, 2020-07-08, https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/home-ministry-sets-up-panel-to-coordinate-probe-into-3-gandhi-family-trusts/story-KpJkxlJqXIUUhLVwzvq2oN.html) was that "the BJP was engaging in diversionary tactics". It also "questioned it on visits and exchanges between the BJP and the Communist Party of China (CPC)". On the 2022 cancellation, Abhishek Manu Singhvi said "The Rajiv Gandhi Foundation has nothing to add, nothing to fear... you don't ask these questions of many holy cows" (reported via Indian Express / indiacsr.in). No statement from RGF itself about the embassy line-item was found. Whether RGF was asked is unknown.
verdicts.innocentReading: RGF (and RGICS) ran a study of an India-China free trade arrangement during a period of officially promoted India-China rapprochement under the 2005 Strategic and Cooperative Partnership and the 2006 Friendship Year. The embassy partnered in or co-funded that dialogue work, as foreign missions commonly do with policy institutes. RGF then published the embassy's name in its own annual report. Voluntary publication is the opposite of concealment, and it is the only reason the BJP could cite it in 2020. Whether the receipt breached the 1976 Act's procedural requirements (prior permission or returns) is a separate, still-unadjudicated question. It is tiered alleged in fcra-actions:c057.
verdicts.reason: The core fact survives, but only one outlet supports it and the claim over-reaches. The Indian Express article (published 2022-10-23, updated 2022-10-24) states in its own voice: "The RGF annual report for 2005-06 mentions the Embassy of The People's Republic of China as one of the 'partner organisations and donors'. China's name figures in the list of donors for the Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Contemporary Studies (RGICS)". So the listing is confirmed, but only through one outlet. The primary annual report could not be opened. It is not on rgfindia.org/annual-reports-rgf/, whose list starts at 2012-13, and web.archive.org is blocked by egress policy (403). The only other copy found, indiacsr.in, is a verbatim reprint of the IE article, not an independent source. The CONTRACT requires the primary record or two independent outlets for `documented`, so the correct tier is `reported`. The rider "origin of the BJP's China-funding narrative against the Gandhi family" is only partly supported. IE says the BJP leaders "were referring to an account of donations made to RGF in 2005-06 and its annual report", and Ravi Shankar Prasad cited "the donors list of the RGF annual report in 2005-06". But Nadda said the trigger was "Today I was shocked to watch on TV". So "origin" is our characterisation, not the source's. The rider is also political narrative with a family as its object, which belongs in `narratives`, not in an edge.
verdicts.corrections: 1) tier: documented → reported (single outlet, Indian Express; indiacsr.in is a reprint, not corroboration). Add upgradeIf: "RGF Annual Report 2005-06 donor page opened (Wayback snapshot of rgfindia.org c.2006-07, or a physical copy), or RGF FC-3 return for FY2005-06". Add killIf: "RGF annual report 2005-06 opened and the Embassy of the PRC does not appear among partners/donors". 2) text: remove "— origin of the BJP's China-funding narrative against the Gandhi family"; restate as "RGF's FY2005-06 annual report lists the Embassy of the People's Republic of China among its 'partner organisations and donors' (per Indian Express)". Move the BJP-use point into the existing narrative entry. There, cite Nadda (2020-06-25: "$300,000", "shocked to watch on TV") and Prasad ("donors list of the RGF annual report in 2005-06") as alleged, and note the family framing. 3) pred "direct": the listed category mixes partner and donor, and no amount is in the source. Either keep pred direct with a = null plus an explicit note that the report's category is "partner organisations and donors", or use a weaker listing predicate. Do NOT import Shah's ₹1.35 crore (FY2005-07, alleged) into this edge. 4) src label: the date should read "Indian Express, 2022-10-23 (updated 2022-10-24)". 5) Add a contra/response reference: Congress (HT 2020-07-08) called it diversionary and cited BJP-CPC exchanges. There is no RGF-specific denial of the listing, and whether RGF was asked is unknown. 6) Sibling c009 (RGICS) rests on the same single sentence and needs the same downgrade to reported. 7) The narrative strongestCase cites c008 as "(documented, ...)"; change it to "(reported, ...)".

verdicts.dateTest: Claim written out: PRC embassy is listed as a donor to RGICS in FY2005-06. The cited article (Indian Express, datePublished 2022-10-23, not 2022-10-24 as the record says) mentions RGICS in one sentence: "China's name figures in the list of donors for the Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Contemporary Studies (RGICS), a policy think tank promoted by the RGF." That sentence gives no year. "Same period" / from 2005 to 2006 comes from the sentence before it, which is about the RGF annual report for 2005-06: "The RGF annual report for 2005-06 mentions the Embassy of The People's Republic of China as one of the 'partner organisations and donors'." Reading the RGICS sentence as FY2005-06 is reasonable, but it is our inference, not something the article states. The period falls under FCRA 1976, and RGICS existed then, so nothing in the dates contradicts the claim.
verdicts.identityTest: The article names "China" for RGICS. It does not name "the Embassy of the People's Republic of China". Only the RGF sentence names the Embassy. Nadda's quote separately refers to "People's Republic of China and the Chinese embassy". So linking the edge to ngo:china-embassy-prc is our inference. The actual donor could have been the embassy, a PRC ministry, or a Chinese state-linked institute. The recipient is correctly identified as RGICS, "a policy think tank promoted by the RGF". There is no FCRA registration number for RGICS in the record, and whether RGICS held FCRA registration at all is an open gap in the file.
verdicts.baseRate: We have no quantified base rate, and the file does not compute one. Embassies of major powers funding or co-sponsoring Indian foreign-policy think tanks and seminars is common: US, German, Japanese and EU missions, plus foundations such as KAS and FES, routinely show up in donor and partner lists of ORF, ICRIER, Gateway House and others. Being "listed as donor" is probably not discriminating among Delhi foreign-policy think tanks in the 2000s. What stands out here is that the donor is the PRC and that the recipient is tied to the ruling family. That depends on who the donor is, not on the listing being unusual. We did not check donor lists for the SPEC's control comparators (VIF, India Foundation) on the same basis. The file's symmetry section admits it could not open them.
verdicts.denialFound: none found for RGICS specifically — asked / not asked. The article does not say whether RGICS or RGF was asked about the RGICS listing. The Congress response on record (fcra-actions:c058, Singhvi, 2022-10, via indiacsr.in: "The Rajiv Gandhi Foundation has nothing to add, nothing to fear…") and the July 2020 "diversionary tactics" response (political-trusts:c011, HT 2020-07-08) are general responses to the RGF/China allegation, not to the RGICS line. WebSearch budget for this session was exhausted, so no further search for an RGICS-specific response was possible.
verdicts.innocentReading: In 2005-06 RGF/RGICS carried out an India-China FTA study that concluded an FTA would benefit India. The Chinese embassy (or a PRC body) most likely co-sponsored related seminars, delegations or research exchanges, which is ordinary diplomatic outreach to a think tank. Under FCRA 1976, an organisation with registration or prior permission could legally receive foreign-government money, and disclosing the donor in its own annual report is the transparency the law expects. The listing itself shows no quid pro quo, and no amount for RGICS is given anywhere in the source.
verdicts.reason: The core fact survives. Indian Express states in its own voice that "China's name figures in the list of donors for the Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Contemporary Studies (RGICS)". But the tier "documented" is not earned. (1) The RGICS donor list and the annual report were never opened: the record rests on one outlet's account of documents first circulated by the BJP in 2020. Under CONTRACT, that is "reported" (one credible outlet with published documents), not "documented" (primary record, or two independent outlets). (2) The source does not name the embassy for RGICS, only "China". (3) The source does not date the RGICS listing. "Same period" is inferred from the sentence before. The claim is partially confirmed and over-tiered, so downgrade rather than kill.
verdicts.corrections: tier: documented -> reported. d: replace with the verbatim sentence "China's name figures in the list of donors for the Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Contemporary Studies (RGICS), a policy think tank promoted by the RGF". Add: "IE does not state the year for the RGICS listing; FY2005-06 is inferred from the adjacent RGF-annual-report sentence; amount not stated; donor named only as 'China', not specifically the embassy." s: either keep ngo:china-embassy-prc and flag in d that the embassy identity is inferred for RGICS, or use a generic PRC-government node. lab: "China named in RGICS donor list (per IE; year inferred FY2005-06)". Source label date: Indian Express 2022-10-23 (datePublished), not 2022-10-24. Fix the same date in c008 and in the file's sources header. Entity ngo:rajiv-gandhi-institute-for-contemporary-studies, d[0]: change "[documented]" to "[reported]", and change "per RGF's own published annual report" to "per Indian Express's account". IE does not say the RGICS list is in RGF's annual report. Entity ngo:china-embassy-prc: soften the "RGICS's donor list" wording the same way. Add upgradeIf: "RGICS/RGF FY2005-06 annual report or FC-3/FC-4 return opened, showing the PRC embassy line (and amount)". Add killIf: "the primary donor list shows no PRC/Chinese-government entity for RGICS". Add a contra pointing to c011/fcra-actions:c058, or record "no RGICS-specific response found; not asked in source".

verdicts.dateTest: The claim is that JP Nadda alleged, by tweet, that PMNRF donated to RGF in the UPA years. The tweets were posted on Friday 26 Jun 2020, not 25 Jun. The Hindu (published 26 Jun 2020, 10:54 IST) says Nadda "on Friday further accused the RGF of receiving funds from the ... PMNRF", a day after the Chinese-embassy allegation of 25 Jun. HT (8 Jul 2020) only says "last month". The grant's own window is also too wide. The recipient's statement puts it at one grant: "Rs 20 lakh from the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund in the Financial Year 2005", after the Dec 2004 tsunami. The record's "from 2005, to 2008" is taken from the two annual-report screenshots, not from the transfer itself. Tenure overlap: UPA-I began May 2004 and Manmohan Singh became PM, so the grant falls inside the window. Sonia Gandhi chaired RGF, so that part overlaps. There is no documented overlap for her supposed PMNRF board seat.
verdicts.identityTest: PMNRF and RGF are correctly identified, and s→t is the right direction for a grant. The co-control link fails. The claim text says "Sonia Gandhi historically on its board", but that is only Nadda's assertion ("Who sat on the PMNRF board? Smt. Sonia Gandhi"). The PMNRF site (pmnrf.gov.in/en/about) says "Disbursements are made with the approval of the Prime Minister" and that the fund "operates from the Prime Minister's Office". Wikipedia's PMNRF article, citing India Today (18 Aug 2020), says the fund has been controlled by the PMO since 1985 and "The President of Congress is not a member of PMNRF anymore". Sonia Gandhi became Congress president in 1998. So in FY2005 the person who approved the grant was PM Manmohan Singh, who HT lists as an RGF trustee, not Sonia Gandhi. The claim's "names Sonia Gandhi as beneficiary" is also wrong. RGF, an institution, received the grant, and no source says any person benefited. That wording casts a family member as the recipient, which the edge cannot carry.
verdicts.baseRate: Not established. We found no list of PMNRF grants to NGOs for the 2004 tsunami, and the web-search budget was used up. Relief funds sending money to established NGOs for relief after the 2004 tsunami was widespread, so a single ₹20 lakh tsunami grant does not single anyone out by itself. The part that could matter is the overlap between PMNRF's approving authority and RGF's trustees (Manmohan Singh). Testing that needs the same check run on PM CARES and NDA-era aligned trusts (the SPEC's VIF/India Foundation control). Nobody has run it, and neither the file nor the sources do.
verdicts.denialFound: There is a response, and it is not a denial but an explanation. The claim's current contra (c011, a general Congress "diversionary tactics" line) is not it. RGF's statement, issued by Congress chief spokesperson Randeep Surjewala on 26–27 Jun 2020 and carried by IANS, reads: "Pursuant to the unprecedented tsunami in the last week of 2004, RGF received a modest amount of Rs 20 lakh from the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund in the Financial Year 2005 which was duly utilised to undertake relief activities in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands ... This grant has been duly reflected in all filings to the income tax and the Home Ministry and no authority has ever found any wrongdoing of any nature." Source: https://www.orissapost.com/received-a-modest-amount-of-rs-20-lakh-from-pmnrf-for-relief-work-in-andaman-rgf/ (IANS, 27 Jun 2020). The same wire copy is at newsd.in, npnews24.com and menafn.com.
verdicts.innocentReading: A one-time ₹20 lakh (₹0.2 crore) PMNRF grant to an established NGO for tsunami relief in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands in FY2005, approved in the normal way by the PM's office. RGF says it was used for that purpose, audited, and shown in its income-tax and FCRA filings to the Home Ministry. It also appears in RGF's published annual reports, which is how Nadda found it. The one real concern is a possible conflict of interest: the approving PM, Manmohan Singh, was an RGF trustee. That can be raised as an analytic governance point without treating the grant as a diversion of funds.
verdicts.reason: The claim is refuted as written because it mixes up tiers and gets several facts wrong. The money transfer itself is no longer just an allegation. The recipient admits it (₹20 lakh, FY2005, tsunami relief), and The Hindu independently reports that "The RGF ... has in its annual reports for 2005-2006 and 2007-08 shown that the PMNRF donated funds to it." That contradicts the record's own `d` ("we could not independently confirm PMNRF itself appears as a line-item donor") and makes the `killIf` pointless. What remains unproven is the framing: "diversion", "brazen fraud", Sonia Gandhi sitting on the PMNRF board, and Sonia Gandhi as "beneficiary". Official PMNRF material and Wikipedia/India Today contradict or fail to support the board claim, since Congress-president membership ended in 1985. The HT source does say what is quoted (Nadda's tweet text, PMNRF donating to RGF, Sonia Gandhi chairing RGF), but it gives no amount. It also says the donor lists Nadda posted named SBI, GAIL, MHA and MoH, which is why the author's read was muddled. The grant edge should be `reported`, with an amount and the RGF statement as its contra. It could be upgraded to `documented` from RGF's FY2005-06 annual report or PMNRF accounts. Nadda's diversion and board claims belong in a separate `alleged` narrative, not in the edge label.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Tier: change the grant edge ngo:pmnrf→ngo:rajiv-gandhi-foundation from `alleged` to `reported`. Upgrade to `documented` once RGF's 2005-06 annual report or PMNRF accounts are opened directly. 2) `a`: null → 0.2 (₹ crore; ₹20 lakh), with `d` noting FY2005 (FY2004-05 per the RGF statement) and the purpose, tsunami relief in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. 3) `from`/`to`: "2005"/"2008" → "2005"/"2005". Explain in `d` that the 2005-06 and 2007-08 annual reports were Nadda's screenshots, not separate grants. 4) Date in `lab`: "25 Jun 2020" → "26 Jun 2020". 5) Delete from `d`: "donor lists shown named PSUs and ministries, not PMNRF by name; we could not independently confirm PMNRF itself appears". The Hindu (https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/rajiv-gandhi-foundation-got-funds-from-pmnrf-during-upa-regime-says-bjp-chief-nadda/article31921071.ece) contradicts it, and RGF has admitted the grant. Add The Hindu and the IANS/Orissa Post RGF statement to `srcs`. 6) Replace `killIf` (RGF's own statement already confirms the grant) with something like: "PMNRF records show the grant was not for tsunami relief or was not used for it". 7) Text: remove "names Sonia Gandhi as beneficiary", since the recipient is the institution. Recast "Sonia Gandhi historically on its board" as Nadda's assertion only, and cite the PMNRF site / India Today saying the PMO has controlled the fund since 1985 and the Congress president is not a member. Note that the approving authority in FY2005 was PM Manmohan Singh (an RGF trustee). 8) Contra: add a new `contra` edge for the RGF/Surjewala statement (grant used for its purpose, audited, filed with IT and MHA, no wrongdoing found) aimed at the diversion allegation. c011 as it stands is a general political rebuttal, not a response to this claim. 9) Move the "diversion / brazen fraud" allegation into a narrative (or a separate `alleged` analytic node) with the RGF response attached, so the grant edge carries only the documented flow. 10) Symmetry: add an analytic item comparing PM-controlled relief funds and trustee overlap under NDA (PM CARES) with aligned trusts, as the SPEC control requires.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim as worded is "four India Foundation directors became Union ministers in 2014 and stayed on as directors." That fails. The Wire article (Swati Chaturvedi, published 2017-11-04T03:58+05:30) describes the board only as it stood on the publication date. It says nothing about any director becoming a minister in 2014. The date comes from Wikipedia's paraphrase, and it is wrong for at least one of the four. M.J. Akbar became MoS External Affairs in July 2016. Suresh Prabhu (Railways) and Jayant Sinha (MoS Finance) joined in November 2014. Sitharaman became MoS (Independent Charge) in May 2014 and Defence Minister (Cabinet) in September 2017. The edge's "from":"2014" is therefore not supported by the cited source. The only date the source supports is 2017-11-04: on that day Sitharaman was Defence Minister and was listed on India Foundation's directors page. The "to": null (open-ended) is also unsupported, because nothing opened shows her board status after November 2017. The "sitting cabinet minister" part does pass: at publication she was Defence Minister, a cabinet post. Quote: "the India Foundation lists among its directors defence minister Nirmala Sitharaman and commerce and industry minister Suresh Prabhu, and two ministers of state – Jayant Sinha (civil aviation) and M.J. Akbar (external affairs)."
verdicts.identityTest: Passes. The node ngo:india-foundation is the Delhi think tank run by Shaurya Doval and Ram Madhav, which The Wire identifies. The Wire itself separates it from a namesake FCRA trust run by Ambassador Suryakanti Tripathi, registered in 2004: "There is an India Foundation shown for each of the years but that is a trust run by Ambassador Suryakanti Tripathi". Any FCRA-number lookup must not merge the two. The person is Nirmala Sitharaman, named explicitly and described as defence minister. One caveat: India Foundation is a trust, so "director" is the foundation's own term for its board members (The Wire cites "the directors page of the India Foundation website"). No DIN applies, and no MCA record can confirm the role. The only evidence is the website listing reproduced by The Wire.
verdicts.baseRate: Not established. The fleet control is a UPA-era equivalent: did any sitting UPA minister serve as a trustee or board member of a Congress-aligned think tank or trust (RGF, RGCT, RGICS)? That test was not run for this record, and I could not run it because the WebSearch budget is used up. For context, it is common for think tanks aligned with a ruling party to have serving politicians on their boards. The unusual part The Wire reports is four serving ministers at once, together with event sponsorship by foreign firms that have business before their ministries. The file's own base rates count FCRA enforcement, not ministers holding board seats, so they do not discriminate on this property. A role edge does not need a base rate to be true. The "conflict-of-interest" framing does need one.
verdicts.denialFound: The ministers were asked and did not reply. The Wire: "The Wire asked Nirmala Sitharaman, 'Would you accept that there is a conflict of interest…' Similar questions were put to Prabhu, Akbar and Sinha. Till the time of publication, none of them chose to reply." The PMO (Nripendra Misra) was also asked and did not answer. India Foundation denied the allegations in a statement on its homepage, as reported by The Quint on 2017-11-05 (https://www.thequint.com/news/hot-news/ajit-dovals-son-shaurya-conflict-of-interest-the-wire). It called the article "speculative and clearly intends to insinuate wrong-doing where there is none." It said the directors named "were members of the Foundation long before they were made Ministers," that "no foreign funding had been received," and that the directors had not "furthered the commercial or private interests of any company." Shaurya Doval told The Wire: "There is no conflict of interest as India Foundation does not conduct any commercial transactions… Its charter does not include lobbying." The Wire replied the same day (Siddharth Varadarajan, https://thewire.in/politics/shaurya-doval-response-the-wire-questions-answers-india-foundation). The record currently contains none of these responses.
verdicts.innocentReading: Sitharaman and the others joined the board of a policy think tank close to their party before they entered government, as the foundation says. Staying on an unpaid advisory-style board is common for politicians with policy interests. Sponsorship of conferences, possibly received through a partner organisation such as FICCI, is legally different from a foreign contribution to the trust under FCRA. The Wire offers no evidence that any minister made a decision that favoured a sponsor. The piece is a propriety or appearance-of-conflict argument, supported by two anonymous former officials (a defence secretary and a cabinet secretary), not a finding of wrongdoing.
verdicts.reason: The source is reachable. The full article body is in the page's JSON-LD articleBody, so the record's note that it "could not render The Wire article body" is out of date. The article confirms the core role edge: on 2017-11-04, India Foundation listed Defence Minister Nirmala Sitharaman among its directors, and she was asked about it and did not reply. That supports tier "reported": one credible outlet, with a published screenshot of the directors page. The claim text as written is wrong, though. It attributes to The Wire two things the article does not say: that the four directors "became Union ministers in 2014" (false for M.J. Akbar, who became a minister in 2016) and that they "stayed on." It also cites a Wikipedia paraphrase as the effective source. The "stayed on" part is in fact supported, but by India Foundation's own denial statement, which the record leaves out. The claim is refuted as worded. It should survive only in corrected form, still as "reported."
verdicts.corrections: 1. Text/lab: replace with "The Wire (4 Nov 2017) reported that India Foundation listed Defence Minister Nirmala Sitharaman among its directors, alongside ministers Suresh Prabhu, Jayant Sinha and M.J. Akbar; it framed this as a conflict of interest. The ministers were asked and did not reply." Remove "became Union ministers in 2014." 2. from: change "2014" to null, or add an observed date of "2017-11-04". Optionally add a note that India Foundation says she was a member before becoming a minister (May 2014), citing the foundation's statement via The Quint. to: leave null, but add to gaps that her board status after November 2017 is unknown. 3. srcs: make The Wire the primary source (body verified via JSON-LD) and demote Wikipedia to secondary. Delete the "could not render The Wire article body" caveat from d. 4. Add a contra/denial field quoting India Foundation's statement ("insinuate wrong-doing where there is none"; directors were "members of the Foundation long before they were made Ministers"; "no foreign funding"), plus Shaurya Doval's "no conflict of interest… charter does not include lobbying." Also record that the ministers were asked and did not reply. 5. Identity note: add The Wire's warning that a different trust called India Foundation (the Suryakanti Tripathi trust, registered 2004) appears in the FCRA returns, and that the two must not be merged. 6. Narrative (contested claim): change "genuine, documented institutional-overlap fact" to "reported (single outlet, website screenshot; confirmed in substance by India Foundation's own statement)." Also correct "four 2014-vintage Union ministers," since Akbar became a minister in 2016. 7. Symmetry: run the same check for UPA-era sitting ministers who held trustee or board seats at Congress-aligned trusts (RGF/RGCT/RGICS) before the conflict-of-interest framing is used as discriminating.

verdicts.dateTest: FAILS. Claim form: "Finance Act 2016 amended FCRA [in 2016] and so shielded BJP from the 2014 Delhi HC finding." The 2016 amendment was retrospective only to 26 Sep 2010, the date of FCRA 2010. This file's own entity note says so ("with effect from 2010-09-26"). The Delhi HC finding covered Sterlite/Sesa donations made under FCRA 1976 "up to the year 2009" (c020/c021, from Indian Kanoon doc 190292989). The 2016 amendment's window (from Sep 2010) and the donations (up to 2009) do not overlap. The Hindu, 3 Feb 2018 (https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/fcra-amendment-in-finance-bill/article22636668.ece), says so directly: "The amendment, though done retrospectively, only made valid the foreign donations received after 2010, the year when the 1976 Act was amended. The retrospective amendment did not apply to donations prior to 2010." It goes on: "In a move to extend relief to the two parties, the government has again proposed an amendment through the Finance Bill, 2018." So the 2016 Act could not have shielded BJP from the 2014 finding. Only the 2018 amendment, reaching back to 1976, did that.
verdicts.identityTest: The source node (ngo:finance-act-2016-fcra-amendment) is the wrong instrument for this predicate. The cited source does not name the 2016 Act. The Wikipedia article (Electoral_Bond_Scheme now redirects to "Electoral bonds") says only: "...retrospective amendments made to the Foreign Currency Regulation Act (FCRA) by the government, on two separate occasions, in an effort to shield the BJP and the Congress from prosecution for FCRA violations, as determined by the Delhi High Court." It gives no years, misnames the Act as "Foreign Currency", and does not say that each amendment separately shielded the parties. Splitting "two occasions" into a 2016 edge and a 2018 edge that each "shielded BJP" is the researcher's own inference, and The Hindu contradicts it. The target (BJP, Respondent No.4 in ADR v UoI) is identified correctly.
verdicts.baseRate: Not really applicable, because this is a legislative-effect claim. On symmetry, the same reading applies to INC (c024), and it fails for the same date reason. The 2016 amendment benefited every Indian company with foreign shareholding within FEMA limits that donated after 2010, which is a broad class. It did not specifically benefit the two parties' pre-2010 exposure.
verdicts.denialFound: None found; not asked. The Wikipedia article (line on FCRA) says the amendment passed "with the support of the opposition". No government or BJP statement on the 2016 amendment's link to the Delhi HC case was located. Web search budget was exhausted, and The Wire's piece on the 2018 Finance Bill (https://thewire.in/business/finance-bill-seeks-amend-fcra-condone-illegal-donations-bjp-congress-received-foreign-companies) did not render.
verdicts.innocentReading: The Finance Act 2016 changed the FCRA 2010 "foreign source" definition to line it up with FEMA foreign-investment limits. That let Indian-incorporated companies with foreign shareholding give to NGOs and parties from 2010 on. It is a prospective and near-term regularisation of the post-2010 regime. It could not, and did not, reach the 2004–09 Vedanta-subsidiary donations. That gap is why the government brought the 2018 amendment (Finance Bill 2018 clause 217), which went back to 1976.
verdicts.reason: The decisive problem is chronology. The 2016 amendment was retrospective only to Sep 2010. The donations the 2014 Delhi HC judgment addressed were made under FCRA 1976 up to 2009. The Hindu (3 Feb 2018) says explicitly that the 2016 amendment "did not apply to donations prior to 2010", and that the 2018 Finance Bill was the move "to extend relief to the two parties". The only cited source (Wikipedia) never names 2016. It speaks of "two separate occasions" jointly, so reading each occasion as its own shield is an unsupported conjunction. The claim is factually wrong as written, not just superseded.
verdicts.corrections: Kill c023 rather than leaving it as supersededBy c025, because a superseded edge implies it was once true. Apply the same kill to c024 (INC), since the identical defect applies. If a 2016 edge is wanted, restate it as: "Finance Act 2016 retrospectively (from 26 Sep 2010) narrowed FCRA 2010 'foreign source' definition; did not cover pre-2010 donations addressed by the 2014 Delhi HC judgment". Tier it reported, citing The Hindu 2018-02-03 (URL above). Strengthen c025/c026 by adding The Hindu as a second source, with its quote: "the government has again proposed an amendment through the Finance Bill, 2018... to extend relief to the two parties". Also fix the entity note for ngo:finance-act-2016-fcra-amendment. Its publicRole ("First of two retrospective amendments widely reported to have shielded both BJP and Congress from the consequences of the 2014 Delhi HC finding") should instead say the 2016 amendment did not reach the finding. Update the Wikipedia source URL to https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electoral_bonds (the current title after the redirect), and note that the article calls the Act "Foreign Currency Regulation Act". In the narrative "bipartisan cover-up", drop the implication that both 2016 and 2018 legalised the 1976-era donations; only 2018 did.
